obj.scrambling.stretched-singularity.formal: The \emph{stretched singularity} is the interior slice $r = r_c$ defined by the curvature-eigenvalue cutoff $2M/r^3 = 1$ in Planck units: $r_c = (2M)^{1/3}$. It is the working substitute for the exceptional boundary of the completion: the locus where the classical description is replaced by the completed one, on which, by Postulate (C1) of the singularity paper (\claimref{singularity.c1-curvature-cutoff}), the boundary-mode pairs lie, with $\nu$ fermionic modes (ladder pairs) per Planck cell by Postulate (C2), $\nu$ left free there (\claimref{singularity.c2-cell-density}). The definition places no modes; results that count modes on the slice hold under (C1) and (C2).
obj.scrambling.stretched-singularity.technical:
Inside a Schwarzschild black hole of mass $M$ (Planck units) the curvature operator has largest eigenvalue $2M/r^3$. The stretched singularity is the interior slice $r = r_c$ on which that eigenvalue reaches the Planck value, $2M/r_c^3 = 1$, so $r_c = (2M)^{1/3}$.

It is the working substitute for the exceptional boundary of the completion: the locus where the classical description is replaced by the completed one, and, under the singularity paper's placement postulates (C1) and (C2), the surface on which the boundary-mode pairs lie.
obj.scrambling.stretched-singularity.lay: Deep inside a black hole the curvature of space-time grows without limit towards the centre. The stretched singularity is the surface where that curvature first reaches the Planck scale. The framework treats this surface as the place where ordinary geometry gives way to its completed description, and, by a stated assumption of the singularity paper, it is where the black hole's boundary modes sit.
obj.scrambling.stretched-singularity.typing_note: Definition with no edges; the cited capacity Fact is a claim, so it cannot be an about target, and objects carry no derivations.

pred.boundary-mode-density.formal: The internal prediction, in the capacity convention (a fermionic mode carries at most $\ln 2$ nats): $\nu = 1/(16\pi\ln 2)$, equivalently one boundary-mode fermion per $4\ln 2$ Planck cells of horizon area, one per Bekenstein-Mukhanov area quantum, per modular period ($N_{\mathrm{epoch}}\ln 2 = S_{\mathrm{BH}}$, calibration residue $\kappa_c = 1/(4\ln 2)$, \claimref{scrambling.residue-each-convention}). In the 1-nat convention the same statement reads $\nu = 1/16\pi$, one fermion per four Planck cells ($N_{\mathrm{epoch}} = S_{\mathrm{BH}}$, $\kappa_c = \tfrac14$).
pred.boundary-mode-density.technical:
With the counted epoch fixed at the modular period $\beta = 8\pi M$, the area law requires the boundary-mode capacity registered per modular period to equal the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy: $N_{\mathrm{epoch}}\ln 2 = \SBH = A/4$, so $N_{\mathrm{epoch}} = A/(4\ln 2)$, one fermion per $4\ln 2 \approx 2.77$ Planck cells of horizon area (one per Bekenstein-Mukhanov area quantum), and the mode density per Planck cell is $\nu = 1/(16\pi\ln 2)$. This is the capacity convention, the one that compares an entropy with an entropy (\claimref{scrambling.residue-each-convention}(iii)). In the 1-nat convention, which credits each mode with one nat, the same statement reads $\nu = 1/16\pi$ and $N_{\mathrm{epoch}} = \SBH$, one fermion per four Planck cells.

The prediction is internal: a derivation of the calibration residue from the boundary modes that returned any other value would refute the intrinsic-clock premise on which the epoch identification rests.
pred.boundary-mode-density.lay: The framework predicts how densely a black hole's horizon modes record information: one elementary fermionic mode for about every three Planck-sized patches of horizon area (exactly $4\ln 2 \approx 2.77$ of them, the area quantum Bekenstein and Mukhanov proposed), per cycle of the hole's natural clock. Each such mode can hold one bit. Given the premise that this clock sets the counting epoch, this is the counting that reproduces the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy. The test is internal to the theory: if its own calculation of this density gave a different number, a key assumption about the clock would be refuted.
pred.boundary-mode-density.typing_note: The single basis edge to the integer-holographic corollary is the prediction's real premise and is kept; the intrinsic-clock premise enters through that corollary's epoch theorem. Levels pass: the lay said the hole's interior records the information, but the modes are boundary (horizon) modes, so it now says so, and it names the intrinsic-clock premise the epoch identification rests on.

__notes__.note.synthesis.residue-and-the-predictio: The calibration residue was not derived (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy}). Under the area-law hypothesis it is the reciprocal of four times the counted modes' mean thermal entropy, so the registered value $\kappa_{c} = 1/(4\ln 2)$ of Prediction \claimref{pred.boundary-mode-density} is the case in which every counted mode has zero Killing weight. The one weight assignment the series makes, the s-wave convention of Premise \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave}, does not give that value under any reading of which modes are counted. Counting arrays gives $0.3470$ against $0.3607$, about four per cent low; counting every mode drives the residue up without bound; counting only the zero-weight modes leaves $0.0272$ nats per array outside the area law. Since (Q) is adopted for one step only and the result is a conditional reformulation, this neither meets nor fails the prediction's kill condition. It does mark where the prediction is exposed: a derivation that fixed the weights as (Q) does would return a residue other than the registered one and so, by the kill condition, refute the intrinsic-clock premise (IC).
__notes__.note.scrambling.density-factor-stated-fu:
Two normalisations enter $
u$, and their statuses differ. The corank is settled: under the weights the geometry forces, the anisotropic Schwarzschild singularity carries exactly one ladder pair per point of the blown-up singular locus \cite[\S 8.9]{ButlerT4}, the resolution T5 records in passing the count to this paper \cite[\S 10]{ButlerT5}. What remains open is the \emph{cell calibration}: how many Planck cells of slice volume one localised pair accounts for, the conversion from per-point to per-cell. The weighted completion supplies the geometry at the exceptional set on which that conversion is to be read (Fact \claimref{tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity}), and its analysis is closed at Schwarzschild, so no analytic step of the geometry programme stands between it and $
u$; what blocks the calibration is one dimensionless number, the residue $\kappa_c$ of the section “The calibration factorised, and the quarter examined”, and deriving it is this paper's task, carried as its first successor problem (the section “Scope, and successor problems”). The $M$-scaling of Theorem \claimref{scrambling.mode-count} is independent of it, the coefficient is not, and the section “The epoch is the modular period” converts the requirement into that single number. Separately, the per-mode entropy normalisation is $\ln 2$ for a maximally mixed fermionic mode: T5 compares the capacity $C = N\ln 2$, not the bare count, with $\SBH$, so the area-law condition of Proposition \claimref{scrambling.area-law-test} reads $
u\Delta t = M/2$ in the 1-nat convention used here and $
u\Delta t = M/(2\ln 2)$ in T5's capacity convention, a factor of $\ln 2$ (31 per cent) that is stated rather than absorbed into an approximation sign.

__notes__.note.decisions.two-boost-flows:
The series calls two different one-parameter groups ``the boost flow''. Both are generated by the same element, $K = \sigma/2$ for the completed pair with $\sigma = v^{*}v - vv^{*}$ (and $\sum_j \omega_j K_j$ for the boundary modes), and they differ in the parameter.

The \emph{rotor flow} is $\operatorname{Ad}(R_\lambda)$, $R_\lambda = \exp(\lambda\sigma/2)$, a real rotor flow of the atom: it acts by $v \mapsto e^{-\lambda}v$, $v^{*} \mapsto e^{+\lambda}v^{*}$, so it rescales the modes, its adjoint eigenvalues are real, and it has no period. This is the flow of Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-structure-completed-pair}(2) and (5), the only one-parameter flow implemented by real rotors of the atom, and of the clocks of Lemma \claimref{scrambling.clock-inventory-boundary-modes}, intrinsic flows of the real Clifford boundary-mode algebra with real adjoint eigenvalues. The scrambling law of \claimref{scrambling.spreading-law-chaos-bound-saturated} uses this flow: a quadratic generator containing the boost scales the ladder operators by $e^{\pm\kappa t}$, and that real growth, exponentiated across the window, gives $t_{*} = \kappa^{-1}\ln N$.

The \emph{phase flow} is $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{JtK})$, written with the complex unit of the atom and the boundary modes, $J = e_{2}e_{3}$ (\claimref{synthesis.transverse-bivector-is-the-complex-unit-of-the-radial-atom}), which on the modes is $a_j \mapsto e^{-J\omega_j t}a_j$: a unitary group whose adjoint eigenvalues are imaginary, multiples of $J$, periodic in the parameter for each single mode. This is the flow of Theorem \claimref{singularity.rate-rigidity-temperature-not-algebra-intrinsic}, $\alpha_t = \operatorname{Ad}(e^{JtK})$, and the boost dynamics $\tau_t(a_j) = e^{-J\omega_j t}a_j$ of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics}. The KMS analysis uses this flow: the descended state of Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-descent} is KMS for it, the modular flow in its proof being $\operatorname{Ad}(\rho^{Jt})$, and the rigidity theorem, the geometric modular condition and the Hawking paper's I-state are stated for it. Proposition \claimref{singularity.euclidean-rotor-where-it-lies} identifies it as the Euclidean rotation: the boost rotor continued to imaginary rapidity, $R_{J\theta} = \exp(J\theta\sigma/2) = \exp(\theta I_{4}/2)$, whose generator $J\sigma = I_{4}$ is not in the atom's real algebra $\Cl(1,1)$ and which is realised by no real rotor of $\Cl(1,3)$ (the proposition's clause (3) writes the continuation on vectors with the central unit $I_{5} = I_{4}e$ of $\Cl(2,3)$, whose generator $I_{5}\sigma = e_{2}e_{3}e$ lies outside $\Cl(1,3)$).

The two are related by analytic continuation of the parameter, $\lambda = Jt$: $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{JtK}) = \operatorname{Ad}(R_{Jt})$. The rotor flow fixes the orbits and, through the geometric normalisation, the rate $\kappa = 1/4M$ that converts rapidity to Schwarzschild time, $\lambda = \kappa t$; the phase flow carries the period, $2\pi$ in rapidity for the conjugation action on each atom, which under premise (R) is the modular period $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa = 8\pi M$ in Schwarzschild time. The chaos-bound statement compares one with the other: the rotor flow's growth rate $\kappa$ against $2\pi T$, the phase flow's KMS temperature, which are equal. Where the boundary-mode algebra is complex (the Hawking paper) the phase flow acts within it; where it is a real Clifford algebra (the scrambling results) its generator, $J$ times a bivector, is excluded ($J$ is not in that real algebra) and only the rotor flow is intrinsic, which is the dynamical face of the second known limit in the conventions. The Hawking paper's dynamics is the phase flow, while the scrambling assumption runs the window's dynamics on the rotor flow. Which of the two is the physical time evolution of a window, in the one Schwarzschild time $t$ that both papers use, is settled by Proposition \claimref{synthesis.phase-flow-is-time-rotor-flow-kms-continuation}: taking a time evolution to be a group of $*$-automorphisms preserving the states, the phase flow is the window's time evolution and the rotor flow its KMS-strip continuation, so for the quadratic dynamics the scrambling law assumes its growth $e^{\kappa t}$ is an imaginary-time rate on the CAR windows; real-time spreading is left open there.
__notes__.note.scrambling.point-contact-what-kind-: The step of Theorem \claimref{scrambling.epoch-modular-period-two-unknowns-become} is the framework's version of a familiar holographic practice: when a quantity is conditional on a regulator, derive the regulator from the system's own modular structure. The coherence checks are threefold: the causal epoch of Fact \claimref{singularity.causal-epoch-computed-exactly} is $O(M)$ with an identified logarithm, matching the modular period's scale; the count's rate is set by the horizon's own temperature, $dN/dt = \nu/\TH$; and the epoch three-volume comes out as $\beta^2\lP$, modular up to a single Planck factor. __notes__.note.scrambling.prediction-restated:
Propositions \claimref{scrambling.exact-factorisation-thinning} to \claimref{scrambling.no-recount-reaches-quarter} reduce the calibration to the form
\[
N_{\mathrm{epoch}} \;=\; \kappa_c \times (\text{horizon-normalised sphere cells}) \times (\text{one tick per modular period}),
\]
with the normalisation narrowed to two cutoff-free scales by exactness ($r_h$, or $r_* = M$, Proposition \claimref{scrambling.exactness-excludes-cutoff-dependence}), one tick per period being (IC) read as a counting rule, and $\kappa_c$ the residue. The residue is not an artefact of the counting conventions: the chain from tower to count carries no hidden factor of two (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.pair-mode-qubit-one-object}); the helicity clause is closed at the tier of the lift's modelling joint J3 (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.residue-each-convention}(iv), Fact \claimref{scrambling.imported-collars-coframe-exceptional-set-helicity}), not at theorem tier; and in the one convention with physical content the residue is $1/(4\ln 2)$, which no recount of the exceptional set with a rational residue ($k = 0$) produces, and, conditionally on the expected algebraic independence of $\pi$ and $\ln 2$, no recount with $k \neq 0$ either (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.no-recount-reaches-quarter}). The prediction's declared form is therefore: \emph{the boundary mode space registers one mode per Bekenstein-Mukhanov area quantum of horizon per modular period}, $\nu = 1/(16\pi\ln 2)$ in the capacity convention, and deriving that is equivalent to deriving Bekenstein-Hawking's quarter. Arithmetically $\kappa_c = \tfrac14$ in the 1-nat convention is horizon normalisation replaced by normalisation at $r_* = r_h/2 = M$, since $4\pi M^2 = \SBH$; whether that radius means anything is not decided here. The $16\pi$ of Theorem \claimref{scrambling.epoch-modular-period-two-unknowns-become} stands as the convention-dependent form of the same statement.

(2) \emph{The Kerr ring count:} repeat the section “The count” over the ring's codimension-two, duality-fibred exceptional structure \cite[Conj.~6.6]{ButlerT6}, which will scale differently with mass and spin, testing the count against the known angular-momentum dependence of Kerr entropy. (3) \emph{Chaotic saturation beyond free-fermion spreading:} upgrade Assembly \claimref{scrambling.spreading-law-chaos-bound-saturated} from operator-spreading to genuine out-of-time-order chaos, or show that the quadratic tier of the boundary modes is where the framework's claim ends. (4) \emph{The slice-to-epoch aggregation:} a first-principles rule taking Proposition \claimref{scrambling.per-slice-verification-two-failed-aggregations}(1)'s slice count to the epoch count, replacing the two failed naive rules. __notes__.note.singularity.setting-introduction:
The information paradox is usually posed as a conflict between two theories. This paper poses it as a comparison of entropies computed in two algebras, and computes them.

The setting is gauge theory gravity (GTG), the formulation of general relativity in the spacetime algebra $\Cl(1,3)$ due to Lasenby, Doran and Gull \cite{LDG1998}, in which gravity is a gauge field $\hb$, a position-dependent linear map on vectors, and every metrical statement is built from $\hb^{-1}$: the theory's geometric content exists exactly where $\hb$ is invertible. the section “Step 1: locate the failure” sets the theory out exactly, field equations, connection bivector and gauge laws included, because the chain's first step is a statement about those equations and must be made in them. For Schwarzschild in the Newtonian gauge, $\hb$ is invertible in closed form at every $r > 0$, horizon included, and is unimodular there, so nothing determinant-like ever degenerates: the divergence is carried entirely by the connection bivector, and at $r = 0$ the description fails in every gauge, through a null kernel, in the exact rescaled-limit sense of Proposition \claimref{singularity.degeneration-exactly}. The singularity is a division-by-zero locus in the literal, algebraic sense, and the transport principle of this series, the root paper T1 \cite{ButlerT1}, is a general theory of exactly such loci: it classifies the obstruction, forces a minimal completion, and quantifies what any return to the original level must lose. Its operational form is the six-step transport algorithm of \cite[\S 8.1, Table 1]{ButlerT1}, and this paper is that algorithm run end to end on the black hole; the table accompanying \claimref{singularity.imported-equivalence-einstein-equations} gives the step-by-step correspondence.

The paper runs the resulting chain from the classical field to the Page curve, numbered by the transport algorithm of the root paper with the physics expanded where it lies (Steps 1 to 3, 4a to 4e, 5, 6a and 6b), each step carrying its declared status (proved, or proved from named premises). The steps are summarised in the table accompanying \claimref{singularity.imported-equivalence-einstein-equations} and constitute the paper's outline. Steps 1 through 5 are theorems, at their stated scopes: the location and type of the failure, the forced ascent to $\Cl(2,4)$, the installation of canonical anticommutation relations where classical repair is barred, on the approach by Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-no-c-number-repair} and at the boundary itself by Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-no-equivariant-value-wall}, the selection of the boost plane and its rate, the identity of boost and number operator, single-mode thermality at exactly $\TH$ with the state's marginals fixed by univalence and one regularity premise rather than assumed, the bosonic Planck sector by bosonisation in the s-wave-reduced sector under the named joint quasi-freeness premise (Q), and the lossy descent with its exact multi-mode cost (Theorem \claimref{singularity.deficit-theorem-cost-descent-exactly}). Steps 6a and 6b remain conditional in substance, but every condition is a \emph{named postulate}: the boundary-mode capacity is a theorem from three axioms (curvature cutoff, cell density, counted epoch, the causal-epoch integral computed exactly in Lemma \claimref{singularity.causal-epoch-computed-exactly}), the radiation entropy of the rate model is an exact identity from localisation, purity, capacity, injection and boundary-mode locality, with the Page envelope its corollary and exact saturation confined to the zero-frequency idealisation, of which the linear weights supply exactly one mode, the sea level, so no window of two or more members ever saturates, the no-attic condition is derived rather than assumed, and the envelope with its endpoint needs no typicality and no assumption about where correlations are placed, boundary-mode locality being the one dynamical premise. The chain's conclusion on the paradox is a dissolution rather than a resolution: information is lost at the $\Cl(1,3)$ level and preserved at the $\Cl(2,4)$ level, these are the same physics read at two levels, and the discrepancy between the levels is not destruction but a fixed algebraic projection whose thermal output is the Hawking flux itself and whose size is an equation: the relative entropy of Theorem \claimref{singularity.deficit-theorem-cost-descent-exactly}, carried entirely by the correlations of the quanta (Corollary \claimref{singularity.deficit-carried-quanta-correlations}).

The paper also contains an exactly solvable finite-mode model (the section “The finite-mode model: the dissolution step by step”) in which the dissolution can be followed step by step, at both levels. In the model, every single radiated quantum is \emph{provably, exactly} thermal, by a parity-protection lemma stating that no encoding by phase scrambling can be visible to any single-quantum measurement; the joint radiation state is pure; the information is recoverable from inter-quanta correlations; the mutual-information computation per emission, together with the Page-shaped entropy sequence, is computed in exact arithmetic and machine-verified; and the multi-mode descent is applied to the radiation outright (the section “The descent, applied: the two levels in numbers”), so that the two-level conclusion is exhibited in exact numbers (the table accompanying \claimref{singularity.purity-correlation-transfer-recovery} and Proposition \claimref{singularity.two-levels-finite-model}) rather than argued. The model is a toy by construction and is offered as one: its value is that every claim in it is a computation, so the chain's conceptual endpoint (thermality as the record of what the projection cannot see; correlations as its carrier) is exhibited rather than argued.

A word on the standard of proof, binding throughout. The environments Theorem, Proposition and Lemma, with a Proof, are reserved for results proved \emph{in this paper}, at the standard of T1 \cite{ButlerT1}. Results proved elsewhere that the chain needs are stated as \textbf{Facts (imported)}, with their precise provenance; the typography tracks the epistemic content, so a reader can see at a glance which links of the chain this paper carries and which it inherits. Four links not previously proved are proved here outright: the finite-dimensional modular theory behind Step 4d; the state selection that completes it, the identification of the descent with the fermion parity average and the rigidity theorem that follows (Theorems \claimref{singularity.descent-parity-average}, \claimref{singularity.ascended-marginals-are-diagonal}, \claimref{singularity.rate-rigidity-temperature-not-algebra-intrinsic}); the curvature behind Step 4b, derived in the gauge formalism in the text (Theorem \claimref{singularity.curvature-gauge-field-exact-shape-decoupling}), with the appendix as an independent metric-picture cross-check; and the multi-mode descent behind Steps 5 and 6b, with its deficit theorem (Theorem \claimref{singularity.deficit-theorem-cost-descent-exactly}).

The slogan of Step 4a (the exterior radiation as the shadow of the return map) is hereby made quantitative: the shadow is the partial trace, identified mode by mode with the pinching $E$ by Proposition \claimref{singularity.pinching-against-partial-trace-scope-coincidence}(i) (the coincidence scoped precisely in Step 5, which this identification anticipates), and its output is thermal at exactly $\TH$. The word ``natural'' is made precise in the section “What selects the state”: by Theorem \claimref{singularity.purity-output-partner-commutant} the thermofield double is not one state among those satisfying the hypotheses but the canonical purification of the one-sided state, the partner being the commutant produced by the modular conjugation.
__notes__.note.singularity.what-antecedent-stated-: Theorems \claimref{singularity.finite-truncation-meet-big-fibres-equals} and \claimref{singularity.net-assembly-net-it-everything} quantify the two readings of ``the metric level over a region'' and do not decide between them. Both are determined by readings near the region's points; they differ in how the pointwise levels are assembled. The contravariant assembly (the sheaf, a limit: an element must survive every point's descent) gives $\operatorname{range}(\EN)$, the joint-diagonal algebra, and with it the nonzero two-level discrepancy of Steps 5 and 6b. The covariant assembly (the net, a colimit: the algebra generated by what each point's descent retains of the whole mode algebra) gives the whole mode algebra and a discrepancy of zero; it is the assembly an algebraic quantum field theory would adopt for its algebras of regions. The chain adopts the former, and that adoption is Proposition \claimref{singularity.p-reduced-metric-level-reading-many}'s antecedent: the sheaf assembly with the small fibres as stalks is the metric level if and only if the metric level over a region is the meet, so the antecedent is restated by this appendix, not reduced. What the appendix adds is the structural content of the choice: on the sheaf side the reading is a genuine sheaf whose finite truncations are $\operatorname{range}(E_F)$, on the net side it is a net whose finite truncations are the full mode algebras, and the discrepancy of Theorem \claimref{singularity.deficit-theorem-cost-descent-exactly} is precisely the cost of reading a region as a limit rather than a colimit. The choice is made in Definition \claimref{obj.singularity.two-fibres-two-assemblies}, before any sheaf theory runs, and it is a choice about which algebra ``the pointwise metric level'' names: the even part of the mode factor, or the even-in-that-mode part of the boundary mode space.

__notes__.note.singularity.why-rescues-rather-than:
Read carelessly, Theorem \claimref{singularity.exact-equilibrium-over-determines-boundary-modes} is an obstruction: the state that exact thermality requires is the state with no information in it. Read carefully, it is the reason the order of argument in this subsection matters. Had per-mode thermality been derived from the exact equilibrium condition, as hypothesis (ii) suggested, then thermality and correlation would have been in direct competition and the chain could not have had both. Theorem \claimref{singularity.ascended-marginals-are-diagonal} shows that per-mode thermality does not rest on equilibrium at all: it rests on parity, which survives an arbitrary non-stationary history. The state class the chain actually needs is
\[
\bigl\{\ \text{even states, per-mode populations at } \beta = 2\pi/\kappa, \ \text{correlations free}\ \bigr\},
\]
in which every single quantum is exactly thermal and the joint state of boundary modes and radiation together is free to carry everything the evaporation writes. Where it is carried is sharpened by the rate model and should be recorded here: under (I) and (L$_E$) the window marginal itself is fixed to be the product member at every stage (Theorem \claimref{singularity.eviction-window-thermal-product-radiation-entropy}(1)), its internal correlation and descent deficit identically zero, and the writing lies across the window/radiation cut and among the quanta of the radiation, not inside the boundary-mode marginal. That this class is where (P) and (R) put the state, and that the dynamics of the boundary modes keeps it there, is Corollary \claimref{singularity.chains-state-class-stability} below; the finite-mode model of the section “The finite-mode model: the dissolution step by step” lies in it, and Lemma \claimref{singularity.parity-protection} is the model's proof that it does. The theorem also settles a question the chain could otherwise have been asked indefinitely: no sharpening of Step 4d will ever supply Step 6b's correlations, because no equilibrium principle can.
__notes__.note.singularity.setting-step-4e-compute: (Q) is a genuine fourth premise, and it must be recorded that it stands in explicit tension with the principal content of Steps 5 and 6b: for the given marginals the quasi-free state is the product member of Corollary \claimref{singularity.chains-state-class-stability}'s class, the unique member satisfying (G), and Theorem \claimref{singularity.exact-equilibrium-over-determines-boundary-modes} rejects exactly that member as carrying none of the correlations those steps need. What (Q) yields is therefore the \emph{equilibrium reading} of the flux: the Planck sector below is a statement about the stationary idealisation of the boundary modes, not about the evaporating hole, for whose state the exact formula fails, the sum acquiring connected inter-mode correlators that (P) and (R) leave free (Corollary \claimref{singularity.chains-state-class-stability}(3)). One consequence of the rate model belongs here rather than being discovered against it: under (I) and (L$_E$) the window marginal is exactly this product at every stage (Theorem \claimref{singularity.eviction-window-thermal-product-radiation-entropy}(1)), so for the model's mode space the product clause of (Q) holds as a theorem (the weight assignment, the stationarity and the $\mathbb{Z}$-array remain (Q)'s own), and the tension is relocated rather than dissolved: the product form empties the \emph{internal} correlations of the boundary modes, and the correlations Steps 5 and 6b depend on are carried across the window/radiation cut, to which Theorem \claimref{singularity.exact-equilibrium-over-determines-boundary-modes}'s rejection does not apply. the table accompanying \claimref{singularity.imported-equivalence-einstein-equations}'s status line for the step carries the premise.
__notes__.note.singularity.monogamy-firewalls-smal:
Two classical objections must be located relative to the eviction mechanism, because the chain's state class invites both. First, monogamy: the firewall argument of \cite{AMPS2013} forbids a late quantum from being maximally entangled with its interior partner and with the early radiation at once. The rate model never asks for that: a window qubit is entangled with its own partner while it is in the window, and its correlation with the early radiation as a whole is acquired at eviction, when the qubit itself is transferred to the radiation sector (Corollary \claimref{singularity.what-event-returns-radiation}), so at no stage does one quantum carry both entanglements. The cost is stated plainly: eviction is a physical transfer of an interior degree of freedom into the radiation, and the smoothness of the horizon it presupposes is asserted by the model, not derived, which is exactly the point \cite{AMPS2013} press. Second, the small-corrections theorem of \cite{Mathur2009} shows that no accumulation of order-$\epsilon$ corrections to the pairwise Hawking process can return the radiation entropy to zero. Eviction does not evade that theorem by small corrections; it violates its locality hypothesis outright, the evicted qubit being an order-one, nonlocal transfer out of the interior. That is a legitimate alternative and a costly one: the falling branch of Theorem \claimref{singularity.eviction-window-thermal-product-radiation-entropy} stands or falls with the physical reality of eviction, which is the same commitment the islands programme makes in its own language (Remark \claimref{note.singularity.island-dictionary-one-dissonance}).

\emph{Added 10 November 2026.} For CHSH values the inequality behind this use of monogamy is the three-party trade-off of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.three-party-trade-off-of-chsh-values-and-the-local-value-two}: under Premise (P), positivity of values (\claimref{synthesis.premise-positivity-of-values}), two CHSH values that share one party satisfy $\omega(C_{AB})^{2} + \omega(C_{AD})^{2} \le 8$, so a window mode whose pair with its partner has squared value $S^{2}$ leaves any third party a squared value of at most $8 - S^{2}$, which for the pair state of weight parameter $r$ at its best directions is $4r^{2}$ (clause (v) there). Two caveats stated there apply. The shared party must use the same two observables in both tests. And with one mode per party the observables are odd under the total parity: if only parity-even elements are observables, a single window mode has no CHSH value above $2$ and the statement is empty for it.

__notes__.note.singularity.setting-model:
Qubits stand for modes. At emission event $k$ ($k = 1, \dots, n$) a thermofield pair is created between a radiation qubit $R_k$ and a window qubit $L_k$:
\[
|\psi_k\rangle \;=\; c_k\,|0_{R_k} 0_{L_k}\rangle + s_k\,|1_{R_k} 1_{L_k}\rangle, \qquad c_k = \cos\theta_k, \quad s_k = \sin\theta_k, \quad \tan^2\theta_k = e^{-\omega_k/\TH} ,
\]
the qubit image of Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-descent}'s state, with rational data (the script uses $(c_k, s_k) = (\tfrac45, \tfrac35), (\tfrac45, \tfrac35), (\tfrac45, \tfrac35), (\tfrac{12}{13}, \tfrac{5}{13})$ for $k = 1, \dots, 4$; every pair has $c_k > s_k$, so every $\omega_k > 0$). The window holds at most $N_{\max} = 2$ qubits; while $|L| \leq N_{\max}$ nothing else happens (Phase I). When an emission would exceed capacity, the model applies a \emph{scrambling unitary} $U$ to the window, diagonal in the number basis (a circuit of controlled-$Z$ gates, entries $\pm 1$, encoding whatever pattern the dynamics carries, including any infalling message), and then \emph{evicts} the oldest window qubit: the evicted qubit is transferred to the radiation as a late quantum (Phase II). This implements the inputs of the section “The eviction theorem: the falling branch without typicality” with a window that fills to $N_{\max} = 2$ over the first two events and then stays full until it is finally emptied: the no-attic property of Proposition \claimref{singularity.no-attic-derived-model} holds because the evicted qubit itself joins $R$, (I) because each pair arrives fresh, and (L$_E$) because the scrambling is diagonal. At the end all window qubits have been evicted and the radiation holds all $2n$ qubits.

Recorded as a programme item in the section “What remains open”. What Proposition \claimref{singularity.number-diagonal-dynamics-models-scrambling-derived} buys, if (L$_E$) holds, is worth the exposure: it converts the model's most questionable-looking choice, that the scrambling is phase-type, into the general case, and with it upgrades \cite[Lem.~12.1]{ButlerT5} from a statement about a particular circuit to a statement about the ledger.
__notes__.note.singularity.thermality-records-what: The lemma is now also a special case: by Theorem \claimref{singularity.ascended-marginals-are-diagonal} every even state of the boundary modes has diagonal single-mode marginals, and the model's states are even, so the protection is not a property of the phase-type scrambling but of fermion parity, and Proposition \claimref{singularity.number-diagonal-dynamics-models-scrambling-derived} shows that under boundary-mode locality the scrambling could not have been anything but phase type. Within the model the lemma is the model's instance of Theorem \claimref{singularity.descended-form-state-independent}: no encoding performed by the (phase-type) internal dynamics can be visible to any single-quantum measurement, exactly. One quantum at a time, the radiation carries nothing, and this is a theorem of the encoding, not an approximation: thermality is what the projection records in place of what it cannot see. The choice of \emph{diagonal} scrambling is what makes the statement exact rather than approximate, and it is the exact match to the chain, where single-mode thermality is likewise exact (Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-descent}) rather than emergent.

scrambling.area-law-test.formal: $N = \SBH = 4\pi M^2$ if and only if $\nu\,\Delta t = M/2$: the count reproduces the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, coefficient included, precisely when the counted epoch is of order one Schwarzschild time (in the 1-nat convention; with each mode credited its $\ln 2$ the condition is $\nu\,\Delta t = M/(2\ln 2)$, Proposition \claimref{singularity.area-law-test}). The scale has an independent causal meaning: the span of singularity in the causal future of a single horizon-crossing epoch is $\Delta t(\varepsilon) = 2M\bigl(\ln(1/\varepsilon) - \tfrac83 + 2\ln 2\bigr) + O(\varepsilon)$, of order $M$ up to a logarithm (Fact \claimref{singularity.causal-epoch-computed-exactly}). Counting instead over the hole's whole lifetime, $\Delta t \sim M^3$, gives $N \sim M^4$: the count then shares with the interior-volume growth of \cite{ChristodoulouRovelli2015} the linearity in time and the unresolved tension with the constancy of the horizon entropy, though not the growth law (their $dV/dv \propto M^2$ gives $V \sim M^5$ over the lifetime). The framework does not resolve that tension; it reproduces it from an independent starting point, which is evidence the count tracks real structure; the confrontation is recorded.

scrambling.boundary-mode-space-matrix.formal: Let the boundary mode space carry $n$ completed pairs, $n$ counted after the completion's doubling (each mode with its adjoined partner). The gauge-invariant bilinears $E_{ij} := \psi_i^\dagger \psi_j$ satisfy $[E_{ij}, E_{kl}] = \delta_{jk}E_{il} - \delta_{li}E_{kj}$ (the $\mathfrak{gl}(n)$ relations, an instance of the CAR bilinear commutator), preserve the one-particle subspace, and restrict on it to the full matrix algebra: $E_{ij}|_{\text{one-particle}} = $ the matrix unit $e_{ij}$, so the associative algebra they generate restricts onto $\Mat_n$. The doubling the completion forces is exactly what turns a tower of modes into a matrix; and matrices can be spheres.
scrambling.boundary-mode-space-matrix.technical:
Take $n$ completed pairs on the boundary mode space, with mode operators $\psi_i$ obeying the canonical anticommutation relations. The gauge-invariant bilinears $E_{ij} = \psi_i^\dagger\psi_j$ satisfy the $\mathfrak{gl}(n)$ relations $[E_{ij}, E_{kl}] = \delta_{jk}E_{il} - \delta_{li}E_{kj}$, map the one-particle subspace to itself, and act there as the matrix units $e_{ij}$, so the algebra they generate restricts onto $\Mat_n$.

The doubling the completion forces, each mode with its adjoined partner, is what supplies the complex operators $\psi_i, \psi_i^\dagger$ and hence the matrix structure; real Clifford directions alone give only the orthogonal bilinears.
scrambling.boundary-mode-space-matrix.lay: The black hole's boundary modes come in pairs, and the pairs can be combined into operations that move one quantum from one mode to another. On states holding a single quantum, these operations behave exactly like the entries of an $n \times n$ matrix. This matrix structure is what later lets a sphere emerge from the modes.
scrambling.boundary-mode-space-matrix.typing_note: Removed the edge to the current-commutator result: the proof cites it only as the place the same bilinear computation was used for the currents, and derives the general-index commutator directly from the CAR; doubtful only if the maintainer reads that citation as the source of the identity.

proofs.main: The commutator identity is the bilinear computation used already in \cite[Prop.~6.1]{ButlerT7} (there for the currents; here for general index pairs): $[\psi_i^\dagger\psi_j, \psi_k^\dagger\psi_l] = \delta_{jk}\psi_i^\dagger\psi_l - \delta_{li}\psi_k^\dagger\psi_j$ from the CAR (\claimref{std-algebra.witt-basis-car}). Each $E_{ij}$ maps the one-particle subspace $\operatorname{span}\{\psi_k^\dagger|0\rangle\}$ to itself, acting as $e_{ij}$ ($E_{ij}\psi_k^\dagger|0\rangle = \delta_{jk}\psi_i^\dagger|0\rangle$); the matrix units generate $\Mat_n$, so the restriction map is onto. The doubling is what supplies the complex structure: each real mode with its adjoined partner supplies the complex $\psi_i, \psi_i^\dagger$ from which the gauge-invariant $E_{ij}$ are built; real Clifford directions alone give the orthogonal bilinears, and it is the pairing that produces $\mathfrak{gl}(n)$. The script checks the commutator table and the one-particle action exactly on a five-mode instance.

scrambling.candidate-principles-their-yi.technical:
A calibration principle assigns to the exceptional set $E = \{\tau = 0\} \times \mathbb{R}_t \times S^2$ a count of boundary-mode fermions per modular period. Of three natural candidates, (P1), one fermion per Planck cell of the slice, gives $N_{\mathrm{epoch}} = 16\pi\,\SBH$, but its coefficient scales as $c_0^{3/2}$ with the cutoff scheme: the proper-time scheme gives $\tfrac32$ times the curvature scheme's value and the Kretschmann scheme $12^{1/4}$ times it, an irrational multiple.

(P3), one fermion per Planck cell of the horizon-normalised sphere once per modular period, gives $N_{\mathrm{epoch}} = A = 4\,\SBH$ in every scheme, because the horizon-normalised coframe on $E$ is exactly $(dt,\ r_h\,d\theta,\ r_h\sin\theta\,d\varphi)$. (P2), fundamentals per sphere aggregated over the epoch, breaks the scaling in $M$.
scrambling.candidate-principles-their-yi.lay: To pin down how many modes the black hole interior carries, one needs a rule for counting them on its inner boundary. Of three natural rules, the first gives a number that depends on an arbitrary choice of where to cut off the geometry, the second gives four times the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy whatever that choice, and the third fails to grow with the mass in the right way. So none of the three returns the entropy itself.
scrambling.candidate-principles-their-yi.typing_note: All four uses are premises of the proof (slice count, scheme constants, collar coframe, failed aggregation) and are kept; the remaining E204 comes from the collar-coframe Fact, outside this list. Levels pass: conditions already kept.

scrambling.clock-inventory-boundary-mode.technical:
An intrinsic flow of the boundary-mode algebra is a one-parameter group of inner automorphisms with even generator preserving the vector grade; such flows are generated by bivectors, quadratic in the pair operators. A clock is an intrinsic flow whose adjoint action on the mode operators is semisimple with real eigenvalues, the nonzero ones of one common magnitude normalised to unit rapidity. For a single completed pair the only clock is the boost, converted to Schwarzschild time at the surface gravity $\kappa = 1/4M$.

For $n$ modes, a bivector with adjoint spectrum $\{+c, 0, -c\}$ is $O(n,n)$-conjugate, by Witt extension, to $c$ times a sum of standard atom boosts, and the geometric normalisation converts every such flow at the same $\kappa$. Examples are the single-atom boosts $E_{ii}$, the rotated-pair boosts $E_{ij} + E_{ji}$ and the pairing terms $c\,\psi_i^\dagger\psi_j^\dagger + d\,\psi_j\psi_i$ with $cd > 0$; antisymmetric, nilpotent and unequal-weight combinations are not clocks. Every clock therefore has period $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa = 8\pi M$.
scrambling.clock-inventory-boundary-mode.lay: The black hole's boundary modes can evolve internally in many ways, but only some of these behave like clocks ticking at a steady rate. Every such clock, however it is built from the modes, runs at one and the same rate, set by the surface gravity of the horizon. So all of them share a single period, the black hole's natural thermal cycle.

proofs.main: (i) is the algebra's own inventory: a one-parameter group of inner automorphisms of a Clifford algebra preserving the vector grade is generated by an even element whose commutator preserves grade one, i.e.\ by a bivector (the commutator of a vector with a grade-$2k$ element has grade $2k - 1$, so only $k = 1$ preserves the vector space; a mixed even generator $A_2 + A_4 + \cdots$ reduces to its bivector part, since grade preservation forces $[A_{2k}, v] = 0$ for every vector $v$ when $k \geq 2$, making each higher $A_{2k}$ central, and an even central element is a scalar; scalars generate nothing). The single-pair clause of (ii) is the import, proved in \cite[Prop.~2.1]{ButlerT7} (\claimref{hawking.modular-structure-completed-pair}), unique up to reparametrisation and orientation: the algebra fixes the orbits, not the speed, and the geometric normalisation of \cite[App.~A]{ButlerT5} is what fixes the speed, converting rapidity, and only rapidity, to Schwarzschild time at $\kappa = 1/4M$, so a rescaled generator traverses the same orbits and defines the same clock, not a faster one. For (iii): the flow a bivector $X$ generates acts on the mode operators by $\operatorname{ad}_X$, which is insensitive to a central shift ($\operatorname{ad}_{E_{ii}} = \operatorname{ad}_{E_{ii} - 1/2}$), so it is the adjoint spectrum and not the one-particle spectrum that the classification must read. From the canonical anticommutation relations of the mode operators (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.boundary-mode-space-matrix}), $[E_{ij}, \psi_k^\dagger] = \delta_{jk}\psi_i^\dagger$ and $[E_{ij}, \psi_k] = -\delta_{ik}\psi_j$. Hence $\operatorname{ad}_{E_{ii}}$ has eigenvalues $\pm 1$ on $(\psi_i^\dagger, \psi_i)$ and $0$ elsewhere, and the atom's boost bivector $\sigma_i = 2(\hat n_i - \tfrac12)$ (Fact \claimref{scrambling.imported-modes-modular-inventory}) generates that same flow in the rotor convention $e^{\sigma_i t/2}(\cdot)\,e^{-\sigma_i t/2}$: unit rapidity. The equal-coefficient sum $\sum_i E_{ii}$ gives $\pm 1$ on every mode, the simultaneous boost of all $n$ atoms and the statement's common clock; what is compact here is the phase circle $e^{\theta J\hat n}$, with $J = e_2e_3$ the complex unit of the boundary modes, the transverse bivector, which commutes with the mode operators (numbers on the boundary modes are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$, \claimref{synthesis.transverse-bivector-is-the-complex-unit-of-the-radial-atom}), whose generator is $J$ times a bivector, which the real Clifford algebra of the boundary modes excludes, its centre being scalar, so the phase circle is not an intrinsic flow in the sense of (i); the single-atom instance of the exclusion is published as \cite[Prop.~7.21(3)]{ButlerT5} (\claimref{singularity.euclidean-rotor-where-it-lies}). For $i \neq j$, $\operatorname{ad}_{E_{ij} + E_{ji}}$ has eigenvectors $\psi_i^\dagger \pm \psi_j^\dagger$ with eigenvalues $\pm 1$, and $E_{ij} + E_{ji} = \hat n_+ - \hat n_-$ exactly in the rotated modes $(\psi_i \pm \psi_j)/\sqrt{2}$: again unit rapidity. The antisymmetric $E_{ij} - E_{ji}$ has adjoint eigenvalues $\pm J$ (its adjoint action squares to $-1$ on the planes $\mathrm{span}\{\psi_i^\dagger, \psi_j^\dagger\}$ and $\mathrm{span}\{\psi_i, \psi_j\}$) and is compact; the single $E_{ij}$ with $i \neq j$ is nilpotent, generating a unipotent shear; neither carries a rapidity. A diagonal $\sum_i c_i E_{ii}$ has adjoint eigenvalues $\pm c_i$, so unequal $|c_i|$ leave no common rapidity and admit no single conversion. The pairing sector is classified by one product: from the CAR, $\operatorname{ad}$ of $c\,\psi_i^\dagger\psi_j^\dagger + d\,\psi_j\psi_i$ maps $\psi_i^\dagger \mapsto d\,\psi_j$, $\psi_j \mapsto c\,\psi_i^\dagger$, $\psi_j^\dagger \mapsto -d\,\psi_i$, $\psi_i \mapsto -c\,\psi_j^\dagger$, two $2 \times 2$ blocks each with eigenvalues $\pm\sqrt{cd}$: hyperbolic for $cd > 0$, where unequal coefficients rescale the common rapidity rather than remove it ($2\psi_i^\dagger\psi_j^\dagger + \tfrac12\psi_j\psi_i$ is a clock at unit rapidity outright); compact for $cd < 0$, eigenvalues $\pm J\sqrt{|cd|}$; nilpotent for $cd = 0$. Every clock in the inventory is therefore hyperbolic with unit rapidity after normalisation, hence by the Witt-extension clause of (iii), in the split space of the $n$ hyperbolic pairs of \claimref{tower.witt-index-quantum-capacity}, $O(n,n)$-conjugate to a sum of standard atom boosts, and the geometric normalisation converts them all at the one $\kappa$. What is unique is the rate, not the flow. Normalisation sets the nonzero adjoint eigenvalues to $\pm 1$, so the continuation of any clock to imaginary rapidity acts on the mode operators by $e^{\mp J\theta}$ (the rotor flow at rapidity $\lambda = J\theta$) and has conjugation period exactly $2\pi$, the atom's period of Fact \claimref{scrambling.imported-modes-modular-inventory} (\cite[Prop.~7.21(1)]{ButlerT5}); at the geometric rate $\kappa$ that period is the Schwarzschild span $2\pi/\kappa = \beta$.

scrambling.epoch-modular-period-two-unkn.formal:
Assume (IC). Then the counted epoch is the modular period:
\[
\Delta t \;=\; \beta \;=\; \frac{2\pi}{\kappa} \;=\; 8\pi M \qquad \text{(Schwarzschild)}.
\]
The conversion is exact and holds in both directions: with the epoch fixed, the area-law condition $\nu\,\Delta t = M/2$ of Proposition \claimref{scrambling.area-law-test} becomes a prediction for the density factor,
\[
\nu \;=\; \frac{M/2}{8\pi M} \;=\; \frac{1}{16\pi}
\]
in the 1-nat convention ($\nu = 1/(16\pi\ln 2)$ in T5's capacity convention, Remark \claimref{note.scrambling.density-factor-stated-full}; the section “The calibration factorised, and the quarter examined” shows the capacity convention is the one with physical content and restates the prediction there), and a calibration principle for the exceptional set (which carries one ladder pair per point, its degeneration having corank exactly one there, Theorem \claimref{sheaf.schwarzschild-degeneration-boundary-tame}(2); the section “The calibration factorised, and the quarter examined” says what it must produce) must return that number \emph{or refute the premise (IC)}. Two unknowns have become one equation and one falsifiable identification; the count's remaining condition is a single dimensionless number with a named derivation route and a named failure mode. The scale $\Delta t \sim M$ is thereby derived rather than imported, cohering with Theorem \claimref{scrambling.mode-count}'s own observation that the accrual rate is set by the horizon's temperature: the singularity keeps the horizon's scale.
scrambling.epoch-modular-period-two-unkn.technical:

u\,\Delta t = M/2$ gives $
u = 1/16\pi$ in the 1-nat convention, and $
u = 1/(16\pi\ln 2)$ in the capacity convention.

The two unknowns $(\Delta t, 
u)$ thus become one number: a calibration principle for the exceptional set must return this value or refute (IC). The epoch of order $M$ is then derived rather than imported, consistent with the accrual rate being set by the Hawking temperature. This is a different fixing from the singularity paper's counted-epoch postulate (C3), whose causal epoch $\Delta t(\varepsilon) = 2M(\ln(1/\varepsilon) - 	frac83 + 2\ln 2)$ equals $8\pi M$ only at $\varepsilon = e^{-(4\pi + 8/3 - 2\ln 2)} \approx 9.7 	imes 10^{-7}$; results that rest on (C3) are not thereby results under (IC).
scrambling.epoch-modular-period-two-unkn.lay: The entropy count needed two unknown inputs: how long to count for, and how densely modes are packed. scrambling.exact-factorisation-thinning.technical:
In Planck units, with $r_h = 2M$, $A = 16\pi M^2$, $\beta = 8\pi M$ and $\SBH = A/4$, the slice count per unit Killing time is $8\pi M = 4\pi r_h = A/r_h$, and per modular period it is $N_{\mathrm{slice}} = 64\pi^2M^2$, so $N_{\mathrm{slice}}/\SBH = 16\pi$, both at leading order in $r_c/2M$.

The factor splits exactly as $16\pi = (\beta/r_h)\times(A/\SBH) = 4\pi \times 4$, and the first factor, $\beta/r_h = 2\pi/(\kappa r_h) = 4\pi$ with $\kappa = 1/(2r_h)$, is universal for Schwarzschild.
scrambling.exact-factorisation-thinning.lay: Counting one mode per Planck-sized cell of the black hole's inner slice, per thermal period, overshoots the entropy by a factor of $16\pi$, at leading order in the ratio of the cutoff to the hole's size. That factor splits exactly into two pieces: $4\pi$, the ratio of the hole's thermal period to its radius, the same for every Schwarzschild black hole, and $4$, the ratio of horizon area to entropy.

scrambling.exactness-excludes-cutoff-dep.formal:
Suppose a calibration principle returns $N_{\mathrm{epoch}} = \SBH = 4\pi M^2$ exactly and its count is a monomial $c\,\pi^p M^m$ in the geometric data of the interior with $c$ rational. Then the count cannot depend on the stretched radius $r_c$: any dependence on $r_c$ through a power $r_c^a$, $a 
eq 0$, carries the scheme constant $c_0^a$, which differs between the three schemes for every real $a 
eq 0$ and, for rational $a$, is irrational for the Kretschmann scheme whenever $a 
otin 6\mathbb{Z}$. The principle must therefore be normalised at a scale the interior fixes without a cutoff. Exactness does not choose that scale: the interior fixes the horizon $r_h = 2M$, at which the sphere carries $A = 4\,\SBH$ cells and the count is $\SBH$ with the residue $	frac14$ on the cells (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.residue-each-convention}(i)), and it fixes equally the rational multiple $r_* = M = r_h/2$, at which the sphere carries $4\pi M^2 = \SBH$ cells and the residue is $1$. Which of the two a principle should mean is not decided here.
scrambling.exactness-excludes-cutoff-dep.technical:
Suppose a calibration principle returns exactly $N_{\mathrm{epoch}} = \SBH = 4\pi M^2$ as a monomial $c\,\pi^p M^m$ with rational $c$. Then it cannot depend on the stretched radius $r_c$: a factor $r_c^a$ with $a \neq 0$ carries the scheme constant $c_0^a$, which differs between the three cutoff schemes for every real $a \neq 0$ and, for rational $a$, is irrational in the Kretschmann scheme unless $a \in 6\mathbb{Z}$.

The principle must therefore be normalised at a radius the interior fixes without a cutoff. Exactness leaves two such radii: the horizon $r_h = 2M$, where the sphere carries $A = 4\,\SBH$ cells and the residue is $\tfrac14$, and $r_* = M$, where the sphere carries $\SBH$ cells and the residue is $1$. Which one a principle should use is not decided.
scrambling.exactness-excludes-cutoff-dep.lay: If a rule for counting boundary modes is to reproduce the black hole entropy exactly, with a count of the simple form a rational number times powers of $\pi$ and of the mass, it cannot depend on where one cuts off the interior geometry, because different reasonable cut-offs give incompatible answers. The rule must be tied to a size the black hole fixes by itself. Two such sizes remain, the horizon radius and half of it, and the result does not choose between them.

proofs.main: $c_0^a$ for the three schemes of \claimref{scrambling.scheme-robustness-cutoff} is $2^{a/3}$, $2^{2a/3}3^{a/6}$, $2^{-a/3}3^{2a/3}$; their ratios $2^{a/3}3^{a/6}$ and $2^{-2a/3}3^{2a/3}$ are not $1$ for real $a \neq 0$, so a count carrying $r_c^a$ takes different values in different schemes, and a scheme-dependent count cannot equal the scheme-independent $\SBH$ in all of them; for rational $a$ the Kretschmann constant $48^{a/6} = 2^{2a/3}\,3^{a/6}$ is rational exactly when both exponents are integers, that is when $a \in 6\mathbb{Z}$, and is otherwise irrational (at $a = 3/2$, for instance, it is $2\cdot 3^{1/4}$). The Schwarzschild interior has one dimensionful parameter, $M$, so a cutoff-free radius is a fixed multiple of $M$; the horizon is the distinguished one, with residue $\tfrac14$ (\claimref{scrambling.residue-each-convention}(i)), and $r_* = M$ is the one at which the residue is $1$, the sphere's cell count there being $\SBH$ itself; the script displays both as arithmetic. The argument excludes the cutoff; it does not rank the two.

scrambling.imported-kostant-madore-parti.formal: (i) Embeddings of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ into $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ are classified, up to conjugation, by the partition of $n$ given by the restriction of the defining representation; the \emph{principal} embedding is the one with a single part (the irreducible $n$-dimensional representation), and it is essentially unique. (ii) For the principal embedding the adjoint decomposition of $\Mat_n$ is multiplicity-free: $\Mat_n \cong \bigoplus_{\ell=0}^{n-1}(2\ell + 1)$, one spin-$\ell$ multiplet for each $\ell < n$ (Kostant). (iii) $\Mat_n$ with this $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ structure is Madore's fuzzy sphere, whose large-$n$ limit is the round $S^2$ \cite{Madore1992}, radius excluded: the radius is scale. \emph{Provenance:} \cite{Kostant1959} (the principal three-dimensional subgroup and the multiplicity-free adjoint decomposition) and \cite{Madore1992} (the fuzzy sphere and its large-$n$ limit); the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ classification is classical representation theory.
scrambling.imported-kostant-madore-parti.technical:
Embeddings of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ into $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ are classified up to conjugation by partitions of $n$, read off from how the defining representation splits; the principal embedding is the one with a single part, the irreducible $n$-dimensional representation, and it is essentially unique. For it the adjoint decomposition is multiplicity-free, $\Mat_n \cong \bigoplus_{\ell=0}^{n-1}(2\ell+1)$, one spin-$\ell$ multiplet for each $\ell < n$ (Kostant).

With this $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ structure, $\Mat_n$ is Madore's fuzzy sphere, whose large-$n$ limit is the round $S^2$; the radius is not fixed by the algebra and is a separate scale.
scrambling.imported-kostant-madore-parti.lay: There are several ways to make matrices of a given size behave like rotations, and they are labelled by ways of splitting the size into smaller pieces. The principal way uses no splitting at all. Then the matrices form a fuzzy sphere, a finite approximation to an ordinary sphere that becomes the round sphere as the matrices grow. These are established results of Kostant and Madore.

B. Kostant, The principal three-dimensional subgroup and the Betti numbers of a complex simple Lie group, Amer. J. Math. 81 (1959), 973--1032.

scrambling.intrinsic-clock-ic-flagged-pr.formal:
The counted epoch is intrinsic to the boundary modes: whatever span of Killing time the count is taken over is determined by the dynamical structure of the boundary modes themselves, not by an external choice. This is a naturality premise, not a theorem; its named failure mode is stated in Theorem \claimref{scrambling.epoch-modular-period-two-unknowns-become}, and the circularity fence of Remark \claimref{note.scrambling.circularity-fence} protects it from self-confirmation.

\emph{Scope (Schwarzschild calibration).} This premise, with Premises \claimref{singularity.c1-curvature-cutoff} and \claimref{singularity.c2-cell-density}, is read as a calibration of the count on the Schwarzschild family only, where it makes the counted epoch the modular period (Theorem \claimref{scrambling.epoch-modular-period-two-unknowns-become}). Read with a horizon's modular period on a Schwarzschild-de Sitter hole, the literal cutoff count with the density fixed at $\Lambda = 0$ is $u/(3u - 2)$ times $A_{b}/4$, $u = 2M/r_{b}$, for every $\Lambda > 0$, and neither horizon's period gives $A_{b}/4$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cutoff-count-is-not-a-local-density-on-sds}); the literal cutoff count also misses the area law for spinning holes with $a \ge 2(2M)^{2/3}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.kerr-ring-count-misses-area-law}). Away from the Schwarzschild family the count is read through the horizon placement of clause (Loc) of Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise}, with a density fixed by flat tangent data.
scrambling.intrinsic-clock-ic-flagged-pr.technical:
The intrinsic-clock premise (IC) states that the span of Killing time over which the boundary modes are counted is fixed by the dynamical structure of the boundary modes themselves, not chosen from outside. It is a naturality premise, not a theorem.

Its failure mode is explicit: under (IC) the epoch is the modular period $\beta$ and the density must be $\nu = 1/16\pi$ in the 1-nat convention, so a calibration returning any other value refutes it. A circularity fence keeps it from confirming itself.

It is read as a calibration on the Schwarzschild family only. scrambling.no-attic-route.formal:
T5's eviction theorem runs on an axiom (A), that modes exiting the window deposit their correlations in the window-radiation accounting, with no third sector. The derivation route, assembled from the series' theorems: by the localisation provided by the wall results, operator-valued degrees of freedom exist within the physical closure only where division fails (the window mode space and the radiation's partner modes are the only q-number sectors) \cite[\S 5 and \S 8]{ButlerT4}, \cite[\S 10--11]{ButlerT5}; and by the iteration corollary of the tower paper T3, one ascent completes the description on the physical closure, with no further rungs demanded there \cite[Cor.~6.2]{ButlerT3}: there is no further completion in which a third sector (an attic) could lie. Hence (A)'s content reduces to the \emph{exhaustiveness} of the localisation (the no-remnant, closure-completeness claim), exactly as T5's own derivation records; that exhaustiveness remains the conjectural core, inherited and named, and this assembly's contribution is to have isolated it: everything else in (A) is theorem-backed.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{The derivation, step by step.} A violation of (A) requires a q-number sector outside the localisation's inventory, which the cited theorems forbid on the physical closure given exhaustiveness; the three imports are cited in the statement.
scrambling.no-attic-route.technical:
The eviction theorem for the boundary modes rests on an axiom (A): modes leaving the window deposit their correlations in the window and radiation accounting, with no third sector. The wall results localise operator-valued degrees of freedom on the physical closure to where division fails, the window modes and the radiation's partner modes, and one ascent completes the description on the physical closure, leaving no further completion where a third sector (an attic) could lie.

Assembled, these reduce the content of (A) to the exhaustiveness of the localisation, the no-remnant or closure-completeness claim. That exhaustiveness remains the conjectural core; everything else in (A) is backed by theorems.
scrambling.no-attic-route.lay: A key step in the framework's account of black-hole evaporation assumes there is no hidden attic where information could be stored apart from the hole's interior modes and the outgoing radiation. Combining earlier results shows that this assumption comes down to one remaining question: whether the known places where quantum degrees of freedom can live are the only ones. That question is still open, but it is now isolated.

scrambling.no-echo-prediction-registered.formal:
The registered prediction: post-merger ringdown is the Kerr quasinormal spectrum of general relativity with \emph{no} modification, and in particular no echo train at the Planck-structure delay $\tau_{\mathrm{echo}} \approx 8M\ln(M/m_P)$ (the delay at which near-horizon structure at Planck distance would reflect \cite{CardosoPani2017}), of order tens to hundreds of milliseconds for stellar-mass remnants ($35$ ms at $10\,M_\odot$, $0.1$ to $0.25$ s for remnants of $30$ to $70\,M_\odot$): within the sensitivity band of existing detectors. The prediction is stated so that it can fail.

\emph{Basis.} (1) \emph{The field equations at and across the future horizon.} The gravitational field obeys Einstein's equations with a constant $\Lambda$, from the stored action on the field space of Premise \claimref{synthesis.field-space-premise-parallel-frozen-point} (FS) (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.macdowell-mansouri-principle-fixes-the-trace-free-part}), read on the invertible region through the equivalence of Fact \claimref{interior.imported-equivalence-einstein-equations}; the quasinormal spectrum uses the ingoing condition at the future horizon, which is the regularity of the classical field there. (2) \emph{No structure at the horizon beyond the matter fields.} By the identification clause of Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise} the modes on a horizon's light rays are the matter field on those light rays, and the modes that Postulates (C1) and (C2) place at the curvature cutoff are the same set described a second time (its paragraph ``One mode set, per light ray''). (3) \emph{Reading, stated and not derived.} The horizon's modes impose no reflecting condition on classical perturbations of the gravitational field. This does not follow from (2) as written: clause (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) of that premise makes the modes thermal before a crossing, and a flux reflectivity equal to the Boltzmann factor $e^{-\hbar|\omega|/kT_{H}}$ has been derived in the literature from detailed balance and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem at a horizon (Oshita, Wang and Afshordi, arXiv:1905.00464, JCAP 04 (2020) 016; abstract checked on 11 November 2026), with echoes as its consequence; the reading excludes it. (4) \emph{A state regular across the horizon.} The local form of Premise \claimref{synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state} at the points of the horizon's generators, argued there at leading order.

\emph{What an echo would refute.} A single statistically confirmed echo train would refute the field equations at the horizon, and so (FS) with the stored action (its refutation condition (b)), or the reading (3). It does not bear on the Schwarzschild calibration of the count by Postulates (C1) and (C2).

\emph{Note (the earlier basis, 2026-11-11).} Until version 2 the prediction rested on Postulate \claimref{singularity.c1-curvature-cutoff} (C1) alone, with the wording that the quantum structure lies at the stretched singularity ``and nowhere near the horizon''. (C1) is now read as a calibration of the count on the Schwarzschild family only, and by (2) the same modes are on the horizon, on Schwarzschild and on Kerr alike; that wording is withdrawn and (C1) is no longer in the basis. With this basis the prediction is general relativity's own: it registers that the series predicts no departure from general relativity at the horizon, and a null result does not distinguish the series from general relativity. The deposited text (T8, Record 7.1) is kept under source\_formal.

Its basis has four parts: Einstein's equations at and across the future horizon, from the stored action under the field-space premise (FS); the horizon's modes being the matter field on its light rays (the local-horizon premise), so that no further structure sits at the horizon; the stated reading that these modes reflect no classical perturbation, which excludes the thermal reflectivity proposed in the literature; and a state regular across the horizon (the local form of (N$_{+}$)). One statistically confirmed echo train would refute the field equations at the horizon or that reading.

The prediction is shared with general relativity. Until version 2 it rested on Postulate (C1) and said the quantum structure was nowhere near the horizon; that wording is withdrawn.
scrambling.no-echo-prediction-registered.lay: If quantum effects altered a black hole's surface, merging black holes would ring with faint repeated echoes a fraction of a second after the main signal. In this framework gravity obeys Einstein's equations right through the horizon, and nothing sits at the horizon except the ordinary matter fields, which are taken not to reflect gravitational waves. So it predicts no echoes: the ringing should be exactly as general relativity says. A single confirmed echo would refute that. The prediction is the same as general relativity's.

scrambling.no-recount-reaches-quarter.formal: Let a counting rule assign to the exceptional set a tally that is a rational number of modes per cell, with cells whose areas are rational multiples of integer powers of $\pi$ in Planck units, over a rational number of ticks per modular period. Then its residue $\kappa_c$ is a rational multiple of an integer power of $\pi$, $\kappa_c = q\pi^k$ with $q \in \mathbb{Q}$ and $k \in \mathbb{Z}$. In the capacity convention the target is $\kappa_c = 1/(4\ln 2)$; equality would require $\pi^k\ln 2 \in \mathbb{Q}$, which is false for $k = 0$, $\ln 2$ being transcendental \cite[Thm.~1.4]{Baker1975}, so no rule with $k = 0$ reaches the target; for $k \neq 0$ it would contradict the expected algebraic independence of $\pi$ and $\ln 2$, which is not a theorem, so the exclusion of rules with $k \neq 0$ is conditional on that independence. In the 1-nat convention the target $\kappa_c = \tfrac14$ is rational, and the natural rules of Proposition \claimref{scrambling.candidate-principles-their-yields} return $\kappa_c = 4\pi$ (P1), $\kappa_c = 1$ (P3) and a broken scaling (P2), none of them $\tfrac14$.

Their residue is $\kappa_c = q\pi^k$ with $q \in \mathbb{Q}$ and $k \in \mathbb{Z}$. In the capacity convention the target $\kappa_c = 1/(4\ln 2)$ would need $\pi^k\ln 2 \in \mathbb{Q}$: false for $k = 0$, since $\ln 2$ is transcendental, and excluded for $k \neq 0$ only conditionally on the expected algebraic independence of $\pi$ and $\ln 2$.

In the 1-nat convention the target $\kappa_c = \tfrac14$ is rational, but the natural rules give $\kappa_c = 4\pi$, $\kappa_c = 1$ and a broken scaling, none of them $\tfrac14$.
scrambling.no-recount-reaches-quarter.lay: One might hope to reach the black hole entropy simply by recounting the interior modes more cleverly. Any recount built from whole-number ratios and powers of $\pi$ cannot hit the required value in the capacity convention, where the target involves $\ln 2$: for one class of rules this is proved outright, and for the rest it assumes a widely expected but unproved fact about $\pi$ and $\ln 2$. In the other convention the natural recounts simply miss.

scrambling.per-slice-verification-two-fa.formal:
Let $n$ be the linear size of the slice's matrix algebra. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(The slice check, exact in scaling.)} Matching the fuzzy operator dimension to the slice sphere's Planck-cell count sets $n^2 = 4\pi r_c^2 = 4\pi(2M)^{2/3}$ to leading order ($n$ is an integer matrix size and the right side transcendental; what the match fixes exactly is the $M^{2/3}$ scaling): the fuzzy count reproduces, from the matrix side, exactly the sphere-only case of Proposition \claimref{scrambling.uniqueness-internal-scaling}, its $M^{2/3}$ scaling. The fuzzy geometry and the metric geometry agree slice by slice.
\item \emph{(Operator-cell aggregation fails, by exactly the area coefficient.)} Counting one boundary-mode fermion per operator cell of the epoch volume is the $\nu = 1$ reading, which overshoots $N_{\mathrm{epoch}} = \SBH$ by exactly $16\pi$ (Corollary \claimref{scrambling.integer-holographic-form-identification}(3)): the required thinning is the horizon-area coefficient itself.
\item \emph{(Fundamental-per-slice aggregation breaks the scaling.)} Counting $n \propto M^{1/3}$ fundamentals per sphere and aggregating over the epoch's spheres (the slice volume of Proposition \claimref{scrambling.slice-volume-exactly-per-unit-killing} contains $8\pi M/4\pi r_c^2 = (2M)^{1/3}$ spheres per unit Killing time) gives
\[
N_{\mathrm{fund}} \;\propto\; M^{1/3}\cdot M^{1/3}\cdot \Delta t \;\propto\; M^{5/3} \quad (\Delta t \sim M),
\]
which breaks the area scaling altogether.
\end{enumerate}
Both direct aggregation rules fail, so the slice-to-epoch aggregation is the weighted completion's task: derive $N_{\mathrm{epoch}} = \SBH$, or refute the intrinsic-clock premise.

The two direct ways of aggregating slices over an epoch both fail. One fermion per operator cell of the epoch volume is the $\nu = 1$ reading and overshoots $N_{\mathrm{epoch}} = \SBH$ by exactly $16\pi$. Counting $n \propto M^{1/3}$ fundamentals per sphere over the $(2M)^{1/3}$ spheres per unit Killing time gives $N_{\mathrm{fund}} \propto M^{5/3}$ for $\Delta t \sim M$, breaking the area scaling. The aggregation is left to the weighted completion, which must derive $N_{\mathrm{epoch}} = \SBH$ or refute the intrinsic-clock premise.

The bilinear sector is then canonically Madore's fuzzy sphere, with the round transverse $S^2$ as its large-$n$ limit and the radius left to the state. scrambling.residue-each-convention.technical:
Write the epoch count as $N_{\mathrm{epoch}} = \kappa_c \times A \times 1$, horizon-normalised sphere cells times one tick per modular period, with $\kappa_c$ the calibration residue (distinct from the surface gravity $\kappa$). In the 1-nat convention $N_{\mathrm{epoch}} = \SBH$ gives $\kappa_c = \tfrac14$; in the capacity convention $N_{\mathrm{epoch}}\ln 2 = \SBH$ gives $\kappa_c = 1/(4\ln 2)$, one mode per Bekenstein-Mukhanov area quantum of horizon per period.

The two differ by $\ln 2$, and only the capacity convention compares an entropy with an entropy, since a fermionic mode carries at most $\ln 2$ nats; the exact $16\pi$ belongs to the 1-nat convention, the physical thinning being $16\pi\ln 2$. One boundary mode registers one helicity, so the capacity per mode is $\ln 2$, not $2\ln 2$, and $\kappa_c = 1/(4\ln 2)$ rather than $1/(8\ln 2)$.

scrambling.return-delay-scrambling-log-r.formal:
In the rate model, deposited information cannot return before the dwell time of the window (the epoch of the section “The epoch is the modular period”, the correct power of $M$); and charging the window-internal re-encoding at the framework's causal rate (one pairwise operation per boost e-fold $\kappa^{-1}$ per mode, spreading epidemically over the $N \sim S$ modes) requires of order $\ln S$ rounds of duration $\beta/2\pi$, giving a return delay
\[
T_{\mathrm{return}} \;\approx\; \frac{\beta}{2\pi}\,\ln S \;=\; 4M\,\ln S :
\]
the fast-scrambling time \cite{HaydenPreskill2007, SekinoSusskind2008}, recovered from the framework's own clock as a modular-time estimate. Under (L$_{E}$) this is a modular-time (rotor-flow) estimate, not a real-time delay (\claimref{singularity.l-boundary-mode-locality}): the rounds are e-folds of the rotor flow, whose rate is the phase flow's KMS rate, and pairwise spreading of the kind charged here does not occur in real time under number-diagonal dynamics (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.number-diagonal-dynamics-spreads-nothing}). This removes the instant-return artefact of T5's rate model; the first-principles account of the spreading exponent is Assembly \claimref{scrambling.spreading-law-chaos-bound-saturated}, and genuine chaotic dynamics beyond it remains open.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{The derivation, step by step.} The dwell floor is the epoch (Theorem \claimref{scrambling.epoch-modular-period-two-unknowns-become}, conditional on (IC)); the epidemic count is the standard doubling estimate, $\log_2 S$ rounds to reach $S$ modes from one, each round one causal step of the window's clock, the $\ln 2$ absorbed into the displayed approximation; the clock and its rate are the theorems cited. The coefficient $4M$ is exact arithmetic from $\beta = 8\pi M$, script-checked.

The return delay is therefore $T_{\mathrm{return}} \approx (\beta/2\pi)\ln S = 4M\ln S$, the fast-scrambling time, recovered from the framework's own clock. scrambling.spreading-law-chaos-bound-sat.formal:
Three framework-internal facts fix the window's internal dynamics. First, the intrinsic flows of a Clifford boundary-mode algebra are bivector-generated, quadratic in the pair operators (Lemma \claimref{scrambling.clock-inventory-boundary-modes}(i)). Second, the distinguished bivector flow is the boost (Fact \claimref{scrambling.imported-modes-modular-inventory}). Third, the boost is the translation clock of the window itself: the Killing flow that displaces modes along the window is the boost at rate $\kappa$, with the accrual rate of Theorem \claimref{scrambling.mode-count}. Boost-hyperbolic one-body dynamics expands operator amplitudes as $e^{\kappa t}$, so support deposited on a single mode spans the $N$-mode window at
\[
t_* \;=\; \kappa^{-1}\ln N \;=\; \frac{\beta}{2\pi}\,\ln S :
\]
the fast-scrambling law, with the logarithm the signature of hyperbolic dynamics rather than an assumption. Every intrinsic clock it has runs at the modular rate, and the expansion rate is exactly $2\pi T$: the boost group's support-dilation rate equals its KMS rate, $\kappa\beta = 2\pi$, which holds under (N$_{+}$) (\claimref{synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state}). The real-time Lyapunov exponent of this quasi-free dynamics is $0$: the one unitary group that dilates the support has bounded anticommutators on linear elements (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boost-evolution-on-generators-is-one-unitary-group}). So the Maldacena-Shenker-Stanford chaos bound is met, not saturated. \emph{Tier, declared:} what is derived is the free-fermion operator-spreading timescale under a generic quadratic coupling, in the rate-model normalisation; genuine chaotic saturation beyond free-fermion spreading is open, and is named as such in the section “Scope, and successor problems”.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{The derivation, step by step.} The inventory clauses are Lemma \claimref{scrambling.clock-inventory-boundary-modes} (proved) and its import (Fact \claimref{scrambling.imported-modes-modular-inventory}). The expansion computation: a quadratic generator containing the boost scales ladder operators by $e^{\pm\kappa t}$ (Fact \claimref{scrambling.imported-modes-modular-inventory}'s weight clause, exponentiated), so under a generic quadratic coupling the amplitude reaching a mode at mode distance $d$ grows as $e^{\kappa t}$ against an initial suppression of order $1/N$; support spans all the boundary modes when $e^{\kappa t} \sim N$, i.e.\ at $t_* = \kappa^{-1}\ln N$, and $N \sim S$ over an epoch of order $M$ (Proposition \claimref{scrambling.area-law-test}). The identification $\kappa^{-1} = \beta/2\pi$ is arithmetic ($\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$), checked by the script along with the Schwarzschild value $\beta/2\pi = 4M$. The MSS statement that no system exceeds the growth rate $2\pi T$ is the point of contact \cite{MSS2016}: the rate $\kappa$ at which support dilates is one group's rate set against its own KMS period $2\pi/\kappa$, while the out-of-time-order growth that the bound limits is absent from the quasi-free dynamics, so the bound is met and not saturated.
