scrambling.uniqueness-internal-scaling.formal: Call a timescale \emph{admissible} when the Schwarzschild geometry supplies it without tuning: the light-crossing, causal-epoch, and modular scales, $\Delta t \propto M$ up to logarithmic dressings, and the evaporation lifetime, $\Delta t \propto M^3$. Write the count as $N \propto M^p\,\Delta t$ with $p$ determined by the cutoff scheme. Then $p = 1$, produced by the framework's own curvature cutoff, is the \emph{unique} power for which an admissible timescale of order $M$ delivers the area law $N \propto M^2$: a sphere-only count (cells of the $r_c$-sphere, no $t$-stretch) gives $4\pi r_c^2 \propto M^{2/3}$, hence $p = 2/3$ and $N \sim M^{5/3}$; a fixed (mass-independent) cutoff radius gives volume per unit time $\propto \sqrt{M}$, hence $p = 1/2$ and $N \sim M^{3/2}$; and no admissible infrared choice repairs either: matching $M^{p + q} = M^2$ with $p \in \{2/3, 1/2\}$ requires $q \in \{4/3, 3/2\}$, and no admissible timescale has those exponents (a logarithmic dressing changes no exponent). The scaling test could have failed and did not.
scrambling.uniqueness-internal-scaling.technical:
Write the mode count as $N \propto M^p\,\Delta t$, with $p$ fixed by the cutoff scheme, and call a timescale admissible when the Schwarzschild geometry supplies it without tuning: the light-crossing, causal-epoch and modular scales, $\Delta t \propto M$ up to logarithmic dressings, and the evaporation lifetime, $\Delta t \propto M^3$. The framework's curvature cutoff gives $p = 1$, and with an admissible timescale of order $M$ this yields the area law $N \propto M^2$.

This power is unique among the schemes compared: a sphere-only count gives $p = 2/3$ and $N \sim M^{5/3}$, a fixed cutoff radius gives $p = 1/2$ and $N \sim M^{3/2}$, and repairing either would need a timescale exponent $q \in \{4/3, 3/2\}$, which no admissible timescale has, since a logarithmic dressing changes no exponent.
scrambling.uniqueness-internal-scaling.lay: The number of quantum modes counted near a black hole's singularity grows with the mass in a way that depends on where the count is cut off. Only the framework's own cutoff, combined with a natural timescale of the order of the black hole's mass, gives a count that grows like the horizon area, as black-hole entropy should. The other cutoffs considered give the wrong growth, and no natural choice of timescale repairs them.

singularity.area-law-test.formal:
Assume (C1)-(C3), write $N_{\mathrm{6a}} = (dN_{\mathrm{6a}}/dt)\,\Delta t$ for the mode count of the counted epoch, and let $C := N_{\mathrm{6a}}\ln 2$ be its boundary-mode capacity in nats, $\ln 2$ per fermionic mode. Then, at leading order in $M$, $C = S_{\mathrm{BH}} = 4\pi M^2$ if and only if $
u\,\Delta t = M/(2\ln 2)$: the capacity matches the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy \cite{Bekenstein1973, Hawking1975}, the coefficient calibrated by $
u\,\Delta t$ rather than predicted (the closing paragraph of this section quantifies the conventions), exactly when the counted epoch is of order one Schwarzschild time, which is what (C3) supplies via Lemma \claimref{singularity.causal-epoch-computed-exactly}, the $\ln 2$ being absorbed into the order-one calibration of $
u\,\Delta t$. It is the capacity, not the bare count, that premise (C) and Fact \claimref{singularity.assembled-page-curve-up-typicality} compare with $S_{\mathrm{BH}}$; the count itself then reads $N_{\mathrm{6a}} = S_{\mathrm{BH}}/\ln 2$. Counting over the hole's whole lifetime instead gives $N_{\mathrm{6a}} \sim M^4$, which shares with the interior-volume growth of Christodoulou-Rovelli \cite{CR2015} the linearity in advanced time and the unresolved tension with the constancy of the horizon entropy, though not the mass scaling: their $dV/dv \propto M^{2}$ gives $V \sim M^{5}$ over the lifetime, while $dN_{\mathrm{6a}}/dt \propto M$ gives $M^{4}$ here.
singularity.area-law-test.technical:
Under the postulates (C1) to (C3), let $N_{\mathrm{6a}} = (dN_{\mathrm{6a}}/dt)\,\Delta t$ be the mode count of the counted epoch and $C = N_{\mathrm{6a}}\ln 2$ its boundary-mode capacity in nats. Using the stretched-singularity count, $dN_{\mathrm{6a}}/dt = 8\pi
u M$ at leading order, the capacity equals the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, $C = \SBH = 4\pi M^2$, if and only if $
u\,\Delta t = M/(2\ln 2)$.

The match therefore holds exactly when the counted epoch is of order one Schwarzschild time, which is what (C3) supplies through the causal-epoch computation; the coefficient is calibrated through $
u\,\Delta t$, not predicted. Counting over the whole lifetime instead gives $N_{\mathrm{6a}} \sim M^4$.
singularity.area-law-test.lay: The framework counts quantum modes on a surface just outside a black hole's singularity. Granting the paper's three counting postulates (C1) to (C3), a curvature cutoff, a cell density and a counted epoch, and for large black holes (at leading order in the mass), if those modes are counted over a span of time comparable to the black hole's natural time scale, their total information capacity matches the standard black-hole entropy, which grows with the horizon area. The overall number is set by one order-one constant rather than predicted. Counting over the hole's whole life would instead give far too many modes.

singularity.assembled-page-curve-up-typi.formal:
Assume (i) the ascended description is globally pure, (ii) at each stage the joint state on radiation $\otimes$ partner-mode space is Page-typical, and (iii) the inputs of Theorem \claimref{singularity.eviction-window-thermal-product-radiation-entropy}, whose clause (2) supplies the thermal arm. Let $\Sth(t)$ be the thermal accumulation of the emitted radiation and $C(t) = N_{\mathrm{6a}}(M(t))\ln 2 \approx S_{\mathrm{BH}}(M(t))$ the boundary-mode capacity of Step 6a, $N_{\mathrm{6a}}$ its mode count. Then
\[
S_{\mathrm{rad}}(t) \;=\; \min\bigl(\Sth(t),\, C(t)\bigr)
\]
up to subleading corrections: rising along Hawking's curve, turning over at the crossing (about half the initial entropy), falling along the shrinking capacity, vanishing at complete evaporation. \emph{Assembly and provenance:} the capacity arm is the Schmidt inequality, self-contained (a pure bipartite state has equal marginal spectra, so $S_R = S_L \leq \ln\dim L = C$); the thermal arm is Theorem \claimref{singularity.eviction-window-thermal-product-radiation-entropy}(2) and needs boundary-mode locality, which is why (iii) is in the hypothesis line; saturation for typical states is Page's theorem \cite{Page1993} (\claimref{singularity.imported-page-average-entropy-subsystem}), the imported ingredient and the reason this is a Fact rather than a theorem of this paper; hypothesis (i) supplies purity, the emission count supplies $\dim R$, Proposition \claimref{singularity.stretched-singularity-count} with the epoch supplies $\dim L$, Proposition \claimref{singularity.area-law-test} identifies the capacity with the area law, and monotone mass loss makes $C$ decreasing.
singularity.assembled-page-curve-up-typi.technical:
Assume the ascended description is globally pure, that at each stage the joint state on radiation and partner modes is Page-typical, and the inputs of the eviction theorem. With $\Sth(t)$ the thermal accumulation of the emitted radiation and $C(t) = N_{\mathrm{6a}}(M(t))\ln 2 \approx \SBH(M(t))$ the boundary-mode capacity, the radiation entropy is $S_{\mathrm{rad}}(t) = \min(\Sth(t), C(t))$ up to subleading corrections.

The capacity arm is the Schmidt bound for a pure bipartite state, the thermal arm comes from the eviction theorem and needs boundary-mode locality, and saturation for typical states is imported from Page's theorem on the average entropy of a subsystem.

On the modes, the product of radiation and partner-mode space is the mode split of the Clifford algebra. For the even states used, the tensor product of marginals is the product of commuting even elements, the Schmidt statement (equal nonzero spectra of the two sides) holds for every pure even state, and a typical even state is drawn from a parity sector, not from an abstract tensor product; there the mean entropy exceeds Page's value by a rational amount of order $1/(mn)$, below the order at which this statement is made (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.mode-split-of-the-clifford-algebra-and-its-klein-twist-to-the-tensor-product}(iv), (v), (vii)). The statement is unchanged.
singularity.assembled-page-curve-up-typi.lay: The Page curve describes how the entropy of a black hole's radiation should behave if no information is lost: it rises, turns over at about half the initial entropy, and falls back to zero. This entry assembles that curve in the framework, up to small corrections, using the count of modes at the singularity as the black hole's capacity. It assumes that the full description stays pure, that the joint state of radiation and partner modes is typical in Page's sense, and that the inputs of the eviction theorem hold. The key step, that typical states reach the largest allowed entropy, is taken from Page's result rather than proved here.

proofs.main:
The capacity arm is the Schmidt inequality. By hypothesis (i) the joint state on radiation $R$ and partner modes $L$ is pure, so its two marginals have the same nonzero spectrum and
\[
S_{\mathrm{rad}} \;=\; S_R \;=\; S_L \;\leq\; \ln\dim L .
\]
The partner-mode space is the boundary-mode space of the counted epoch: Proposition \claimref{singularity.stretched-singularity-count} with the epoch gives $\dim L = 2^{N_{\mathrm{6a}}}$, so $\ln\dim L = N_{\mathrm{6a}}\ln 2 = C(t)$, and Proposition \claimref{singularity.area-law-test} identifies this capacity with $S_{\mathrm{BH}}(M(t))$ at leading order. Monotone mass loss makes $C$ decreasing.

The thermal arm is clause (2) of Theorem \claimref{singularity.eviction-window-thermal-product-radiation-entropy}, whose inputs (hypothesis (iii)) include boundary-mode locality: the radiation's entropy is its thermal accumulation $\Sth(t)$, and the emission count supplies $\dim R$, with $\ln\dim R = \Sth(t)$ at leading order. Hence $S_{\mathrm{rad}}(t) \leq \min(\Sth(t), C(t))$.

Saturation is Page's theorem (\claimref{singularity.imported-page-average-entropy-subsystem}): by hypothesis (ii) the joint state is Page-typical, so the smaller marginal's entropy is within $m/2n \leq 1/2$ nat of $\ln\min(\dim R, \dim L)$, a subleading correction. Therefore $S_{\mathrm{rad}}(t) = \min(\Sth(t), C(t))$ up to subleading corrections. The curve rises with $\Sth$ along Hawking's curve, turns over where the two arms cross (about half the initial entropy, as the paper's figure of the envelope shows), falls with the shrinking capacity, and vanishes at complete evaporation, where $C = 0$.

singularity.bundle-maps-quantise-without.formal: On a finite truncation the second quantisation of a bundle map $\{a_x\}$ of the mode line bundle is the sum of single-point bilinears $d\Gamma(a) = \sum_j \psi^{\dagger}_{x_j} a_{x_j} \psi_{x_j} = \sum_j a_{x_j} N_{x_j}$, a multiplication operator in the joint number basis, commuting with every occupation number. A one-particle map with a cross component $a_{xy} \neq 0$, $x \neq y$, quantises instead to a generator containing $\psi^{\dagger}_x\psi_y$, which carries the sector $(N_x, N_y) = (0,1)$ onto $(1,0)$.
singularity.bundle-maps-quantise-without.technical:
On a finite truncation, the second quantisation of a bundle map $\{a_x\}$ of the mode line bundle is a sum of single-point terms, $d\Gamma(a) = \sum_j a_{x_j} N_{x_j}$. It is therefore a multiplication operator in the joint number basis and commutes with every occupation number.

By contrast, a one-particle map with a cross component $a_{xy} \neq 0$, $x \neq y$, quantises to a generator containing $\psi^{\dagger}_x\psi_y$, which carries the sector $(N_x, N_y) = (0,1)$ onto $(1,0)$: that is hopping.
singularity.bundle-maps-quantise-without.lay: A bundle map acts separately at each point and never mixes different points. When such a map is turned into an operator on many-particle states, the result simply weighs each point by how many particles sit there, so it never moves a particle from one point to another. A map that does link two points, by contrast, produces exactly such a move.
singularity.bundle-maps-quantise-without.typing_note: No store premises; the proof applies the definition of second quantisation directly.

proofs.main: The block form is the definition of second quantisation applied to a bundle map, each summand a polynomial in one point's ladder, and for a line bundle $\psi^{\dagger}_x a_x \psi_x = a_x N_x$; the cross-component computation is $\psi^{\dagger}_x\psi_y|0_x 1_y\rangle = |1_x 0_y\rangle$. Both are verified as exact matrix identities, together with the controlled-$Z$ generator $\sigma_x\sigma_y$ conserving both occupations: cross-point diagonal products are not hopping and were never excluded.

singularity.c1-curvature-cutoff.formal:
The q-number boundary mode space of the singularity is supported on the stretched singularity, the surface on which the curvature reaches the Planck scale: $2M/r^3 = 1$ in Planck units, i.e.\ $r_c = (2M)^{1/3}$.

\emph{Note (form and calibration).} The form of this premise is forced, not chosen: an algebraic (pointwise) curvature criterion at a mass-independent value selects a member of the family $r_c^{3} = 2M/\lambda$, of which this premise is $\lambda = 1$, and, with an isometry-invariant density for Premise \claimref{singularity.c2-cell-density}, the leading count sees the threshold $\lambda$ and the density $\nu$ only through the one number $\kappa_{s} = \nu\lambda^{-1/2}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.c1-c2-forms-forced-one-number}). At leading order this premise together with (C2) is equivalent to (C2$'$), the modes carried by the exceptional set itself with $\nu' = \tfrac23\kappa_{s}$ modes per Planck area of its Kasner measure $\mu_{E} = 12\pi M$ per unit Killing time; the two differ only at relative order $(2M)^{-2/3}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.exceptional-boundary-measure-one-calibration}). The premise is kept as stated.

\emph{Scope (Schwarzschild calibration).} This premise, with Premise \claimref{singularity.c2-cell-density} and the intrinsic-clock premise (IC) (Premise \claimref{scrambling.intrinsic-clock-ic-flagged-premise}), is read as a calibration of the count on the Schwarzschild family only. Read literally on other holes the count fails the area law: on a Schwarzschild-de Sitter hole, with the counted epoch read as the hole's modular period, it is $u/(3u - 2)$ times $A_{b}/4$, $u = 2M/r_{b}$, for every $\Lambda > 0$, and no horizon's period gives $A_{b}/4$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cutoff-count-is-not-a-local-density-on-sds}); for a spinning hole with $a \ge 2(2M)^{2/3}$ the cutoff locus is a timelike tube beyond the inner horizon and the literal count misses the area law by a factor of order $M^{-1/3}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.kerr-ring-count-misses-area-law}). Away from the Schwarzschild family the count is read through the horizon placement, the modes on the horizon with a density fixed by flat tangent data, as clause (Loc) of Premise \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise} states. On Kerr the class of placements that the Note calls forced fails at both ends of the spin range: besides the tube at $a \ge 2(2M)^{2/3}$, at slow rotation ($0 < a \le \tfrac45\rho$, $\rho \le M/3$) no level set $|z| = \rho$ of the modulus of the curvature scale chosen independently of the spin, with any density, gives $A_{+}/4$ exactly at zero and at nonzero spin (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.no-spin-independent-modulus-level-set-gives-the-area-law-exactly-on-slow-kerr}); the window between the two regimes and criteria that use the phase of the complex scale are not treated. A count placed at fixed proper distance from the Kerr horizon locus is a fixed multiple of the area by construction, so it cannot fail and tests nothing; it is a hypothesis of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.stretched-horizon-count-on-kerr-is-a-multiple-of-the-area-by-construction} and is not adopted. This premise is unchanged.
singularity.c1-curvature-cutoff.technical:
Postulate: the q-number boundary mode space of the singularity is supported on the stretched singularity, the interior surface on which the curvature reaches the Planck scale, $2M/r^3 = 1$ in Planck units, so that $r_c = (2M)^{1/3}$.

It is taken as an axiom of the count, not derived: it fixes the surface on which the boundary modes are counted.

Its form is forced: any algebraic, mass-independent curvature criterion picks a slice $r_c^{3} = 2M/\lambda$, and this premise is the member $\lambda = 1$; with the uniform density of (C2) the leading count depends on the two premises only through one number, $\nu\lambda^{-1/2}$. At leading order the pair is equivalent to counting the modes on the exceptional set itself with its Kasner measure, with a single calibration constant, the premise (C2$'$). The series keeps (C1) and (C2) as they are.

The premise is read as a calibration on the Schwarzschild family only. Read literally elsewhere the count misses the area law: on a Schwarzschild-de Sitter hole, counted over the hole's own modular period, it exceeds a quarter of the horizon area by the factor $u/(3u - 2)$, $u = 2M/r_{b}$, and on fast-spinning holes the cutoff surface is a tube beyond the inner horizon whose literal count misses the area law by a factor of order $M^{-1/3}$; on slowly spinning holes no surface of fixed field-strength modulus, chosen independently of the spin, gives the area law exactly at zero and nonzero spin, so the class of placements that is forced on Schwarzschild fails on Kerr at both ends of the spin range. Elsewhere the count is the placement of the modes on the horizon with a density fixed by flat data.
singularity.c1-curvature-cutoff.lay: This assumption says where the quantum degrees of freedom near a black hole's singularity live: on the surface inside the black hole where the gravitational field strength (curvature) reaches the Planck scale. That surface sits at a radius growing like the cube root of the mass. It is an assumption of the counting, not a derived result, and it is used only to calibrate the count on non-rotating black holes in otherwise empty space; on spinning black holes, or with a positive cosmological constant, read literally it gives the wrong entropy.

The corank factor in $\nu$ is fixed at one, since the forced weighted completion gives exactly one ladder pair per point of the blown-up singular boundary; what remains in $\nu$ is the Planck-cell calibration.

Its form is forced: a density invariant under the isometries of the slice is uniform, and with the slice family any algebraic, mass-independent curvature criterion selects, the leading count depends on (C1) and (C2) only through one number, $\nu\lambda^{-1/2}$. At leading order the pair is equivalent to counting the modes on the exceptional set itself with its Kasner measure, with a single calibration constant, the premise (C2$'$). The series keeps (C1) and (C2) as they are.

The premise is read as a calibration on the Schwarzschild family only. With the density fixed there, the literal count on a Schwarzschild-de Sitter hole, over the hole's own modular period, exceeds a quarter of the horizon area by the factor $u/(3u - 2)$, $u = 2M/r_{b}$, and on fast-spinning holes it misses the area law by a factor of order $M^{-1/3}$. Elsewhere the count is the placement of the modes on the horizon with a density fixed by flat data.

That calibration is made on non-rotating black holes in otherwise empty space; on spinning black holes, or with a positive cosmological constant, the same rule read literally gives the wrong entropy.

singularity.causal-epoch-computed-exactl.formal:
For the Schwarzschild gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), along the rain worldlines of the interior, the radial infall worldlines with unit energy at infinity whose velocity $\hb^{-1}(x')$ is $D$-parallel and which are the worldlines of the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand frame of the section “Step 1: locate the failure” (velocity $e_t$ in the gauge $\hb = 1 - \beta P$), $|dt/dr| = \sqrt{r/2M}\;r/(2M - r)$ in static Killing time $t$, so the span of Killing time between crossing $r = 2M(1 - \varepsilon)$ and reaching the singular locus $r = 0$ is
\[
\Delta t(\varepsilon) \;=\; \int_0^{2M(1-\varepsilon)} \sqrt{\frac{r}{2M}}\,\frac{r\,dr}{2M - r}
\;=\; 4M\Bigl(\tfrac12\ln\frac{1+u}{1-u} - u - \tfrac{u^{3}}{3}\Bigr)\Big|_{u = \sqrt{1-\varepsilon}}
\;=\; 2M\Bigl(\ln\tfrac{1}{\varepsilon} - \tfrac83 + 2\ln 2\Bigr) + O(\varepsilon) :
\]
of order $M$ for any fixed regulator $\varepsilon$, with only logarithmic sensitivity to the horizon-crossing cutoff, the coefficient $2M$ of the logarithm being independent of the worldline's energy. The informal estimate ``$\Delta t \sim M$ up to a logarithm'' is exactly this statement, with the logarithm identified.
singularity.causal-epoch-computed-exactl.technical:
For the Schwarzschild field on flat spacetime, along the rain worldlines of the interior, radial free fall (velocity $\hb^{-1}(x')$ $D$-parallel) with unit energy at infinity, the worldlines of the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand frame, $|dt/dr| = \sqrt{r/2M}\;r/(2M - r)$ in static Killing time. The span of Killing time between crossing $r = 2M(1-\varepsilon)$ and reaching the singular locus $r = 0$ is computed in closed form, and expands as $\Delta t(\varepsilon) = 2M\bigl(\ln\tfrac{1}{\varepsilon} - \tfrac83 + 2\ln 2\bigr) + O(\varepsilon)$.

So the epoch is of order $M$ for any fixed regulator $\varepsilon$, with only logarithmic sensitivity to the horizon-crossing cutoff, and the coefficient $2M$ of the logarithm does not depend on the worldline's energy.
singularity.causal-epoch-computed-exactl.lay: An observer falling into a black hole from rest far away crosses the horizon and then reaches the singularity. This result computes exactly how much of the outside clock time that journey spans. The answer is about the black hole's mass in natural units, with a mild logarithmic dependence on exactly where the horizon crossing is taken to be.

proofs.main: Read in Gauge Theory Gravity, a geodesic of the static metric below is a worldline whose velocity $\hb^{-1}(x')$ is $D$-parallel (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}, clause (iii)). For a radial geodesic of the static metric with conserved energy $\mathcal{E} = f\,dt/d\lambda$ per unit mass, the normalisation gives $(dr/d\lambda)^{2} = \mathcal{E}^{2} - f$, so $dt/dr = \mathcal{E}/\bigl(f\sqrt{\mathcal{E}^{2} - f}\bigr)$; at $\mathcal{E} = 1$, $\sqrt{1 - f} = \sqrt{2M/r}$ and $|dt/dr| = \sqrt{r/2M}\,\bigl|r/(r - 2M)\bigr|$, which is the stated integrand for $r < 2M$. Substituting $r = 2Mu^{2}$ turns the integral into $4M\int_0^{\sqrt{1-\varepsilon}} u^{4}/(1 - u^{2})\,du$, and the integrand identity $u^{4}/(1 - u^{2}) = -u^{2} - 1 + 1/(1 - u^{2})$ gives the antiderivative $-u^{3}/3 - u + \tfrac12\ln\frac{1+u}{1-u}$, checked by differentiation; the closed form follows. For the expansion, $u = \sqrt{1 - \varepsilon} = 1 - \varepsilon/2 + O(\varepsilon^{2})$ gives $\tfrac12\ln\frac{1+u}{1-u} = \tfrac12\ln\frac{4}{\varepsilon} + O(\varepsilon) = \tfrac12\ln\tfrac1\varepsilon + \ln 2 + O(\varepsilon)$ and $u + u^{3}/3 = \tfrac43 + O(\varepsilon)$, so $\Delta t = 2M\ln\tfrac1\varepsilon + 4M(\ln 2 - \tfrac43) + O(\varepsilon)$. Near the horizon $dt/dr \approx 1/f$ for every $\mathcal{E}$, which is why the logarithm's coefficient is universal. Both the integrand identity and the substitution are verified exactly in the deposited script, as identities of rational functions, and the closed form is checked against the integral by exact rational Riemann bounds at the rational endpoint $\varepsilon = 1999 \cdot 10^{-6}$.

singularity.class-relative-no-go-no-supp.formal: Assume Fact \claimref{sheaf.function-linearity-tame-constructions}. Let the \emph{supplied class} consist of the second quantisations $d\Gamma(a)$ of the $C^\infty(E)$-linear endomorphisms $a$ of the mode line bundle (the line bundle over $E$ whose fibre at $x$ is the one-particle line of the mode there), together with the products of the parity sections $\sigma(x)$. Then no generator in the supplied class moves occupation from the ladder at one point of $E$ to the ladder at another: every one of them commutes with every $N_x$. Indeed the supplied class is \emph{ultralocal}: each of its generators is a sum of single-point terms, a multiplication operator in the joint number basis, and propagates nothing between points, so the theorem excludes hopping by generators that could not move anything in any case. Within the supplied class, the no-hopping half of Premise \claimref{singularity.l-boundary-mode-locality} is a theorem. The class does not contain, and the theorem does not exclude, pairing generators of the form $v^{*}_x v^{*}_y + v_y v_x$: these are $C^\infty$-linear in their coefficient functions, commute with the total parity $\Gamma$, are not joint-diagonal, and do not commute with $N_x$; their exclusion remains part of Premise \claimref{singularity.l-boundary-mode-locality}.
singularity.class-relative-no-go-no-supp.technical:
Assume function-linearity of the tame constructions, and let the supplied class consist of the second quantisations $d\Gamma(a)$ of the $C^\infty(E)$-linear endomorphisms $a$ of the mode line bundle, together with products of the parity sections $\sigma(x)$. Every generator in this class commutes with every $N_x$, so none moves occupation between points of $E$: the class is ultralocal, each generator a sum of single-point multiplication operators in the joint number basis.

Within this class the no-hopping half of the boundary-mode locality premise is therefore a theorem. Pairing generators $v^{*}_x v^{*}_y + v_y v_x$ lie outside the class: they commute with the total parity $\Gamma$ but not with $N_x$, and their exclusion remains part of the premise.
singularity.class-relative-no-go-no-supp.lay: The framework supplies only certain kinds of operators to drive the quantum modes at the singularity. Given that the series' tame constructions are function-linear (an imported fact), this result shows that none of those supplied operators can move a particle from one point to another, because each acts point by point. It does not rule out operators that create or destroy particles in pairs, so excluding those still has to be assumed.

The pairing clause is an exact matrix computation on two modes (the section “Machine verification”): $v^{*}_x v^{*}_y + v_y v_x$ commutes with $\Gamma = \sigma_x\sigma_y$, has off-diagonal entries in the joint number basis, and fails to commute with $N_x$; it is not of the form $d\Gamma(a)$ for a bundle map $a$, since it changes the total occupation by two.

singularity.deficit-carried-quanta-corre.formal:
Write $\rho_k$ for the single-mode marginals of $\rho$ and $C(\rho) := \sum_k S(\rho_k) - S(\rho)$ for the total correlation. If every $\rho_k$ is diagonal in its number basis (as Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-descent} guarantees for thermofield injections and Lemma \claimref{singularity.parity-protection} for the model), then the single-mode marginals of $\EN(\rho)$ equal those of $\rho$, and
\[
\rel{\rho}{\EN\rho} \;=\; C(\rho) - C(\EN\rho) :
\]
the deficit is the total correlation of the ascended state minus the classical, number-basis correlation that survives descent. No single-quantum quantity contributes anything: the cost of the descent consists entirely of inter-quanta correlations. In particular, for a globally pure $\rho$, $S(\rho) = 0$ and the deficit is the whole descended entropy, $\rel{\rho}{\EN\rho} = S(\EN\rho)$.
singularity.deficit-carried-quanta-corre.technical:
Let $\rho_k$ be the single-mode marginals of $\rho$ and $C(\rho) = \sum_k S(\rho_k) - S(\rho)$ its total correlation. If every $\rho_k$ is diagonal in its number basis, then $\EN$ leaves each single-mode marginal unchanged and the deficit of descent is $\rel{\rho}{\EN\rho} = C(\rho) - C(\EN\rho)$.

So the cost of descent consists entirely of correlations between quanta. For globally pure $\rho$ it is the whole descended entropy, $\rel{\rho}{\EN\rho} = S(\EN\rho)$.
singularity.deficit-carried-quanta-corre.lay: Descent replaces a quantum state by a version that keeps only its classical occupation records. When each individual mode already looks classical on its own, this result shows that everything lost in descent lies in the correlations between modes. No single mode on its own carries any of the loss.

singularity.deficit-theorem-cost-descent.formal:
Let $E$ be the pinching by any complete family of orthogonal projectors ($\EN$ included) and $\rho$ a density matrix. Then $E$ is idempotent, trace-preserving, and self-adjoint for the Hilbert-Schmidt pairing, and
\[
S\bigl(E(\rho)\bigr) - S(\rho) \;=\; \rel{\rho}{E(\rho)} \;\geq\; 0 ,
\]
with $S$ the von Neumann entropy and $D$ the relative entropy, and with equality if and only if $\rho = E(\rho)$. The level discrepancy of Step 6b is this quantity: not a slogan but a relative entropy, computed once and for all.
singularity.deficit-theorem-cost-descent.technical:
Let $E$ be the pinching by a complete family of orthogonal projectors, the multi-mode descent $\EN$ included. Then $E$ is idempotent, trace-preserving and self-adjoint for the Hilbert-Schmidt pairing, and for every density matrix $\rho$ the entropy increase under $E$ is exactly a relative entropy: $S(E(\rho)) - S(\rho) = \rel{\rho}{E(\rho)} \geq 0$, with equality if and only if $\rho = E(\rho)$.

The level discrepancy of the chain is this quantity, so the cost of descent is an exact relative entropy rather than a qualitative statement.
singularity.deficit-theorem-cost-descent.lay: Descent here means discarding the parts of a quantum state that link different sectors, keeping only the blocks along the diagonal. The theorem says the entropy gained by doing so equals a standard measure of how distinguishable the original state is from its descended version. The gain is never negative, and it is zero only when there was nothing to discard.
singularity.deficit-theorem-cost-descent.typing_note: Removed the mechanically added transport-algorithm edge: the theorem is a general identity for pinchings with no store premises; its only outside input is Klein's inequality, cited to the literature and not an imported claim in the store.

proofs.main:
Idempotency and trace preservation are the orthogonality and completeness of the $\Pi_\varepsilon$. Self-adjointness: $\tr(E(a)\,b) = \sum_\varepsilon \tr(\Pi_\varepsilon a \Pi_\varepsilon b) = \sum_\varepsilon \tr(a\, \Pi_\varepsilon b \Pi_\varepsilon) = \tr(a\,E(b))$ by cyclicity of the trace. The key step: $E(\rho)$ commutes with every $\Pi_\varepsilon$, hence so does every function of it, hence $E\bigl(\log E(\rho)\bigr) = \log E(\rho)$; self-adjointness with $b = \log E(\rho)$ then gives
\[
\tr\bigl(\rho \log E(\rho)\bigr) \;=\; \tr\bigl(E(\rho) \log E(\rho)\bigr) ,
\]
whence $\rel{\rho}{E\rho} = \tr\rho\log\rho - \tr\rho\log E\rho = -S(\rho) + S(E\rho)$. Nonnegativity and the equality case are Klein's inequality, the single classical input of the theorem \cite[\S 11.3]{NielsenChuang}. The script verifies the structural clauses on a generic rational matrix and the key identity, in moment form $\tr\bigl(\rho\,(E\rho)^m\bigr) = \tr\bigl(E\rho\,(E\rho)^m\bigr)$, on the model's scrambled two-pair state, in exact arithmetic.

singularity.envelope-endpoint-why-bounda.formal:
From (L), (U), (C), (I) and (L$_E$), with no typicality and no assumption about the placement of correlations:
\[
S_R(t) \;\leq\; \min\bigl(\Sth(t),\, C(t)\bigr) \qquad \text{and} \qquad S_R(\text{complete evaporation}) = 0 .
\]
The premise (L$_E$) cannot be dropped: a window unitary that is not number diagonal can leave the remaining window qubit far more mixed than its thermal marginal, and then $S_R$ exceeds $\Sth$. Two pairs with $(c, s) = (\tfrac{24}{25}, \tfrac{7}{25})$, the window rotation $|00\rangle \mapsto \tfrac35|00\rangle + \tfrac45|11\rangle$, $|11\rangle \mapsto -\tfrac45|00\rangle + \tfrac35|11\rangle$ on $(L_1, L_2)$, and then the eviction of $L_1$ leave $\rho_{L_2} = \operatorname{diag}(\tfrac{5968}{15625}, \tfrac{9657}{15625})$, so $S_R = S_L \approx 0.96$ bits against $\Sth = 2H(\tfrac{576}{625}) \approx 0.55$ nats, that is $0.79$ bits.
singularity.envelope-endpoint-why-bounda.technical:
From the rate-model inputs (L), (U), (C), (I) and boundary-mode locality (L$_E$), with no typicality and no assumption about where correlations sit, the radiation entropy obeys $S_R(t) \leq \min(\Sth(t), C(t))$ at every stage, and $S_R = 0$ at complete evaporation.

(L$_E$) cannot be dropped: in an explicit two-pair example a window unitary that is not number diagonal leaves the remaining window qubit more mixed than its thermal marginal, giving $S_R \approx 0.96$ bits against $\Sth \approx 0.79$ bits.
singularity.envelope-endpoint-why-bounda.lay: In the framework's model of black-hole evaporation, which assumes two sectors, overall purity, a window of the stated size and fresh thermal pairs injected at each step (the rate model's inputs (L), (U), (C), (I)), the entropy of the emitted radiation never exceeds either its thermal value or the black hole's remaining capacity, and it returns to zero once the hole has fully evaporated. This needs no assumption that the state is typical. It does need the assumption that the internal dynamics never shifts occupation numbers (boundary-mode locality, (L$_E$)): a small explicit example shows that without it the bound fails.

proofs.main: The bound and the endpoint are Theorem \claimref{singularity.eviction-window-thermal-product-radiation-entropy}(2). Every input other than (L$_E$) holds in the example. singularity.eviction-window-thermal-prod.technical:
Under the rate-model inputs (L), (U), (C), (I) and (L$_E$), with number-diagonal window dynamics, free radiation quanta that never return, and the no-attic property, let $W(t)$ be the set of pairs whose window half is still in the window and $C(t) = |W(t)|\ln 2$. Then the window state is the product of its members' thermal marginals, and $S_R(t) = S_L(t) = \sum_{k \in W(t)} h_k$ exactly.

Consequently $S_R \leq \min(\Sth, C)$ with $S_R = 0$ at complete evaporation; $S_R = \Sth$ exactly before any eviction; and $S_R = C - \sum_{k \in W(t)}(\ln 2 - h_k)$, with $S_R = C$ exactly when every window member is maximally entangled.

The tensor product of clause (1) is read on the modes as follows. The pairs are even states of fermionic modes, and for even states the tensor product of the marginals is the product, in the Clifford algebra of the modes, of commuting even elements: the window state is $\prod_{k \in W(t)}\tfrac12(1 + r_{k}p_{k})$, $p_{k}$ the parity of mode $k$ and $r_{k} = c_{k}^{2} - s_{k}^{2}$, with no twist, and the radiation has the same nonzero spectrum (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.mode-split-of-the-clifford-algebra-and-its-klein-twist-to-the-tensor-product}(iv), (v)). The four clauses hold unchanged in that reading.
singularity.eviction-window-thermal-prod.lay: In the framework's rate model, on its stated postulates (two sectors, global purity, a fixed window capacity, fresh thermal injection and boundary-mode locality), with internal dynamics that only changes phases and emitted quanta that never return, a black hole emits quanta that are each entangled with a partner mode kept inside, and partners are later pushed out as the hole shrinks. This result shows the inside state is always a simple product of thermal pieces, so the radiation's entropy is just the sum of the entropies of the partners still inside. That gives a rising branch, a ceiling set by the shrinking capacity, and zero entropy at the end.

proofs.main:
By (L) and (U) of \claimref{singularity.rate-models-kinematic-inputs-l-u} the global state is pure on $H_{L(t)} \otimes H_{R(t)}$ at every stage, so $S_R = S_L$ (equal marginal spectra of a pure state), and by (C) $\dim H_{L(t)} = 2^{|W(t)|}$, so $S_L \leq C(t)$ is the dimension bound.

For (1), consider the joint number basis of all the qubits ever injected, labelled $R_k, L_k$. By (I) the state at injection of pair $k$ is the previous state tensored with $c_k|0_{R_k}0_{L_k}\rangle + s_k|1_{R_k}1_{L_k}\rangle$, so its support lies in the configurations with $R_k = L_k$ for every injected $k$ and its amplitude on such a configuration is $\pm\prod_k c^{(k)}_{b_k}$, with $c^{(k)}_0 = c_k$, $c^{(k)}_1 = s_k$. By (L$_E$, \claimref{singularity.l-boundary-mode-locality}) every subsequent operation is either a diagonal unitary on the window, which multiplies each configuration by a phase and preserves both the support and every squared amplitude, or an eviction, which relabels a qubit from $L$ to $R$ and touches no amplitude (no attic, by \claimref{singularity.no-attic-derived-model}); the radiation quanta are free. So at every stage the support constraint $R_k = L_k$ holds and the squared amplitude of each configuration is $\prod_k (c^{(k)}_{b_k})^{2}$. Now trace out the radiation. Every $R_k$ is in the radiation (the emitted quanta never return), so two configurations that agree on the radiation agree on every $L_k$ with $k \in W(t)$ by the support constraint: $\rho_L$ has no off-diagonal entries. Its diagonal entry at the window configuration $(b_k)_{k \in W(t)}$ is the total probability of the global configurations extending it, which is $\prod_{k \in W(t)}(c^{(k)}_{b_k})^{2}$ times the sum over the other pairs' configurations, and that sum is $1$. This is the product state displayed, and its entropy is $\sum_{k \in W(t)} H(c_k^{2}) = \sum_{k \in W(t)} h_k$.

(2) $W(t)$ is a subset of the injected pairs and every $h_k \geq 0$, so $\sum_{W(t)} h_k \leq \sum_{k \leq t} h_k = \Sth(t)$; and $\sum_{W(t)} h_k \leq |W(t)|\ln 2 = C(t)$ since each $h_k \leq \ln 2$. At complete evaporation $W = \varnothing$ and the sum is empty. (3) is (1) with $W(t)$ the full set of injected pairs. (4) is (1) rewritten as $|W|\ln 2 - \sum_{W}(\ln 2 - h_k)$, with equality in $S_R \leq C$ exactly when every term of the shortfall vanishes; in the idealisation the shortfall is identically zero, so $S_R = C$ whenever an eviction has occurred and $S_R = \Sth$ before, which is $\min(\Sth, C)$ in both regimes. The script verifies (1) on the thermal model at every stage, from the exact spectrum of $\rho_L$, as an identity of formal logarithms; the strict inequality of (4) at every stage with a nonempty window, by rigorous rational bounds; and (4)'s exact saturation on an idealised run simulated on exact density matrices along a decreasing capacity schedule.

singularity.function-linear-endomorphism.formal: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the sheaf of sections of a vector bundle over $E$ and $D$ a $C^\infty(E)$-linear endomorphism of $\mathcal{F}(E)$. Then $D$ is tensorial: $(Ds)(x)$ depends only on $s(x)$, so $D$ is a bundle map $\{a_x\}$; for a line bundle, multiplication by a function.
singularity.function-linear-endomorphism.technical:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the sheaf of sections of a vector bundle over $E$ and $D$ a $C^\infty(E)$-linear endomorphism of $\mathcal{F}(E)$. Then $D$ is tensorial: $(Ds)(x)$ depends only on $s(x)$, so $D$ is a bundle map $\{a_x\}$, and on a line bundle it is multiplication by a function.

The proof uses a local frame and a bump function to show that $(Ds)(x) = 0$ whenever $s(x) = 0$.
singularity.function-linear-endomorphism.lay: If an operation on fields commutes with multiplication by ordinary functions, it cannot look at neighbouring points: its output at a point depends only on the field's value there. In the simplest case, a field with one component at each point, such an operation is just multiplication by a fixed function.
singularity.function-linear-endomorphism.typing_note: No store premises; a self-contained bump-function argument.

proofs.main: If $s(x) = 0$, take a local frame $(t_i)$ near $x$ and a bump $\chi$ equal to $1$ near $x$ and supported in the frame's domain; then $\chi^2 s = \sum_i f_i\, \chi t_i$ with $f_i := \chi \cdot (\text{coefficient of } s \text{ on } t_i)$ global and $f_i(x) = 0$, while $(1 - \chi^2)s$ is $(1 - \chi^2)$ times $s$. Linearity gives $(Ds)(x) = \sum_i f_i(x)\,(D\chi t_i)(x) + (1 - \chi^2)(x)\,(Ds)(x) = 0$. So $(Ds)(x)$ is determined by $s(x)$, and $a_x$ is the induced fibre map.

singularity.imported-induced-geometry-in.formal: Inside the horizon, for the Schwarzschild field in the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand gauge field $\hb = 1 - \beta P$, $\beta = \sqrt{2M/r}$, of Fact \claimref{sheaf.gauge-field-cometric}, the background surface $r = r_c$ ($0 < r_c < 2M$) is spacelike: its tangent vectors $e_t$, $e_\theta$, $e_\phi$ have physical squares $Q(\hb^{-1}(e_t)) = 1 - 2M/r_c < 0$ and $-r_c^{2}$, $-r_c^{2}\sin^{2}\theta$ in the coordinate normalisation, so its induced metric is $ds_3^{2} = |f(r_c)|\,dt^{2} + r_c^{2}\,d\Omega^{2}$ with $|f(r_c)| = 2M/r_c - 1$: Killing time $t$ is a spatial coordinate along it. On a surface of constant $r$ the static time and the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand time differ by a function of $r$ alone, so this is also the induced metric read in the static chart. \emph{Provenance:} this is read off the static form of the metric, the section “The metric of the gauge field, and its static form”, with $f < 0$ for $r < 2M$.
singularity.imported-induced-geometry-in.technical:
Inside the horizon, for $0 < r_c < 2M$, the background surface $r = r_c$ of the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand gauge field is spacelike: the physical square of its time direction, $Q(\hb^{-1}(e_t)) = 1 - 2M/r_c$, is negative. Its induced metric is $ds_3^{2} = |f(r_c)|\,dt^{2} + r_c^{2}\,d\Omega^{2}$ with $|f(r_c)| = 2M/r_c - 1$, the same in the static chart since the two times differ by a function of $r$ on the slice.

Killing time $t$ is therefore a spatial coordinate along the slice. The result is read off the static form of the Schwarzschild metric, using $f < 0$ for $r < 2M$.
singularity.imported-induced-geometry-in.lay: Inside a black hole the roles of space and time swap, so a surface at fixed radius is a slice of space rather than a moment of time. Described by the gravitational field on flat spacetime, the background direction of outside clock time has become spacelike there, stretched by a factor that depends on the radius. This is read directly from the standard form of the black-hole field.

singularity.imported-page-average-entrop.formal:
Let $\mathcal{H} = \mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$ with $\dim\mathcal{H}_A = m \leq n = \dim\mathcal{H}_B$, and let $\psi$ be a pure state drawn from the unitarily invariant measure on the unit sphere of $\mathcal{H}$. The average entanglement entropy of the subsystem $A$ is
\[
\langle S_A \rangle \;=\; \sum_{k=n+1}^{mn} \frac{1}{k} \;-\; \frac{m-1}{2n} \;\simeq\; \ln m - \frac{m}{2n} \qquad (1 \ll m \leq n),
\]
so a typical pure state's smaller marginal is within $m/2n \leq 1/2$ nat of the maximum $\ln m$. Page conjectured the formula \cite{Page1993}; it was proved by Foong and Kanno, by Sanchez-Ruiz, and by Sen.
singularity.imported-page-average-entrop.technical: For a pure state of a bipartite system of dimensions $m \leq n$, chosen at random with respect to the unitarily invariant measure, the average entropy of the smaller subsystem is $\sum_{k=n+1}^{mn} 1/k - (m-1)/2n$, which for large $m$ is $\ln m - m/2n$. A typical state therefore nearly saturates the bound $\ln m$ on the smaller side's entropy, missing it by at most half a nat. The series uses it for saturation in the assembled Page curve.
singularity.imported-page-average-entrop.lay: If a large quantum system in a pure state is split into two parts, and the state is picked at random, the smaller part is almost always as mixed as it can possibly be: its entropy falls short of the maximum by at most half a unit. Don Page worked out the average in 1993, and others proved his formula soon after. The series uses this to say that the entropy of a black hole's radiation reaches the largest value its counting allows.

imported_from.citation: D. N. Page, Average entropy of a subsystem, Phys. Rev. Lett. 71 (1993), 1291--1294.
S. K. Foong and S. Kanno, Proof of Page's conjecture on the average entropy of a subsystem, Phys. Rev. Lett. 72 (1994), 1148--1151.
J. Sanchez-Ruiz, Simple proof of Page's conjecture on the average entropy of a subsystem, Phys. Rev. E 52 (1995), 5653--5655.
S. Sen, Average entropy of a quantum subsystem, Phys. Rev. Lett. 77 (1996), 1--3.

singularity.l-boundary-mode-locality.formal:
\emph{Premise (L$_{E}$), boundary-mode locality.} On every finite window of the boundary modes, $v_{1}, \dots, v_{n}$ satisfying the CAR, the internal dynamics $\alpha_{t}$ of the boundary modes commutes with the descent at all times:
\[
\alpha_{t}\circ\mathcal{E} \;=\; \mathcal{E}\circ\alpha_{t} \quad \text{for all } t, \qquad \mathcal{E} = E_{1}\circ\cdots\circ E_{n}, \quad E_{k}(x) = N_{k}xN_{k} + (1 - N_{k})x(1 - N_{k}),
\]
$\mathcal{E}$ the descent of the window (Proposition \claimref{singularity.descent-what-it-erases}).

\emph{The version 1 wording, equivalent.} By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boundary-mode-locality-is-descent-covariance}, on every finite window this holds if and only if the dynamics is generated by elements of the abelian algebra $\mathcal{D}$ that the $\sigma_{k} = 2N_{k} - 1$ generate, diagonal in the joint number basis: the internal dynamics is generated by the geometric data the framework supplies on $E$, the boost bivector field $x \mapsto \sigma_{r}(x)$ and its products. Cross-point products such as $\sigma_{j}\sigma_{k}$ correlate phases without moving occupation; hopping $v_{j}^{*}v_{k} + v_{k}^{*}v_{j}$, pairing $v_{j}^{*}v_{k}^{*} + v_{k}v_{j}$ and every other generator with a component outside $\mathcal{D}$ are excluded by the one clause. Within the class of generators the framework supplies, the exclusion of hopping is a theorem (Theorem \claimref{singularity.class-relative-no-go-no-supplied}); what the premise adds is the exclusion of unsupplied generators, pairing terms and the possible differential dynamics, which Proposition \claimref{singularity.l-stabiliser-tangent} places in the tangent of the vacuum orbit and in its stabiliser.

\emph{What it forbids.} By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.number-diagonal-dynamics-spreads-nothing}, every dynamics the premise admits carries an evolved mode operator only to the modes directly coupled to it, and every local commutator and out-of-time-order correlator is almost periodic and bounded: the premise forbids exponential real-time commutator growth. The real-time spreading law $t_{*} = \kappa^{-1}\ln N$ of Proposition \claimref{scrambling.spreading-law-chaos-bound-saturated} is therefore not realised under it, and the scrambling time is a modular-time statement: the growth $e^{\kappa t}$ is a rate of the rotor flow, the KMS-strip continuation of the phase flow that is the windows' time evolution (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.phase-flow-is-time-rotor-flow-kms-continuation}). The premise is kept over fast real-time scrambling; the two cannot both hold.
singularity.l-boundary-mode-locality.technical:
Postulate: on every finite window of boundary modes, the internal dynamics commutes with the descent at all times. This is equivalent to the original wording, that the dynamics is generated by the geometric data on $E$, the boost bivector field and its products, all diagonal in the joint number basis, so that cross-point products correlate phases while hopping, pairing and any unsupplied generator are excluded by a single clause. Within the class of generators the framework supplies, the exclusion of hopping is a theorem; what the premise adds is the exclusion of unsupplied generators.

The premise has a cost: under it no operator spreads beyond the modes it is directly coupled to and nothing grows exponentially in real time, so the scrambling law $t_{*} = \kappa^{-1}\ln N$ has no real-time reading. The scrambling time survives as a statement in modular time, the imaginary-time continuation of the windows' evolution. The series keeps the premise and gives up fast real-time scrambling.
singularity.l-boundary-mode-locality.lay: This assumption says that the quantum modes at a black hole's singularity evolve in a way that never disturbs what a measurement of their occupations would find: they change phases and build correlations, but never move particles between points or create them in pairs. Part of this is proved for the operators the framework supplies; ruling out any other operators is assumed. The assumption has a price: under it, information placed in one mode does not spread rapidly through the others in real time, so the fast scrambling often attributed to black holes holds here only as a statement about the modes' thermal clock, not about their actual evolution.

singularity.l-stabiliser-tangent.lay: The operators acting quadratically on two or more fermionic modes come in two kinds: those that move a particle between modes and those that create or destroy particles in pairs. On the empty state the first kind leaves its direction unchanged, as does pair destruction, while pair creation genuinely changes it. So the only part of the locality assumption that does real work starting from the empty state is the ban on pair creation.

singularity.models-entropy-sequence-exac.formal:
In the run of the table accompanying \claimref{singularity.purity-correlation-transfer-recovery}, Theorem \claimref{singularity.eviction-window-thermal-product-radiation-entropy}(1) reads as follows: at every stage the window state $\rho_L$ is diagonal in the number basis, with the product distribution of its current members, so that, with $W(t)$ the set of pairs whose window half is still in the window,
\[
S_R(t) \;=\; S_L(t) \;=\; \sum_{k \in W(t)} H(c_k^{2}) \qquad \text{exactly, and} \qquad \tr\rho_R(t)^{2} \;=\; \prod_{k \in W(t)}\bigl(c_k^{4} + s_k^{4}\bigr) .
\]
Consequently $S_R = \Sth$ exactly through Phase I; in Phase II, $S_R \leq C$ with equality if and only if every window member is maximally entangled, so that with the model's pairs the inequality is strict at every Phase II stage with a nonempty window; and $S_R = 0$ at completion. The model therefore realises the envelope, the exact rising branch and the endpoint of Theorem \claimref{singularity.eviction-window-thermal-product-radiation-entropy}, and exhibits the falling branch's departure from exact saturation, not its saturation.
singularity.models-entropy-sequence-exac.technical:
In the finite model's run, at every stage the window state $\rho_L$ is diagonal in the number basis with the product distribution of its current members. Hence $S_R(t) = S_L(t) = \sum_{k \in W(t)} H(c_k^2)$ and $\tr\rho_R(t)^2 = \prod_{k \in W(t)}(c_k^4 + s_k^4)$ exactly.

So $S_R = \Sth$ exactly through the first phase; in the second phase $S_R \leq C$, strictly at every stage with a nonempty window since the model's pairs are not maximally entangled; and $S_R = 0$ at completion.
singularity.models-entropy-sequence-exac.lay: In the explicit small model of evaporation, the entropy of the radiation can be computed exactly at every step. It equals the thermal value while the window fills, stays strictly below the capacity as the hole shrinks, and returns to zero at the end. The model thus shows the general bounds at work, but not the idealised case in which the capacity is reached exactly.
singularity.models-entropy-sequence-exac.typing_note: Kept parity protection (the support constraint drives the proof); the eviction theorem is specialised in the statement but the proof recomputes it in the model, so it was not added.

proofs.main: The radiation contains $R_k$ for every injected pair $k$, and the window contains $L_k$ for $k \in W(t)$ only. By the support constraint $R_k = L_k$ (Lemma \claimref{singularity.parity-protection}), two global configurations that agree on every radiation qubit agree on every window qubit, so tracing out the radiation leaves no off-diagonal entries: $\rho_L$ is diagonal, with entries the probabilities of the window configurations. A window configuration is a choice of $b_k \in \{0, 1\}$ for $k \in W(t)$, and its probability is $\prod_{k \in W(t)}(c^{(k)}_{b_k})^{2}$ times the sum over the remaining pairs' configurations, which is $1$; the controlled-$Z$ phases square away. So the distribution is the product of the members' thermal distributions, its Shannon entropy is $\sum_{k \in W(t)}H(c_k^{2})$, its collision probability is $\prod_{k \in W(t)}(c_k^{4} + s_k^{4})$, and $S_R = S_L$, $\tr\rho_R^{2} = \tr\rho_L^{2}$ by purity of the global state. The Phase I identity is the first two rows of the table; $C = |W(t)|\ln 2$ and $H(c_k^{2}) \leq \ln 2$ with equality only at $c_k = s_k$ give the Phase II clause; and $W = \varnothing$ at completion gives $0$. The script computes the exact spectrum of $\rho_L$ at every stage, verifies the entropy identity as an identity of formal logarithms, and decides the strict inequalities by exact rational bounds on the logarithms of the primes involved.

singularity.no-attic-derived-model.formal: Under (L), (U) and (C): modes exiting the window carry no q-number content out of the two-sector decomposition; their correlations are placed, at eviction, in $L(t) \cup R(t)$. The no-attic axiom (A) is a theorem of the model's kinematics.
singularity.no-attic-derived-model.technical:
Under the rate-model inputs (L), (U) and (C), the state space at each stage is exactly $H_{L(t)} \otimes H_{R(t)}$, with no third tensor factor; an eviction transfers one mode's factor from $L$ to $R$, and a unitary step preserves all correlations. Hence modes leaving the window carry no q-number content out of the two-sector decomposition: their correlations remain in $L(t) \cup R(t)$.

The no-attic axiom is thus a theorem of the model's kinematics. Whether the two sectors exhaust real evaporation is not established here and stays inside premise (L).
singularity.no-attic-derived-model.lay: An attic would be a hidden third place, besides the black hole's interior modes and its radiation, where information could end up. In the framework's model, granting its rate-model inputs (L), (U) and (C), the bookkeeping has only those two places, so information leaving the interior must go into the radiation. Whether real black holes have no such third place is still an assumption, now stated openly.
singularity.no-attic-derived-model.typing_note: The proof runs on (L), (U) and (C) alone, so the rate-model postulate was added; the tower and one-sided-completion citations bear on what the proof does not establish (exhaustiveness of the two sectors) and were removed with the transport-algorithm repair edge, the one-sided completion being the removal I am least sure of. proofs.main: By (L) of \claimref{singularity.rate-models-kinematic-inputs-l-u} the state space at every stage is $H_{L(t)} \otimes H_{R(t)}$, with the exact dimensions of (C): there is no third tensor factor. An eviction is the transfer of one mode's factor from the $L$ side of the decomposition to the $R$ side (in physical terms, the mode leaves the shrinking boundary mode space and its content is carried with it into the radiation sector; in the finite-mode model of the section “The finite-mode model: the dissolution step by step” this is implemented literally). A unitary step (U) preserves the global state, hence all its correlations; since the factor carrying them lands in $R$, the correlations of the evicted mode remain in $L \cup R$, which is the assertion. What this proof does \emph{not} establish, and what carries the physical content, is the exhaustiveness of (L)'s two sectors for real evaporation: that no remnant or third sector exists dynamically. That claim is exactly the closure-completeness programme, argued from the tower's floor-one completeness \cite[Cor.~6.2]{ButlerT3} and flagged as the conjectural step; here it lies inside (L), where it is visible, rather than inside an unexamined axiom. One candidate third sector is excluded by theorem rather than by hypothesis: the completion at the black hole forms no shadow wall anywhere in the physical closure, the conserved quantity exiting the manifold through the blown-up boundary \cite[Thm.~8.12, Rem.~8.13]{ButlerT4}, so no degeneracy-generated sector hides inside the two-sector decomposition. The dynamical no-remnant clause of (L) remains the programme's.

singularity.number-diagonal-dynamics-mod.formal: Under (L$_E$) every generator available to the internal dynamics of the boundary modes lies in the abelian algebra generated by $\{\sigma_k\}$, hence is diagonal in the joint number basis and its exponential is a diagonal unitary. Consequently each mode's occupation probabilities are constants of the motion of the boundary modes, so populations set at injection by the local geometry do not drift; and the diagonal scrambling of the finite-mode model, the controlled-$Z$ circuit of the section “The model”, is not a modelling convenience but the general form of what (L$_E$) permits.
singularity.number-diagonal-dynamics-mod.technical:
Under (L$_E$), every generator of the boundary-mode dynamics lies in the abelian algebra generated by the $\sigma_k = 2N_k - 1$, so it is diagonal in the joint number basis and its exponential is a diagonal unitary. Diagonal unitaries change only phases, so every mode's occupation probabilities are constants of the motion, and since the ascended marginals are diagonal each marginal $\varrho_k$ is constant in time.

The model's controlled-$Z$ scrambling is therefore not a modelling convenience but the general form of what (L$_E$) permits.
singularity.number-diagonal-dynamics-mod.lay: Under the locality premise (L$_E$), every internal motion of the boundary modes only changes phases, so the probability that each mode is occupied never changes, so the populations set when the modes are created stay fixed. The simple phase-gate scrambling used in the toy model turns out to be the general form of the dynamics the locality assumption allows.

With Theorem \claimref{singularity.ascended-marginals-are-diagonal} fixing the off-diagonal entries at zero, each $\varrho_k$ is constant in time. The script verifies the invariance for a controlled-$Z$ circuit on the model's mode space and exhibits an orthogonal, parity-preserving hopping rotation that does change the marginal populations, which is exactly the generator (L$_E$, \claimref{singularity.l-boundary-mode-locality}) excludes.

singularity.parity-protection.formal: At every stage of the model, and for \emph{any} sequence of number-basis-diagonal window unitaries, the reduced density matrix of each individual qubit, radiation or window, early or evicted, is exactly its thermal matrix $\operatorname{diag}(c_k^2, s_k^2)$: diagonal, with the original populations, regardless of the scrambling.
singularity.parity-protection.technical:
In the model, for any sequence of number-basis-diagonal window unitaries, the reduced density matrix of every individual qubit, radiation or window, early or evicted, is exactly its thermal matrix $\operatorname{diag}(c_k^2, s_k^2)$.

The reason is a support constraint: each pair contributes only $|00\rangle$ and $|11\rangle$ components, diagonal unitaries preserve that constraint and every squared amplitude, so single-qubit coherences vanish and populations never change.
singularity.parity-protection.lay: In the toy model, every individual quantum, whether in the radiation or still inside, looks exactly thermal on its own, however the inside is scrambled by phase gates. Any information is therefore invisible to measurements of one quantum at a time. It can only show up in correlations among several quanta.
singularity.parity-protection.typing_note: No store premises; a direct support-constraint argument on the model.

proofs.main: The initial global state is supported on computational configurations satisfying $R_k = L_k$ for every $k$ (each pair contributes $|00\rangle$ or $|11\rangle$). A diagonal unitary maps each configuration to itself times a phase: the support constraint is preserved forever, and so is each configuration's squared amplitude. Off-diagonals: the coherence $\langle 0|\rho_{R_k}|1\rangle$ is a sum over pairs of global configurations that differ in the bit $R_k$ and agree everywhere else; but agreement at $L_k$ contradicts the support constraint for one of the two, so the sum is empty and the coherence is exactly zero. (For $L_k$, exchange the roles.) Diagonals: the populations are sums of squared amplitudes, unchanged by diagonal unitaries; they equal $c_k^2$ and $s_k^2$ from the start. Eviction relabels a qubit from $L$ to $R$ and changes no amplitudes.

singularity.purity-correlation-transfer-.technical:
In the model with two pairs and one controlled-$Z$ between $L_1$ and $L_2$, the global state is pure at every stage and at completion $S(R_{\mathrm{all}}) = 0$. The gate damps the coherence of the pair $(R_1, L_1)$ by the visibility $\gamma = c_2^2 - s_2^2$, so its Rényi-2 purity drops from $1$ to $c_1^4 + s_1^4 + 2c_1^2 s_1^2\gamma^2$.

The deficit is relocated, not lost: $\langle X_{R_1}X_{L_1}\rangle = 2c_1 s_1\gamma$ while the dressed correlator gives $\langle X_{R_1}X_{L_1}Z_{L_2}\rangle = 2c_1 s_1$, so the gate pattern is read from multi-qubit correlators although every single qubit is thermal.
singularity.purity-correlation-transfer-.lay: In the smallest scrambled version of the model, the radiation ends up in a pure state, so nothing is lost. Scrambling weakens the correlation within an emitted pair, but the missing correlation reappears in a three-quantum correlation. Measuring those correlations reveals which scrambling was applied, even though each quantum on its own looks thermal.

proofs.main:
(1) Unitarity and relabelling. (2) Write the four-qubit state $\sum_{b_1 b_2} c^{(1)}_{b_1} c^{(2)}_{b_2} (-1)^{b_1 b_2} |b_1 b_1 b_2 b_2\rangle$ with $c^{(k)}_0 = c_k$, $c^{(k)}_1 = s_k$. Tracing out $(R_2, L_2)$: the coherence of $(R_1, L_1)$ between $|00\rangle$ and $|11\rangle$ picks up $\sum_{b_2} |c^{(2)}_{b_2}|^2 (-1)^{b_2} = c_2^2 - s_2^2 = \gamma$; the populations are untouched. The stated purity is $\tr \rho^2$ for the two-by-two supported block $\begin{psmallmatrix} c_1^2 & c_1 s_1 \gamma \\ c_1 s_1 \gamma & s_1^2 \end{psmallmatrix}$. (3) The computations are short enough to print. Write the scrambled state as $|\Psi\rangle = \sum_{b_1, b_2} c^{(1)}_{b_1} c^{(2)}_{b_2} (-1)^{b_1 b_2} |b_1 b_1 b_2 b_2\rangle$ in the order $(R_1, L_1, R_2, L_2)$. The operator $X_{R_1}X_{L_1}$ flips both bits of the first pair, so
\[
\langle X_{R_1}X_{L_1}\rangle
= \sum_{b_1, b_2} c^{(1)}_{b_1} c^{(1)}_{\bar b_1}\, \bigl(c^{(2)}_{b_2}\bigr)^2\, (-1)^{b_1 b_2}(-1)^{\bar b_1 b_2}
= 2 c_1 s_1 \sum_{b_2} \bigl(c^{(2)}_{b_2}\bigr)^2 (-1)^{b_2}
= 2 c_1 s_1 \bigl(c_2^2 - s_2^2\bigr) = 2 c_1 s_1 \gamma ,
\]
using $(-1)^{b_1 b_2}(-1)^{\bar b_1 b_2} = (-1)^{b_2}$ since $b_1 + \bar b_1 = 1$. Dressing with $Z_{L_2}$ inserts one more $(-1)^{b_2}$, which cancels the previous one:
\[
\langle X_{R_1}X_{L_1} Z_{L_2}\rangle
= 2 c_1 s_1 \sum_{b_2} \bigl(c^{(2)}_{b_2}\bigr)^2 (-1)^{b_2}(-1)^{b_2}
= 2 c_1 s_1 .
\]
For the unscrambled state the phases are absent and the same two sums give $2 c_1 s_1$ and $2 c_1 s_1 \gamma$ respectively: the pair of correlators $(\langle XX\rangle, \langle XXZ\rangle)$ takes the value $(2c_1s_1,\, 2c_1s_1\gamma)$ without the gate and $(2c_1s_1\gamma,\, 2c_1s_1)$ with it, so the gate pattern is read off from three-qubit correlations, while Lemma \claimref{singularity.parity-protection} fixes every single-qubit marginal at the identical thermal matrix in both histories. With the script's numbers ($c_1, s_1 = \tfrac45, \tfrac35$; $c_2, s_2 = \tfrac45, \tfrac35$; $\gamma = \tfrac{7}{25}$) the two signatures are $(\tfrac{24}{25}, \tfrac{168}{625})$ and $(\tfrac{168}{625}, \tfrac{24}{25})$, confirmed exactly.

singularity.rate-models-kinematic-inputs.formal:
\leavevmode
\begin{itemize}
\item[(L)] \emph{Localisation, derived in part.} By \cite[Thm.~4.4, Cor.~4.5, Thms 8.7, 8.12]{ButlerT4} and Step 4a, the completion installs q-number degrees of freedom exactly where division fails, which licenses the window mode space $L(t)$ inside the closure of the degenerate locus; the radiation $R(t)$ is a q-number sector on the model's own grounds, its quanta being the emitted modes carried off $E$ by the emission rather than outputs of the localisation theorems; and that these two exhaust the sectors is the model's exhaustiveness postulate. The total state space at each stage is $H_{L(t)} \otimes H_{R(t)}$.
\item[(U)] \emph{Purity.} The ascended description is globally pure, as in Fact \claimref{singularity.assembled-page-curve-up-typicality}(i), each step of the evolution unitary.
\item[(C)] \emph{Capacity.} $\dim H_{L(t)} = 2^{|W(t)|}$ exactly, the number $|W(t)|$ of window modes filling to the mode count $N_{\mathrm{6a}}$ of Step 6a and non-increasing thereafter; the Page reading $C(t) \approx S_{\mathrm{BH}}(M(t))$ is for the full window.
\item[(I)] \emph{Injection.} The $k$-th emitted quantum enters in a thermofield pair $c_k|00\rangle + s_k|11\rangle$ with a fresh window mode, the pair form and the marginals from Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-descent} and Corollary \claimref{singularity.chains-state-class-stability}; its \emph{freshness}, the clause that the pair arrives uncorrelated with everything already present, comes from neither cited result (Corollary \claimref{singularity.chains-state-class-stability}(3) leaves exactly such correlations free) and is an independent assumption of the rate model, marked as such precisely as (L$_E$)'s never-return clause is. The quantum carries the marginal entropy $h_k := H(c_k^{2}) \leq \ln 2$, with $H(p) := -p\ln p - (1-p)\ln(1-p)$ the binary entropy in nats and equality exactly at the maximally entangled pair $c_k = s_k$; the thermal accumulation is $\Sth(t) := \sum_{k \leq t} h_k$.
\end{itemize}
singularity.rate-models-kinematic-inputs.technical:
Postulates of the rate model. (L): the state space at each stage is $H_{L(t)} \otimes H_{R(t)}$, a window mode space inside the closure of the degenerate locus and a radiation sector, the exhaustiveness of these two sectors being postulated. (U): the ascended description is globally pure and each step is unitary. (C): $\dim H_{L(t)} = 2^{|W(t)|}$ exactly, filling to the mode count $N_{\mathrm{6a}}$ and non-increasing afterwards.

(I): the $k$-th emitted quantum enters in a thermofield pair $c_k|00\rangle + s_k|11\rangle$ with a fresh window mode, uncorrelated with everything present, freshness being an independent assumption. It carries $h_k = H(c_k^2) \leq \ln 2$, and the thermal accumulation is $\Sth(t) = \sum_{k \leq t} h_k$.
singularity.rate-models-kinematic-inputs.lay: These are the basic assumptions of the framework's simple model of black-hole evaporation. Everything lives in two places, the black hole's interior modes and the radiation; the total state stays pure; the interior has a definite capacity that only shrinks once full; and each emitted quantum arrives entangled with a fresh partner inside. The freshness of each partner is assumed rather than derived.

singularity.stretched-singularity-count.formal:
Assume (C1) and (C2). For the Schwarzschild field in the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand gauge field $\hb = 1 - \beta P$, $\beta = \sqrt{2M/r}$, of Fact \claimref{sheaf.gauge-field-cometric}, the three-volume of the background slice $r = r_c$ per unit Killing time, from the metric induced by $\hb^{-1}$ (Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-induced-geometry-interior-slice}), is
\[
4\pi\,r_c^{2}\sqrt{|f(r_c)|} \;=\; 4\pi\sqrt{2M}\,r_c^{3/2}\sqrt{1 - \tfrac{r_c}{2M}} \;=\; 8\pi M\sqrt{1 - \tfrac{r_c}{2M}} \;=\; 8\pi M\,\bigl(1 + O(M^{-2/3})\bigr) ,
\]
using $r_c^{3} = 2M$: the cutoff radius conspires with the anisotropic stretch to leave \emph{linear} mass dependence at leading order, special to this cutoff (a mass-independent cutoff radius gives $M^{1/2}$ and can never reach the area law). With $\nu$ fermionic modes per Planck cell, and writing $N_{\mathrm{6a}}$ for the number of boundary modes (the notation Steps 6b and Fact \claimref{singularity.assembled-page-curve-up-typicality} use for this section's count),
\[
\frac{dN_{\mathrm{6a}}}{dt} \;=\; 8\pi\nu M\sqrt{1 - \tfrac{r_c}{2M}} \;=\; \frac{\nu}{\TH}\sqrt{1 - \tfrac{r_c}{2M}} :
\]
the stretched singularity registers $\nu$ modes per Hawking period up to the correction factor $\sqrt{1 - r_c/2M}$, which tends to $1$ as $M \to \infty$ in Planck units ($r_c/2M = (2M)^{-2/3}$). It keeps time with the horizon's own clock.

\emph{Scope (Schwarzschild).} The equality of the forms $8\pi\nu M$ and $\nu/\TH$ of the rate, and with it the wording that the stretched singularity keeps time with the horizon's own clock, is a Schwarzschild coincidence. Carried to the Kerr field with the epoch $2\pi/\kappa_{+}$ and $\nu = 1/16\pi$, the three forms of the rate that agree on Schwarzschild, $8\pi\nu M$, $\nu/\TH$ and $2\nu\kappa A$, give counts $M/s$, $Mr_{+}/(2s^{2})$ and $1$ times $A_{+}/4$, $s = \sqrt{M^{2} - a^{2}}$, and the third agrees only because it is the rate of that result's horizon hypothesis itself (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.stretched-horizon-count-on-kerr-is-a-multiple-of-the-area-by-construction}, clause (v)). So on Kerr the three forms differ, and the Schwarzschild count does not fix which of them is carried.

proofs.main:
Read in Gauge Theory Gravity: the metric below is the derived metric of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), and the manifold is its invertible region.

By Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-induced-geometry-interior-slice} the volume element of the slice is $\sqrt{|f(r_c)|}\,r_c^{2}\sin\theta\,dt\,d\theta\,d\varphi$, and integrating over the sphere gives $4\pi r_c^{2}\sqrt{2M/r_c - 1} = 4\pi r_c^{2}\sqrt{2M/r_c}\,\sqrt{1 - r_c/2M}$. With (C1, \claimref{singularity.c1-curvature-cutoff}), $r_c^{3} = 2M$, so $r_c^{2}\sqrt{2M/r_c} = \sqrt{2M}\,r_c^{3/2} = \sqrt{2M}\sqrt{2M} = 2M$, which is the first display. Multiplying by $\nu$ per Planck cell (C2, \claimref{singularity.c2-cell-density}) gives the second, and $8\pi M = 1/\TH$ is Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-descent}. The script verifies the slice-volume identity along the whole (C1) locus, parametrised by rational $r_c$ with $2M := r_c^{3}$, as an identity of rational functions in $r_c$, together with the rate identity with $\pi$ cancelled; a mass-independent cutoff radius is run as a control and fails the linear-in-$M$ form, the $M^{1/2}$ scaling that can never reach the area law.

singularity.two-levels-finite-model.formal:
In the full model run of the section “The model, run exactly” ($n = 4$ pairs, $N_{\max} = 2$), write $\rho_R$ for the state of the complete radiation at evaporation's end (all eight qubits) and $E := \EN$ for the joint-number dephasing. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (Ascended level.) $\tr \rho_R^2 = 1$: $S_2(\rho_R) = 0$. The radiation is pure, and all information is internal to it (Proposition \claimref{singularity.purity-correlation-transfer-recovery}).
\item (Descended level.) Exactly,
\[
\tr\bigl(E\rho_R\bigr)^2 \;=\; \prod_{k=1}^{4}\bigl(c_k^4 + s_k^4\bigr) \;=\; \frac{817544276833}{6972900390625},
\qquad
S_2(E\rho_R) = \log_2\frac{6972900390625}{817544276833} \approx 3.09 \ \text{bits},
\]
and the von Neumann entropy of $E\rho_R$ is $\sum_k H(c_k^2) = \Sth$ exactly, the full thermal accumulation. Stage by stage, the descended entropy is monotone non-decreasing: read at the $\Cl(1,3)$ level, the radiation's entropy only rises, with no falling branch and no return to zero. This is Hawking's curve, recovered as the wrong-level reading of a history whose ascended state is pure.
\item (The deficit, located.) $\rel{\rho_R}{E\rho_R} = S(E\rho_R) - S(\rho_R) = \Sth$: at completion the radiation's entire information content is the deficit, and the deficit is inter-quanta. Every single-qubit marginal is identical at the two levels (Corollary \claimref{singularity.deficit-carried-quanta-correlations} with Lemma \claimref{singularity.parity-protection}); the decoding correlators of Proposition \claimref{singularity.purity-correlation-transfer-recovery}, whose signatures $(\tfrac{24}{25}, \tfrac{168}{625})$ against $(\tfrac{168}{625}, \tfrac{24}{25})$ distinguish the scrambled from the unscrambled history in the completion, are annihilated exactly by $E$: both become $0$, in both histories, so the two descended histories are indistinguishable by any metric-level measurement, that is, by any joint-number-diagonal observable (Proposition \claimref{singularity.p-reduced-metric-level-reading-many}; under the total-parity grading alone the even correlator $X_{R_1}X_{L_1}Z_{L_2}$ would descend, which is exactly why the pointwise reading is the one the chain needs), and the message does not descend.
\item (What survives, and what is lost.) Descent preserves each intra-pair classical record exactly: the $(R_k, L_k)$ marginal of $E\rho_R$ is the perfectly correlated $\operatorname{diag}(c_k^2, 0, 0, s_k^2)$. And descent destroys every inter-pair correlation exactly: the joint distributions of $(R_k, R_l)$, $k \neq l$, factorise. What the metric level retains is the thermal populations together with the pairwise emission records; everything the scrambling wrote \emph{across} the pairs, which is where Proposition \claimref{singularity.purity-correlation-transfer-recovery} located the information, is erased.
\end{enumerate}
singularity.two-levels-finite-model.technical:
In the full model run with four pairs, let $\rho_R$ be the complete radiation at the end of evaporation and $E = \EN$ the joint-number dephasing. At the ascended level $\tr\rho_R^2 = 1$, so the radiation is pure. At the descended level $\tr(E\rho_R)^2 = \prod_k (c_k^4 + s_k^4)$, $S_2(E\rho_R) \approx 3.09$ bits, and $S(E\rho_R) = \Sth$ exactly, with the descended entropy non-decreasing stage by stage: Hawking's curve, as the metric-level reading of a pure history.

The deficit is $\rel{\rho_R}{E\rho_R} = \Sth$ and is inter-quanta: single-qubit marginals agree at both levels, and the decoding correlators are annihilated by $E$, so the scrambled and unscrambled histories cannot be told apart by any joint-number-diagonal observable. Descent keeps each pair's classical emission record and erases every inter-pair correlation.
singularity.two-levels-finite-model.lay: The toy model can be read at two levels. At the full quantum level the radiation is pure and carries all the information. Read at the ordinary metric level, which keeps only occupation records, the same radiation looks thermal, its entropy only rises, and the trace of the scrambling disappears. This reproduces Hawking's picture of information loss as a reading at the wrong level.
singularity.two-levels-finite-model.typing_note: Added parity protection, cited with the correlation corollary for the equal single-qubit marginals, and the reduced (P_loc) proposition, which the statement uses to equate metric-level measurements with joint-number-diagonal observables (the latter is a judgement call); the paper says Hawking's curve is recovered here, but Hawking's result is not an imported claim in the store, so no standard route was added. Levels pass: conditions already kept.

proofs.main: Computation in exact rational arithmetic, deposited with the script. (1) is Proposition \claimref{singularity.purity-correlation-transfer-recovery}(1). (2) The diagonal of $E\rho_R$ is the configuration distribution of the pure state; by the support constraint ($R_k = L_k$) a configuration is a choice of $b_k \in \{0,1\}$ per pair with probability $\prod_k (c^{(k)}_{b_k})^2$, the accumulated CZ phases squaring away, so the distribution is a product over pairs, its collision probability is $\prod_k (c_k^4 + s_k^4)$, and its Shannon entropy is $\sum_k H(c_k^2) = \Sth$; the monotonicity claim is checked stage by stage (the script also confirms that pinching never increases purity at any stage). (3) is Theorem \claimref{singularity.deficit-theorem-cost-descent-exactly} with $S(\rho_R) = 0$ and Corollary \claimref{singularity.deficit-carried-quanta-correlations}, with Lemma \claimref{singularity.parity-protection} for the single-qubit marginals; the correlator annihilations are checked exactly, in both histories ($X_{R_1}X_{L_1}$ and $X_{R_1}X_{L_1}Z_{L_2}$ are off-diagonal in the joint number basis, so the general vanishing is also visible by inspection of Definition \claimref{obj.singularity.multi-mode-descent}). That the joint-number-diagonal observables are the metric-level measurements is \claimref{singularity.p-reduced-metric-level-reading-many}. (4) Both clauses are read off the diagonal of $E\rho_R$: the intra-pair record is the support constraint surviving as classical correlation, and the inter-pair factorisation is the product structure exhibited in (2); both are checked exactly, for every pair and for the sampled inter-pair joints.
