synthesis.eviction-keeps-one-replica-sad.technical: The island computations of the Page curve are replica computations: the $n$-th Renyi entropy of the radiation is a gravitational path integral summed over geometries joining $n$ copies. At $n = 2$ only two saddles matter at leading order, the disconnected one, giving purity $1/k$ for $k$ radiation states, and the replica wormhole, giving $e^{-S}$ with $S$ the black hole's entropy; the island answer adds them. Reading the black hole's entropy as the capacity bound of the window, $e^{S} = 2^{n_{\mathrm{cap}}}$, is the identification that makes the comparison below; it is a reading of the dictionary, not a result. The eviction mechanism of the series, at zero weight, gives exactly the larger of the two at every stage: on the rising branch the radiation is maximally mixed on its $k$ states, on the falling branch the window, filled to its capacity bound, is maximally entangled with it, and the purity is never the sum. So the two mechanisms map onto each other saddle by saddle, and differ by the subdominant saddle, worth exactly $\ln 2$ of Renyi-2 entropy at the crossing and falling off as $\ln(1 + 2^{-d})$ with the distance $d$ in qubits from it. The split of window from radiation is made in the Clifford algebra of the modes (each side the sub-Clifford algebra of its modes, reduction by projection onto its blades), not by a tensor product; for the even states, those fixed by the total-parity average, the two give the same reduced states, so every eviction statement here is unchanged. A random even state, the Page-typical branch on one parity sector, has the exact average purity $(m + n)/(mn + 2)$ (it would be $(m + n)/(mn + 1)$ for an abstract tensor product with no parity condition); either agrees with the two-saddle value to order $m^{-2}$ at the crossing. At any weights, eviction's falling branch is exactly the thermal entropy of the window; the store's earlier comparison at weights bounded away from zero, which covers every mode of the adopted half-integer weights, measured it against the window's maximal entropy instead, so the extensive difference found there is a choice of baseline, not of mechanism.
synthesis.eviction-keeps-one-replica-sad.lay: Modern calculations of how information comes back out of an evaporating black hole compare two ways the geometry can join copies of the system, and add their contributions. The series has its own mechanism, in which the boundary modes hand their entanglement to the outgoing radiation. Measured with a convenient entropy (the second Renyi entropy), the series' mechanism turns out to follow exactly whichever of the two contributions is larger at each moment, while the standard calculation adds both. The two descriptions therefore line up piece by piece, once the black hole's entropy in the standard calculation is identified with the series' capacity (an identification, not a derivation), and they differ by exactly the smaller piece, which is largest, one bit's worth, at the halfway point of evaporation. A random quantum state, the usual benchmark, agrees with the standard calculation there, whether or not it is restricted, as the series' states are, to a definite even or odd particle number.

proofs.main:
\emph{The split.} Let $A$, $B$ be complementary sets of modes, $\Cl(A)$, $\Cl(B)$ their sub-Clifford algebras, $d_{A}$, $d_{B}$ the dimensions $2^{|A|}$, $2^{|B|}$, $E_{A}$ the projection onto the blades of $\Cl(A)$, and $\Gamma_{A} = \prod_{k \in A}p_{k}$, of square $1$, anticommuting with the generators of $\Cl(A)$ and commuting with $\Cl(B)$. (a) The generators $y\Gamma_{A}$, $y$ a generator of $\Cl(B)$, keep their squares, anticommute with each other and commute with $\Cl(A)$; by Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies} (ground algebra $\Cl(B)$, the planes of $A$, whose volume elements are the $-p_{k}$) they generate an algebra $B'$ commuting with $\Cl(A)$ with $\Cl(A) \otimes B'$ the whole algebra, an ordinary tensor product. (b) Blades are orthogonal for $\langle xy\rangle_{0}$, so $\langle E_{A}(x)y\rangle_{0} = \langle xy\rangle_{0}$ for $y \in \Cl(A)$: $d_{B}E_{A}$ is the partial trace of that tensor product over $B'$. Likewise the partial trace over $\Cl(A)$ is $d_{A}$ times the projection onto the blades of $B'$, which are the even blades of $\Cl(B)$ and $\Gamma_{A}$ times its odd blades; the latter and the odd blades of $\Cl(B)$ are odd, so on an even element this projection is $E_{B}$. (c) Hence for an even state the reductions $d_{B}E_{A}(\rho)$, $d_{A}E_{B}(\rho)$ are the two partial traces of an ordinary tensor product, and if the state is pure they have the same nonzero spectrum (Schmidt decomposition). Evenness is needed: $\tfrac14(1 + e_{1})(1 + e_{2}p_{1})$ is pure with reductions of purity $1$ and $\tfrac12$. (d) Even elements of the algebras of disjoint sets of modes commute, a product of blades from disjoint sets is a blade, scalar only if every factor is and in $\Cl(A)$ only if every factor is; so for such elements $x_{j}$, $\langle\prod x_{j}\rangle_{0} = \prod\langle x_{j}\rangle_{0}$, $E_{A}(\prod x_{j}) = \prod E_{A}(x_{j})$, and traces of powers of products multiply. (e) The pair state with amplitudes $c$ on $\ket{00}$ and $s$ on $\ket{11}$ of modes $k$, $k'$ is $\tfrac14(1 + p_{k}p_{k'})(1 + rp_{k}) + cs(w_{k}w_{k'} + v_{k'}v_{k})$, $r = c^{2} - s^{2}$ (expand $\psi\Omega\psi^{\dagger}$, $\psi = c + s\,w_{k}w_{k'}$, $\Omega = v_{k}w_{k}v_{k'}w_{k'}$, $\dagger$ the anti-automorphism exchanging $v$ and $w$); it is even, and its blades in the algebra of mode $k$ are $\tfrac14(1 + rp_{k})$. The state of the eviction theorem is a product of such pair states, so, reading the pairs of that theorem as these pair states, it is a pure even state, fixed by $x \mapsto \tfrac12(x + \Gamma x\Gamma)$, the total-parity form of the single-mode average of Theorem \claimref{singularity.descent-parity-average}. The last check function verifies (a) to (e) on three and four modes.

\emph{(i).} By Theorem \claimref{singularity.eviction-window-thermal-product-radiation-entropy}(1) the window state is the product of its members' thermal marginals, which, reading the pairs of that theorem as the pair states of (e), is on the split $\rho_{L} = \prod_{k \in W(t)}\tfrac12(1 + r_{k}p_{k})$ by (d) and (e), and the joint state of window and radiation is pure and even, so by (c) $\rho_{R}$ and $\rho_{L}$ have the same nonzero spectrum and $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{R}^{2} = \operatorname{tr}\rho_{L}^{2}$. The purity of the product is the product of the purities by (d). In the algebra of mode $k$, with trace $2\langle\cdot\rangle_{0}$ and $p_{k}^{2} = 1$, $\rho_{k}^{2} = \tfrac14(1 + r_{k}^{2}) + \tfrac12 r_{k}p_{k}$, so $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{k}^{2} = \tfrac12(1 + r_{k}^{2})$, which with $c_{k}^{2} + s_{k}^{2} = 1$ is $c_{k}^{4} + s_{k}^{4}$; zero weight ($c_{k}^{2} = s_{k}^{2} = \tfrac12$, $r_{k} = 0$) gives $\tfrac12$. The script computes $2\langle\rho^{2}\rangle_{0}$ for an element of square $1$ (the vector $e_{3}$ of $\Cl(3,0)$ standing for $p_{k}$) at $c^{2} = \tfrac12, \tfrac23, \tfrac57$ and the purity of the threefold Kronecker product of the matrices; the last check function computes the same in the algebra of the modes, with $p_{k} = f_{k}e_{k}$.

\emph{(ii).} At zero weight each window member is maximally entangled with one radiated quantum (Theorem \claimref{singularity.eviction-window-thermal-product-radiation-entropy}(4), maximally entangled idealisation). After $j$ radiated quanta, write $w = |W(t)|$; by clauses (3) and (4) of that theorem, $w = j$ before the first eviction, and afterwards the window is held at the capacity bound, so $w = \min(j, n_{\mathrm{cap}})$; an evicted pair has both halves in the radiation, where they form a pure pair. So $\rho_{R}$ is the product, in the sense of (d), of $w$ maximally mixed modes with $j - w$ pure even pairs, of purity $2^{-w} = \max(2^{-j}, 2^{-n_{\mathrm{cap}}})$, since $\min(j, n_{\mathrm{cap}})$ is the smaller exponent. It is one of the two terms of $2^{-j} + 2^{-n_{\mathrm{cap}}}$, never their sum, because both terms are positive. The script builds the state vector for every $1 \leq j \leq 6$ and $0 \leq w \leq j$ (radiation register of the $j$ quanta and the $j - w$ evicted partners, window register of the $w$ members, amplitudes in integers), forms $\rho_{R}$ by the exact partial trace, and confirms $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{R}^{2} = 2^{-w}$; it then runs a stage sequence with $n_{\mathrm{cap}} = 6 - j$ and confirms $\max(2^{-j}, 2^{-n_{\mathrm{cap}}})$ at each $j = 0, \ldots, 6$.

\emph{(iii).} First the abstract tensor product. For the unitarily invariant measure on unit vectors of a space of dimension $D = mn$, the second moment is $\langle\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}^{\otimes 2}\rangle = (\mathbb{1} + F)/(D(D + 1))$, with $F$ the swap of the two copies (Schur's lemma on the symmetric square). Since $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2} = \operatorname{tr}[(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}^{\otimes 2})(F_{A} \otimes \mathbb{1})]$ with $F_{A}$ the swap of the two $A$ factors, $\langle\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}\rangle = (\operatorname{tr}F_{A} + \operatorname{tr}FF_{A})/(D(D + 1))$. On the basis $\ket{a_{1}b_{1}a_{2}b_{2}}$, $F_{A}$ sends it to $\ket{a_{2}b_{1}a_{1}b_{2}}$ and $FF_{A}$ to $\ket{a_{1}b_{2}a_{2}b_{1}}$, so $\operatorname{tr}F_{A} = mn^{2}$ and $\operatorname{tr}FF_{A} = m^{2}n$, and $\langle\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}\rangle = mn(m + n)/(mn(mn + 1)) = (m + n)/(mn + 1)$. The script counts the diagonal entries for six pairs $(m, n)$. Then $1/m + 1/n - (m + n)/(mn + 1) = (m + n)/(mn(mn + 1)) > 0$, and $(m + n)/(mn + 1) > 1/\min(m, n)$ because $\min(m, n)(m + n) > mn + 1$ for $m, n \geq 2$ (with $m \leq n$: $m^{2} + mn > mn + 1$). Now the even states. A pure even state is a projector of rank one commuting with the involution $\Gamma$, so its vector lies in an eigenspace of $\Gamma$, a parity sector, of dimension $D/2$; in the tensor product of (a), $\Gamma = \Gamma_{A} \otimes \Gamma_{B}$, and the sector is spanned by the basis vectors $\ket{ab}$ with the parities of $a$ and $b$ equal (or, for the other sector, opposite). By (c) the reduction to $A$ is the partial trace of that tensor product, so $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}$ is again the expectation of $F_{A} \otimes \mathbb{1}$, and Schur's lemma on the symmetric square of the sector gives the second moment $\Pi^{\otimes 2}(\mathbb{1} + F)/(\tfrac{D}{2}(\tfrac{D}{2} + 1))$, $\Pi$ the projector on the sector. The trace of $F_{A}$ on the square of the sector counts $(a_{1}, b_{1}, a_{2}, b_{2})$ with $a_{1} = a_{2}$ and both $b$ of the parity fixed by $a_{1}$: $m(n/2)^{2}$; that of $FF_{A}$ counts those with $b_{1} = b_{2}$: $n(m/2)^{2}$. So $\langle\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}\rangle = \tfrac14 mn(m + n)/(\tfrac14 mn(mn + 2)) = (m + n)/(mn + 2)$. Then $1/m + 1/n - (m + n)/(mn + 2) = 2(m + n)/(mn(mn + 2)) > 0$, $(m + n)/(mn + 2) < (m + n)/(mn + 1)$, and with $m \le n$, $m(m + n) > mn + 2$ since $m^{2} \ge 4$. The last check function counts the two traces on the sector for six pairs $(m, n)$. (The same value is the case $n = 2$ of the sector formula for every index, clause (iv) of the stored result on stabiliser-family averages and the parity sector, which is not needed here.)

\emph{(iv).} At $j = n_{\mathrm{cap}}$, (ii) gives $2^{-j} = 1/m$ with $m = 2^{j}$ and the two-saddle value $2/m$, ratio $2$, so $S_{2}$ differs by $\ln 2$; (iii) with $n = m$ gives $2m/(m^{2} + 1)$, whose ratio to $1/m$ is $2m^{2}/(m^{2} + 1) = 2 - 2/(m^{2} + 1) \in (2 - 2/m^{2}, 2)$, so its $S_{2}$ lies below the eviction value by $\ln 2 - \ln(1 + m^{-2})$, which is in $(\ln 2 - m^{-2}, \ln 2)$ since $0 < \ln(1 + u) < u$. On a sector, $2m/(m^{2} + 2)$ has ratio $2m^{2}/(m^{2} + 2) = 2 - 4/(m^{2} + 2) \in (2 - 4/m^{2}, 2)$ to $1/m$, so its $S_{2}$ lies below the eviction value by $\ln 2 - \ln(1 + 2m^{-2}) \in (\ln 2 - 2m^{-2}, \ln 2)$. Off the crossing the ratio of $2^{-j} + 2^{-n_{\mathrm{cap}}}$ to its larger term is $1 + 2^{-|j - n_{\mathrm{cap}}|}$. The script checks the ratios at $m = 2, 4, 8$ from the computed Haar purity (at $m = 16$ from the formula) and along the stage sequence of (ii).

\emph{(v).} By Theorem \claimref{singularity.eviction-window-thermal-product-radiation-entropy}(1), $S_{R}(t) = \sum_{k \in W(t)}h_{k}$, and $h_{k}$ is the von Neumann entropy of member $k$'s thermal marginal, so $S_{R}$ is the thermal entropy of the window with no correction term at any weight. The deficit of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.eviction-deficit-against-page-deficit} is $\delta_{\mathrm{ev}} = C - S_{R}$ with $C = |W(t)|\ln 2$, the maximal entropy of $|W(t)|$ two-level members; it equals the thermal entropy exactly when every $h_{k} = \ln 2$, that is at zero weight, where $h_{k} = s(0) = \ln 2$. Under the weights $\kappa(k + \tfrac12)$ every member has $|x_{k}| = (2k + 1)\pi \geq \pi$, so the stored clause (iii) applies with $x_{*} = \pi$ and its linear deficit is a deficit against $C$. The Page-typical branch of Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-page-average-entropy-subsystem} is compared against $\ln m$, the logarithm of the dimension, which for a window at zero weight is $C$. $\square$

\emph{Reading (not part of the proof).} Penington, Shenker, Stanford and Yang (arXiv:1911.11977, Sec.~2.2, Eqs.~(2.13) and (2.15); Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-replica-wormhole-two-saddle-purity}) compute the radiation's purity in the end-of-the-world-brane model as $1/k + Z_{2}/Z_{1}^{2}$, the disconnected saddle plus the replica wormhole, schematically $1/k + e^{-S_{0}}$, and in the microcanonical ensemble (Sec.~2.5.1) recover Page's random-state spectrum. With $k = 2^{j}$ and the reading $e^{S} = 2^{n_{\mathrm{cap}}}$ (an identification of the black hole's entropy with the window's capacity bound, not derived) this is the two-saddle value of (ii), and (iii) is Page's random-state value it agrees with at planar order. In the canonical ensemble the transition is smoothed over a region of size $G_{N}^{-1/2}$ in $\log k$ (Sec.~2.5.2); the eviction branch at nonzero weight is not smoothed, by (v). Checked against the source.

synthesis.exceptional-boundary-measure-o.formal:
Work with the Schwarzschild gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) inside its horizon locus, in the synchronous gauge of Lemma \claimref{interior.kasner-form-interior}, whose derived metric is $ds^{2} = d\tau^{2} - A\,dt^{2} - r^{2}d\Omega^{2}$, $A = 2M/r - 1$, with $\tau$ the proper time to the singularity, and write $x := r/2M$. Let $E = \{\tau = 0\}\times\mathbb{R}_{t}\times S^{2}$ be the exceptional set of the weighted blow-up (Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-interior-collar-kasner-form}), whose weights are the Kasner exponents $(-\tfrac13, \tfrac23, \tfrac23)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Defining function.)} $\tau$ is the unique function of $r$ that vanishes on $E$ and has unit timelike physical gradient, $Q(\hb^{T}(\nabla\tau)) = A\,(d\tau/dr)^{2} = 1$; $\tau = \tfrac{2}{3}r^{3/2}(2M)^{-1/2}\,T(x)$ with $T(x) = \sum_{k} \tfrac{3}{2k+3}\binom{2k}{k}4^{-k}x^{k} = 1 + \tfrac{3}{10}x + O(x^{2})$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The measure.)} The three-volume per unit Killing time of the slice at proper time $\tau$ is $V(\tau) = 4\pi r^{2}\sqrt{A} = 12\pi M\,\tau\,\bigl(1 - \tfrac45 x + O(x^{2})\bigr)$, so
\[
\mu_{E} \;:=\; \lim_{\tau\to 0}\frac{V(\tau)}{\tau} \;=\; 12\pi M \quad\text{per unit Killing time}\qquad (3M\,dt\,d\Omega),
\]
finite and nonzero because the weights sum to one ($V \propto \tau^{p_{1}+p_{2}+p_{3}}$, $p_{1}+p_{2}+p_{3} = 1$). It is a measure on $E$ of the dimension of an area, fixed by the derived metric with no free constant, by (i).
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The count on $E$, at leading order.)} An eigenvalue threshold $2M/r^{3} = \lambda$ is the slice $\tau_{c} = \tfrac23\lambda^{-1/2}\bigl(1 + O(x_{c})\bigr)$, since $(2M/r^{3})\tau^{2} = \tfrac49 T(x)^{2}$. Under (C1) and (C2) the count of Proposition \claimref{singularity.stretched-singularity-count} is $dN/dt = \nu V(\tau_{c}) = \nu\tau_{c}\mu_{E}\sqrt{1-x_{c}}/T(x_{c})$, which at the slice of (C1) ($\lambda = 1$) is exactly $8\pi\nu M\sqrt{1 - x_{c}}$. Hence, at leading order in $x_{c} = (2M)^{-2/3}$, $dN/dt = \nu'\mu_{E}$ with
\[
\nu' \;:=\; \nu\,\tau_{c} \;=\; \tfrac23\,\kappa_{s}, \qquad \kappa_{s} := \nu\lambda^{-1/2},
\]
the single constant to which (C1) and (C2) reduce at leading order (filed alongside, synthesis.c1-c2-forms-forced-one-number). So, for the count at leading order, (C1) and (C2) can be replaced by the single premise (C2$'$): the boundary modes are carried by $E$ itself with $\nu'$ fermionic modes per Planck area of $\mu_{E}$; the two give the same leading count, and differ at relative order $x_{c}$ (first coefficient $-\tfrac12$ on the (C1) slice, none for $\mu_{E}$), corrections that belong to the slice.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The number.)} With the counted epoch at the modular period $8\pi M$, the area law $N\ln 2 = \SBH$ of Proposition \claimref{singularity.area-law-test} holds at leading order if and only if $\nu'\ln 2 = 1/(24\pi)$, equivalently $\kappa_{s}\ln 2 = 1/(16\pi)$, the registered density at $\lambda = 1$ (Prediction \claimref{pred.boundary-mode-density}).
\end{enumerate}

Near the singularity the $t$-direction stretches as $	au^{-1/3}$ and the spheres shrink as $	au^{2/3}$, the Kasner exponents that the weighted blow-up forces, and since they sum to one the three-volume per unit Killing time of the slice at $	au$ is $12\pi M\,	au$ at leading order. An eigenvalue threshold $\lambda$ is the proper-time slice $	au_c = 	frac23\lambda^{-1/2}$ at leading order, so under (C1) and (C2) the leading count is $
u'\mu_E$ with $
u' = 
u	au_c = 	frac23\kappa_s$, where $\kappa_s = 
u\lambda^{-1/2}$ is the one constant to which the two postulates reduce. At leading order, then, the slice can be dropped: counting $

synthesis.exceptional-boundary-measure-o.lay: The singularity paper places the black hole's quantum modes on a surface inside the hole where the strength of the gravitational field, its curvature, reaches the Planck value, and packs them at a fixed number per Planck-sized cell. For a large hole, and to leading order, those two assumptions only ever appear multiplied together. This result adds a geometric reason why the surface itself can be dropped. Near the singularity one direction of space stretches while two shrink, at rates whose exponents add up to one, so the volume of a slice near the singularity is proportional to the time left before reaching it. Dividing out that time gives a natural size for the singularity's own boundary, an area, with nothing left to choose. Counting a fixed number of modes per Planck area of that boundary gives the same leading count as the two assumptions together. That one number is not derived; matching the black hole entropy fixes it.

synthesis.finite-normaliser-averages-lea.formal:
Let $e_{1}, \dots, e_{2m}$ be the signed directions of $\Cl(2m, 0)$, $Q(e_{r}) = 1$, with strings $S \subseteq \{1, \dots, 2m\}$, blades $e_{S}$, and the forms $b(S,T) = |S||T| + |S \cap T|$, $q(S) = \binom{|S|}{2} \pmod 2$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra}(ii) (commutation and square signs); adjoin a central unit $\omega$, $\omega^{2} = -1$ (the product of all generators of $\Cl(2m, 1)$ or $\Cl(2m + 1, 0)$, whichever has square $-1$), so that $h_{S} = e_{S}$ or $\omega e_{S}$ has square $+1$, and write $\mathrm{tr} = 2^{m}\langle\cdot\rangle_{0}$. A \emph{family} is a subspace $L \subseteq \mathbb{F}_{2}^{2m}$ of dimension $m$ on which $b$ vanishes, and its \emph{states} are the $2^{m}$ idempotents $\rho = 2^{-m}\prod_{r}(1 + s_{r}h_{S_{r}})$, $S_{r}$ a basis of $L$, $s_{r} = \pm 1$. For $1 \le a < m$, $b' = m - a$, let $A$ be the subalgebra generated by $e_{1}, \dots, e_{2a}$ and $\omega$, $d_{A} = 2^{a}$, $d_{B} = 2^{b'}$, $D = d_{A}d_{B}$; the trace-preserving conditional expectation onto $A$ is the projection onto the blades of $A$, $\rho_{A} = d_{B}$ times the projection of $\rho$, and $\mathrm{tr}\rho_{A}^{n} = (|L_{A}|/d_{A})^{n-1}$ with $L_{A}$ the strings of $L$ inside $\{1, \dots, 2a\}$. A quarter turn $(1 + u)/\sqrt2$, $u = e_{w}$ or $\omega e_{w}$ of square $-1$, permutes the states and acts on strings by $x \mapsto x + b(x, w)w$. The \emph{finite average} $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{fin}}$ is the mean over all states of all families (no clause uses that these states form one orbit of the quarter turns; they do for $m \le 3$, computed, and in general that needs three classical inputs not derived here: Witt's extension theorem, generation of $Sp(2m, 2)$ by transvections, and the sign flips by conjugation with blades); the \emph{sector average} is the mean over the states with $v = \{1, \dots, 2m\} \in L$ and a fixed sign of $h_{v}$, the parity sector, of dimension $D/2$ (one orbit of the quarter turns about even strings for $m \le 4$, computed; not used). Haar values are those of Facts \claimref{synthesis.imported-haar-moments-of-random-pure-state} (whose case $n = 2$ is the mean purity) and \claimref{singularity.imported-page-average-entropy-subsystem}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Count by rank; proved.)} The number of families with $|L_{A}| = 2^{a - e}$ (so $\rho_{A}$ flat of rank $2^{e}$) is $N(a, a - e)\,N(b', b' - e)\,|Sp(2e, 2)|$, with $N(c, k) = \binom{c}{k}_{2}\prod_{r=0}^{k-1}(2^{c-r} + 1)$ the number of $k$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_{2}^{2c}$ on which $b$ vanishes and $|Sp(2e, 2)| = 2^{e^{2}}\prod_{r=1}^{e}(4^{r} - 1)$; the total is $\prod_{r=1}^{m}(2^{r} + 1)$. At $a = b' = 1$: $9$ and $6$ families, $36$ and $24$ states.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Moments two and three agree; proved for every $a$, $b'$ by counting; a special case.)} $\langle\mathrm{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}\rangle_{\mathrm{fin}} = (d_{A} + d_{B})/(D + 1)$ and $\langle\mathrm{tr}\rho_{A}^{3}\rangle_{\mathrm{fin}} = (d_{A}^{2} + d_{B}^{2} + 3D + 1)/((D + 1)(D + 2))$, the Haar values. This is the case of a blade state, with $W = V_{A}$, of the quarter-turn design statement (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.quarter-turn-rotors-of-the-even-subalgebra-form-a-state-design-of-order-three}, clause (iii)), which gives the same moments for every state; it is kept here with its counting proof as a cross-check and is not the general design result.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Moment four does not: values computed, the crossing limit proved.)} $\langle\mathrm{tr}\rho_{A}^{4}\rangle_{\mathrm{fin}}$ exceeds the Haar value for every $a + b' \le 8$: $\tfrac{13}{20}$ against $\tfrac{22}{35}$ at $a = b' = 1$, $\tfrac{3}{17}$ against $\tfrac{52}{323}$ at $a = b' = 2$. For every $a$, $b'$, $n$ (proved): $\langle|L_{A}|^{n-1}\rangle_{\mathrm{fin}} = \sum_{r \ge 0}N(a, r)\,\prod_{j=m-r+1}^{m}(2^{j} + 1)^{-1}\,\prod_{j=0}^{r-1}(2^{n-1} - 2^{j})$, the three factors being the number of $r$-dimensional subspaces of $V_{A}$ on which $b$ vanishes, the fraction of families containing one of them, and the number of $(n-1)$-tuples spanning it. At the crossing $a = b' = c$, $d = 2^{c}$, the $r$-th term of $d^{n-1}\langle\mathrm{tr}\rho_{A}^{n}\rangle_{\mathrm{fin}}$ tends to the Gaussian binomial $\binom{n-1}{r}_{2}$ as $c \to \infty$, so the coefficient tends to $G_{n-1} = \sum_{r}\binom{n-1}{r}_{2}$, the number of subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_{2}^{n-1}$, for every $n \ge 2$ (proved): $2, 5, 16, 67, 374$ for $n = 2, \dots, 6$, where the Haar coefficient tends to the Catalan numbers $2, 5, 14, 42, 132$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.eviction-keeps-one-of-catalan-many-replica-saddles}(iii)). Computed: the coefficient lies within $2^{-16}$ at $c = 16$ and $2^{-32}$ at $c = 24$ below these values. Equivalently the limit is $\phi\sum_{k \ge 0}2^{(n-1)k - k^{2}}\phi_{k}^{-2}$, $\phi_{k} = \prod_{j=1}^{k}(1 - 2^{-j})$, $\phi = \phi_{\infty}$ (the count (i) summed by rank).
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Parity sector; proved.)} For a unit vector drawn from the unitarily invariant measure of the parity sector, $\langle\mathrm{tr}\rho_{A}^{n}\rangle = 2\sum_{\sigma \in S_{n}}(d_{A}/2)^{\#(\sigma^{-1}\eta)}(d_{B}/2)^{\#(\sigma)}/\prod_{l=0}^{n-1}(D/2 + l)$ (the same Schur average as the Fact, on a space that is $(\text{even} \otimes \text{even}) \oplus (\text{odd} \otimes \text{odd})$ and not a tensor product), so the mean purity is
\[
\frac{d_{A} + d_{B}}{D + 2} \quad\text{in place of}\quad \frac{d_{A} + d_{B}}{D + 1} ,
\]
and the sector average of the purity equals it for every $a$, $b'$; so does the sector average of $\mathrm{tr}\rho_{A}^{3}$, with value $(d_{A}^{2} + d_{B}^{2} + 3D + 4)/((D + 2)(D + 4))$ (proved for every $m$ by the same double count; also a corollary of the design statement named in (ii), with $\omega$ as its unit). Computed for $m \le 4$: the sector average of $\mathrm{tr}\rho_{A}^{4}$ exceeds the sector's Haar value. At $m = 2$ the six states reached from $\tfrac14(1 + h_{12})(1 + h_{34})$ by the six bivector quarter turns have purities $1, 1, \tfrac12, \tfrac12, \tfrac12, \tfrac12$, mean $\tfrac23$, against $\tfrac45$ for two unrestricted modes.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Which quarter turns; proved, with the values at $m = 4$ computed.)} The quarter turns about bivectors permute the directions, and the orbit of the family spanned by $\{1,2\}, \{3,4\}, \dots$ is the $(2m - 1)!!$ perfect matchings, equal to the $\prod_{r=1}^{m-1}(2^{r} + 1)$ families containing $v$ exactly for $m \le 3$ ($3$, $15$) and fewer for every $m \ge 4$ ($105$ of $135$ at $m = 4$, where the classes of even strings modulo $v$ fall into orbits of $28$ and $35$ and the mean purity at $a = b' = 2$ is $\tfrac{17}{35}$, against $\tfrac49$ for the sector and $\tfrac{8}{17}$ for the Fact; one quartic quarter turn added restores $135$ and $\tfrac49$). The orbits of the bivector turns on the classes of even strings modulo $v$ are the $\lfloor m/2\rfloor$ size classes $\{2k, 2m - 2k\}$: $3$; $15$; $28 + 35$; $45 + 210$ at $m = 2, 3, 4, 5$; so bivector turns fail for odd $m \ge 5$ as well, although every class then has a real quarter turn of unit norm. Without the adjoined unit, a quarter turn of unit norm about $e_{w}$ exists in $\Cl(2m, 0)$ exactly when $q(w) = 1$; for $m$ odd every class of even strings modulo $v$ has such a member ($e_{v}^{2} = -1$, the even subalgebra has its own unit), and for $m$ even $q$ descends to the classes and is preserved, so for even $m \ge 4$ the classes with $q = 0$ and $q = 1$ are never exchanged ($28$ and $35$ at $m = 4$; $528$ and $495$ at $m = 6$, counted; that these are single orbits at $m = 6$ is not checked).
\item[(vi)] \emph{(Mean entropy; computed.)} The finite average of the entropy is $\ln 2$ times the mean of $e$: $\tfrac25\ln 2 < \tfrac{7}{25}$ at $a = b' = 1$ against Page's $\tfrac13$; at the crossing it lies below $\ln d$ by between $0.84\ln 2$ and $0.86\ln 2$ for $c = 8, 16, 24$, more than $0.56$, where Page's deficit is below $\tfrac12$.
\end{enumerate}
So the average over these states reproduces the imported mean purity and third moment and nothing further: the mean purity (the case $n = 2$ of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-haar-moments-of-random-pure-state}), as used in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.eviction-keeps-one-replica-saddle}(iii), (iv), is reproduced by (ii), but deriving the Haar value needs the state-independent average of the design statement named in (ii) together with invariance of the measure, and holds at powers of two only, while the stored clause is stated for all $m$, $n$; the same Fact, as used at every index in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.eviction-keeps-one-of-catalan-many-replica-saddles}(iii), (iv), and Page's average, as used in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.eviction-deficit-against-page-deficit}, could not: with the finite average the gap $\ln C_{n}/(n - 1)$ would read $\ln G_{n-1}/(n - 1)$, $\tfrac13\ln 16$ at $n = 4$, and the half nat at the crossing about $0.59$. On a parity sector the Renyi-2 comparison at the crossing $d_{A} = d_{B} = d$ reads $2d/(d^{2} + 2)$, below the capacity value in $S_{2}$ by $\ln 2 - \ln(1 + 2d^{-2})$ in place of $\ln 2 - \ln(1 + d^{-2})$; the leading terms and the Catalan limit are unchanged (argued from (iv): the planar permutations contribute $C_{n}d^{1-n}$ in both). None of the stored results is contradicted: they state the Haar values for an abstract tensor product and do not use a finite group or a sector.
synthesis.finite-normaliser-averages-lea.technical: The signed directions generate a finite group whose quarter turns shuffle a finite set of special states, those fixed by a largest commuting set of blades. Averaging over that finite set is exact arithmetic: a reduced state always has a flat spectrum of rank a power of two, and the number of states of each rank is a product of counts of isotropic subspaces. The average purity and the average third moment come out equal to the random-state (Haar) values for every split, by a two-line double count. The fourth moment does not, in every split of at most eight modes (computed): one against one mode it is 13/20 where the random-state value is 22/35. At the point where the two parts have equal size the finite average replaces the Catalan numbers 2, 5, 14, 42 of the random-state moments by 2, 5, 16, 67, the numbers of subspaces of a binary space (proved in the limit of large equal parts), and the mean entropy sits about 0.59 below the maximum instead of one half. If only states of one fermion parity are allowed, the group that preserves parity still reproduces the random-state values of that sector, but those are different numbers, because a parity sector is not a product of two parts: the mean purity has D + 2 in the denominator where the unrestricted formula has D + 1. Finally, the quarter turns in planes of two directions reach every allowed family only for four and six directions; from eight on they reach 105 of 135 families and give a different mean.
synthesis.finite-normaliser-averages-lea.lay: Some of the series' comparisons use the entanglement of a quantum state picked completely at random, a result taken from the literature. This entry asks whether the same numbers can be obtained from the series' own finite group of quarter turns, by averaging over a finite list of states instead of over all of them. The answer is yes for the two simplest measures and no beyond: the finite list gives exactly the random value for the average purity and for the next moment, then departs at the fourth moment in every case computed, up to eight modes (13/20 instead of 22/35 in the smallest), and it gives a different average entropy. It also shows that if only states with an even number of particles are allowed, the random value itself changes slightly, and that quarter turns in planes alone are enough only for the two smallest cases. Everything here is for the finite list of states named, with the splits and sizes stated in each clause.

\begin{proof}
\emph{Setting.} By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra}(ii), $e_{S}e_{T} = (-1)^{b(S,T)}e_{T}e_{S}$ and $e_{S}^{2} = (-1)^{q(S)}$, so the $h_{S}$ of a family commute, square to $1$, and $\rho = 2^{-m}\prod_{r}(1 + s_{r}h_{S_{r}}) = 2^{-m}\sum_{S \in L}\pm h_{S}$ is an idempotent with $\mathrm{tr}\rho = 1$. \emph{Partial trace.} The commutant of $A$ is generated by $\omega$ and the elements $e_{\{1,\dots,2a\}}e_{j}$, $j > 2a$. A blade $e_{S}e_{T}$, $S \subseteq \{1,\dots,2a\}$, $T \subseteq \{2a+1,\dots,2m\}$, is up to sign $e_{S}e_{\{1,\dots,2a\}}^{|T|}$ times a monomial of the commutant in the $|T|$ generators indexed by $T$, and the normalised trace of the commutant vanishes on that monomial unless $T = \emptyset$. So the trace-preserving conditional expectation onto $A$ keeps the blades with $T = \emptyset$ and kills the others; $\rho_{A} = d_{B}$ times it, that is $\rho_{A} = d_{A}^{-1}\sum_{S \in L_{A}}\pm h_{S}$, and since $L_{A}$ is a subspace on which the signs form a character, $\rho_{A}^{2} = (|L_{A}|/d_{A})\rho_{A}$ and $\mathrm{tr}\rho_{A}^{n} = (|L_{A}|/d_{A})^{n-1}$: flat of rank $d_{A}/|L_{A}|$. \emph{Quarter turns.} For $u^{2} = -1$, $(1 + u)h(1 - u)/2$ is $h$ if $u$ and $h$ commute and $uh$ otherwise, which is $\pm h_{x + w}$: the map $x \mapsto x + b(x,w)w$ on strings, with a change of signs, so states go to states and the moments, which do not depend on the signs, are constant on sign classes.

(i) Let $V_{A}$ be the strings inside $\{1,\dots,2a\}$; $b$ restricted to it is the form of $2a$ directions, nondegenerate (the stored clause (iii), even case), so the string space is the orthogonal sum of $V_{A}$ and $V_{B} = V_{A}^{\perp}$, of dimensions $2a$ and $2b'$ ($V_{B}$ is the set of strings of the commutant's monomials of the lemma above, not the strings inside the last $2b'$ directions). Put $I_{A} = L \cap V_{A} = L_{A}$ and $I_{B} = L \cap V_{B}$, of dimensions $k_{A}$, $k_{B}$. Then $L \subseteq (I_{A} \oplus I_{B})^{\perp}$ and $L/(I_{A} \oplus I_{B})$ is a family of $(I_{A}^{\perp}/I_{A}) \oplus (I_{B}^{\perp}/I_{B})$, of dimensions $2(a - k_{A})$ and $2(b' - k_{B})$, meeting neither summand. A maximal subspace on which the form vanishes and which meets neither summand projects injectively to each, so $a - k_{A} = b' - k_{B} = e$ and it is the graph of a linear bijection $\theta$ with $b(\theta x, \theta y) = b(x, y)$ (the form vanishes on the graph and the field has characteristic two); conversely every such graph is one. There are $|Sp(2e, 2)|$ such $\theta$, $N(a, a - e)$ choices of $I_{A}$ and $N(b', b' - e)$ of $I_{B}$, and $L$ is recovered from $(I_{A}, I_{B}, \theta)$. The count $N(c, k)$: an ordered basis of a $k$-dimensional subspace on which $b$ vanishes is chosen in $\prod_{r=0}^{k-1}(2^{2c - r} - 2^{r})$ ways, and each subspace has $\prod_{r=0}^{k-1}(2^{k} - 2^{r})$ ordered bases; the quotient is $\binom{c}{k}_{2}\prod_{r=0}^{k-1}(2^{c-r} + 1)$. The order of $Sp(2e, 2)$ is counted the same way by symplectic bases. At $k = m$ the total $\prod_{r=1}^{m}(2^{r} + 1)$.

(ii) The number of families containing a given nonzero string $x$ is the number of families of $x^{\perp}/x$, $\prod_{r=1}^{m-1}(2^{r} + 1)$, so a nonzero string lies in a fraction $1/(D + 1)$ of the families, and two distinct commuting nonzero strings lie together in a fraction $1/((D + 1)(D/2 + 1))$. Hence $\langle|L_{A}|\rangle = 1 + (d_{A}^{2} - 1)/(D + 1)$, and dividing by $d_{A}$ gives $(d_{A} + d_{B})/(D + 1)$. For the third moment, $|L_{A}|^{2}$ counts ordered pairs $(x, y)$ of $L_{A}$: one pair $(0,0)$; $3(d_{A}^{2} - 1)$ pairs spanning a line; and $(d_{A}^{2} - 1)(d_{A}^{2}/2 - 2)$ ordered pairs of distinct commuting nonzero strings of $V_{A}$. So $\langle|L_{A}|^{2}\rangle(D + 1)(D + 2) = (D + 1)(D + 2) + 3(d_{A}^{2} - 1)(D + 2) + (d_{A}^{2} - 1)(d_{A}^{2} - 4) = d_{A}^{2}(d_{A}^{2} + d_{B}^{2} + 3D + 1)$, and dividing by $d_{A}^{2}$ gives the stated value. Both values are the blade-state case, with $W = V_{A}$, of clause (iii) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.quarter-turn-rotors-of-the-even-subalgebra-form-a-state-design-of-order-three}; the count above is an independent derivation of that case. At $n = 2$ the value is the one Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-haar-moments-of-random-pure-state} states for the mean purity. The same Fact at $n = 3$: the identity gives $d_{A}d_{B}^{3}$, the cycle $\eta$ gives $d_{A}^{3}d_{B}$, its inverse $d_{A}d_{B}$, and the three transpositions $d_{A}^{2}d_{B}^{2}$ each, over $D(D + 1)(D + 2)$: the same.

(iii) The values are evaluations of (i). For the limit put $k = c - e$. With $\binom{c}{k}_{2} = 2^{k(c-k)}\phi_{c}/(\phi_{k}\phi_{c-k})$, $\prod_{r<k}(2^{c-r} + 1) = 2^{kc - k(k-1)/2}\prod_{r<k}(1 + 2^{r-c})$, $|Sp(2e,2)| = 2^{2e^{2} + e}\prod_{r \le e}(1 - 4^{-r})$ and $\prod_{r \le 2c}(2^{r} + 1) = 2^{c(2c+1)}\prod_{r \le 2c}(1 + 2^{-r})$, the power of two in the fraction of families with $e = c - k$ is $2k(c - k) + 2kc - k(k - 1) + 2(c - k)^{2} + (c - k) - c(2c + 1) = -k^{2}$, and the remaining factors tend, as $c \to \infty$ at fixed $k$, to $\phi_{k}^{-2}\prod_{r}(1 - 4^{-r})/\prod_{r}(1 + 2^{-r}) = \phi/\phi_{k}^{2}$. They are bounded uniformly in $c$ by a constant times $\phi_{k}^{-2} \le \phi^{-2}$, so $d^{n-1}\langle\mathrm{tr}\rho_{A}^{n}\rangle_{\mathrm{fin}} = \sum_{k}p_{k}(c)2^{(n-1)k}$ converges by domination to the stated series. \emph{The limit is $G_{n-1}$.} $|L_{A}|^{n-1}$ counts the $(n-1)$-tuples of elements of $L_{A}$; sort them by the subspace $U \subseteq L_{A}$ they span, of dimension $r \le n - 1$. A subspace $U$ of $V_{A}$ lies in some family only if $b$ vanishes on it, and then in the families of $U^{\perp}/U$, a fraction $\prod_{j=m-r+1}^{m}(2^{j} + 1)^{-1}$ of all; there are $N(a, r)$ such $U$; and the tuples spanning a given $U$ are the $r \times (n-1)$ matrices of rank $r$, $\prod_{j<r}(2^{n-1} - 2^{j})$ of them. This gives the displayed sum (at $a = b' = 2$, $n = 4$: $1 + \tfrac{105}{17} + \tfrac{70}{17} = \tfrac{192}{17} = 64 \cdot \tfrac{3}{17}$). At $a = c$, $m = 2c$: $N(c, r) = \binom{c}{r}_{2}\prod_{j<r}(2^{c-j} + 1) = 2^{r(c-r)}2^{rc - r(r-1)/2}(1 + o(1))/\phi_{r}$ and $\prod_{j=2c-r+1}^{2c}(2^{j} + 1) = 2^{2cr - r(r-1)/2}(1 + o(1))$, so their quotient tends to $2^{-r^{2}}/\phi_{r} = 2^{-r(r-1)/2}/\prod_{j=1}^{r}(2^{j} - 1)$; times $\prod_{j<r}(2^{n-1} - 2^{j}) = 2^{r(r-1)/2}\prod_{j<r}(2^{n-1-j} - 1)$ this is $\prod_{j<r}(2^{n-1-j} - 1)/\prod_{j=1}^{r}(2^{j} - 1) = \binom{n-1}{r}_{2}$. The sum has at most $n$ terms, so the limit is $\sum_{r}\binom{n-1}{r}_{2} = G_{n-1}$. The check compares the displayed sum with (i) at small sizes and the values at $c = 16, 24$ with $G_{n-1}$.

(iv) The parity sector is the $+1$ eigenspace of $h_{v}$ on the $D$-dimensional module; in the occupation basis of the lemma's tensor factors it is spanned by the products of an even with an even and an odd with an odd state. The Schur argument of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-haar-moments-of-random-pure-state} applies to the sector as a space of dimension $D/2$: the average of $n$ copies is the symmetriser of the sector over $\prod_{l<n}(D/2 + l)$, and $\mathrm{tr}\rho_{A}^{n}$ is the trace against the cyclic permutation of the $A$ factors. For $\sigma \in S_{n}$ the trace of $P_{\sigma}$ composed with that permutation over $n$ copies of the sector counts the basis labels $(\alpha_{r}, \beta_{r})$ with $\alpha$ constant on the cycles of $\sigma^{-1}\eta$, $\beta$ constant on those of $\sigma$ and $\alpha_{r}$, $\beta_{r}$ of equal parity for each $r$; the parity is then constant on the orbits of the group generated by $\sigma$ and $\sigma^{-1}\eta$, which contains $\eta$ and is transitive, so there are $2$ choices of parity and $(d_{A}/2)^{\#(\sigma^{-1}\eta)}(d_{B}/2)^{\#(\sigma)}$ labels for each. At $n = 2$: $2[(d_{A}/2)^{2}(d_{B}/2) + (d_{A}/2)(d_{B}/2)^{2}]/((D/2)(D/2 + 1)) = (d_{A} + d_{B})/(D + 2)$. For the sector average: the families containing $v$ are the families of $v^{\perp}/v$, $\prod_{r=1}^{m-1}(2^{r} + 1)$ of them; a string $x \notin \{0, v\}$ lies in such a family only if it is even, and then in a fraction $1/(D/2 + 1)$ of them; $V_{A}$ has $d_{A}^{2}/2 - 1$ nonzero even strings and does not contain $v$. So the mean of $|L_{A}|/d_{A}$ is $(1 + (d_{A}^{2}/2 - 1)/(D/2 + 1))/d_{A} = (d_{A} + d_{B})/(D + 2)$. For the third moment: two distinct nonzero even strings $x, y$ of $V_{A}$ with $b(x, y) = 0$ span with $v$ a three-dimensional subspace on which $b$ vanishes ($v \notin V_{A}$), and lie together in a fraction $1/((D/2 + 1)(D/4 + 1))$ of the sector families. On the $E = d_{A}^{2}/2$ even strings of $V_{A}$, $b(x, y) = |x \cap y|$ has radical spanned by the full string $v_{A}$ of $A$, so the number of ordered pairs of distinct commuting nonzero even strings is $(E - 2) + (E - 2)(E/2 - 2) = (E - 2)(E/2 - 1)$. With $\alpha = d_{A}/2$, $\beta = d_{B}/2$, $\Delta = D/2 = 2\alpha\beta$: $\langle|L_{A}|^{2}\rangle(\Delta + 1)(\Delta + 2) = (\Delta + 1)(\Delta + 2) + 3(2\alpha^{2} - 1)(\Delta + 2) + 4(\alpha^{2} - 1)^{2} = \Delta^{2} + 6\alpha^{2}\Delta + 4\alpha^{2} + 4\alpha^{4}$, and dividing by $d_{A}^{2} = 4\alpha^{2}$ gives $(\alpha^{2} + \beta^{2} + 3\alpha\beta + 1)/((\Delta + 1)(\Delta + 2))$, which is the sector's Haar value $2[\alpha\beta^{3} + \alpha^{3}\beta + 3\alpha^{2}\beta^{2} + \alpha\beta]/(\Delta(\Delta + 1)(\Delta + 2))$ and equals $(d_{A}^{2} + d_{B}^{2} + 3D + 4)/((D + 2)(D + 4))$. The sign of $h_{v}$ is fixed on the orbit because even quarter turns commute with $e_{v}$.

(v) The quarter turn about $e_{r}e_{j}$ sends a string to its image under the transposition $(r\,j)$ (it adds $\{r,j\}$ exactly when the string contains one of $r$, $j$), so bivector turns act through the symmetric group on the directions and the orbit of the family of the matching $\{1,2\},\dots$ is the set of matching families, $(2m - 1)!! = \prod_{r=1}^{m-1}(2r + 1)$. Since $2r + 1 = 2^{r} + 1$ for $r = 1, 2$ and $2r + 1 < 2^{r} + 1$ for $r \ge 3$, this equals $\prod_{r=1}^{m-1}(2^{r} + 1)$ exactly for $m \le 3$. Permutations preserve the size of a string, and the symmetric group is transitive on the strings of each size, so the orbits on the classes $\{x, x + v\}$ are exactly the size classes $\{2k, 2m - 2k\}$, $1 \le k \le \lfloor m/2\rfloor$: $\{2, 6\}$ and $\{4\}$ at $m = 4$, $\{2, 8\}$ and $\{4, 6\}$ at $m = 5$. For the last statement: $(1 + e_{w})(1 + e_{w})^{\sim} = 1 + e_{w}e_{w}^{\sim} + e_{w} + e_{w}^{\sim}$ is $2$ exactly when $e_{w}^{\sim} = -e_{w}$, and for these generators $e_{w}^{\sim} = (-1)^{q(w)}e_{w}$. For an even string, $q(x + v) = q(x) + q(v) + b(x, v) = q(x) + m \pmod 2$, since $q(v) = m(2m - 1)$ and $b(x, v) = |x|$: for $m$ odd one of $x$, $x + v$ has $q = 1$; for $m$ even $q$ is a function on classes, and a transvection about $w$ with $q(w) = 1$ preserves it, $q(x + w) = q(x) + q(w) + b(x, w) = q(x)$ when $b(x,w) = 1$. For even $m \ge 4$ both values occur (sizes $2$ and $4$).

(vi) A flat state of rank $2^{e}$ has entropy $e\ln 2$; the means follow from (i), and $\ln 2 = \sum_{k \ge 1}1/(k2^{k})$ lies between its twelfth partial sum and that sum plus $1/(13 \cdot 2^{12})$, inside $(\tfrac23, \tfrac{7}{10})$. Page's values are the formula of Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-page-average-entropy-subsystem}.

\emph{Comparison with the stored results.} Theorem \claimref{synthesis.eviction-keeps-one-replica-saddle}(iii), (iv) uses the mean purity only, which (ii) reproduces; Theorem \claimref{synthesis.eviction-keeps-one-of-catalan-many-replica-saddles}(iii), (iv) uses the moments at every index and their Catalan limit, which (iii) does not reproduce from $n = 4$; Theorem \claimref{synthesis.eviction-deficit-against-page-deficit} uses Page's average, which (vi) does not reproduce. The sector form of the crossing value follows from (iv) at $d_{A} = d_{B} = d$: $2d/(d^{2} + 2) = (2/d)/(1 + 2d^{-2})$.
\end{proof}

synthesis.half-integer-weight-array-carr.technical:
The weights $\omega_k = \kappa k$ of Premise (Q) are one of two evenly spaced, particle-hole symmetric ways to lay out the s-wave fermion array; the other shifts every weight by $\kappa/2$, so that the sea level falls between two modes and no mode has zero weight. The store's reformulation of the calibration residue showed that the first choice, read literally, misses the registered value: one array carries $\ln 2 + \varepsilon$ nats at the Hawking temperature, between $0.7203966$ and $0.7203967$.

For the second choice the array carries exactly $\tfrac12\ln 2$. The array's partition function at the Hawking temperature is the ratio $\vartheta_{3}/\eta$ at the point $\tau = I_4$, where the time after which the array's flow returns to itself equals the thermal period; that ratio is invariant under the exchange of the two periods, which removes the energy term from the entropy, and the classical theta identities give the ratio $\sqrt{2}$ there. Independently of those identities, rigorous rational bounds place the entropy within $10^{-57}$ of $\tfrac12\ln 2$. Under the entropy-matching hypothesis, two such arrays carry exactly the capacity of one registered boundary mode. The second choice also matches the series' account of why the spectrum is Fermi-Dirac: after one modular period its flow is minus the identity on the fermions, the sign one Euclidean period carries; its weights $\kappa(k + \tfrac12) = 2\pi T_{\mathrm{H}}(k + \tfrac12)$ are the fermionic Matsubara frequencies, while (Q)'s $\kappa k$ are the bosonic ones.
synthesis.half-integer-weight-array-carr.lay: The series models the quantum modes at a black hole's boundary as an evenly spaced ladder of energies, and one of its assumptions fixes where the ladder sits: with a rung at exactly zero energy. The other natural choice puts zero midway between two rungs. This result computes what that second choice would mean. At the Hawking temperature each ladder then holds exactly half a bit of entropy, a consequence of classical identities of special functions, so two ladders hold one bit, the amount the series assigns to each counted boundary mode; with the series' current choice no whole number of ladders matches. The second choice also fits the series' explanation of why the radiation obeys fermion statistics. It does not settle which choice nature makes or what is being counted.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} The array is that of Theorem \claimref{singularity.bosonisation-bridge-s-wave-sector}, with only its weights changed. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boundary-mode-thermal-entropy}, a mode of weight $\omega$ has entropy $s(x) = \ln(1 + e^{-x}) + x/(e^{x} + 1)$ with $x = 2\pi\omega/\kappa$, even in $x$, with $s(0) = \ln 2$. In the quasi-free state the array's state is the product of its marginals, so its entropy is the sum $S_{\delta} = \sum_{k}s(2\pi(k + \delta))$. For $\delta = \tfrac12$ the arguments are $\pm(2k + 1)\pi$, $k \geq 0$, each value twice, so $S_{1/2} = 2\sum_{k \geq 0}s((2k + 1)\pi)$; for $\delta = 0$ the argument $0$ occurs once and $\pm 2\pi k$, $k \geq 1$, twice, so $S_{0} = \ln 2 + 2\sum_{k \geq 1}s(2\pi k)$, the array sum of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy}(vi). The offsets $\delta = 0$ and $\delta = \tfrac12$ are the two for which $\omega_{k_{0} - k} = -\omega_{k}$ for some integer $k_{0}$ ($k_{0} = 0$ and $k_{0} = -1$), the condition for the particle-hole map $\psi_{k} \mapsto \psi_{k_{0} - k}^{\dagger}$ to commute with the flow.

\emph{(i), (ii): rigorous bounds.} Write $u = e^{-x}$, so $s = \ln(1 + u) + xu/(1 + u)$; both terms increase with $u$, and the second increases with $x$ at fixed $u$. The script bounds $\pi$ by Machin's formula $\pi = 16\arctan\tfrac15 - 4\arctan\tfrac{1}{239}$, each arctangent bracketed by consecutive partial sums of its alternating series; bounds $e^{\pi}$ by its Taylor polynomial of degree $119$ and the remainder bound $x^{N}/N!\,(1 - x/(N + 1))^{-1}$, hence $e^{-\pi}$ and $u = e^{-n\pi}$ by powers; bounds $\ln(1 + u)$ by consecutive partial sums of its alternating series; bounds $\ln 2 = \sum_{k \geq 1}1/(k2^{k})$ with tail at most $1/((N + 1)2^{N})$; and bounds the tail of the array sum beyond $26$ terms by $s(x) \le u + xu \le (1 + x)e^{-x}$, summed explicitly over $120$ further terms with a remainder $10^{-60}$ far above the true remainder. All rounding is outward to denominators $10^{70}$. The resulting interval for $S_{1/2}$ has width below $10^{-57}$ and lies within $10^{-57}$ of the interval for $\tfrac12\ln 2$, which is (i). The interval for $S_{0}$ lies in $(0.720396698946605, 0.720396698946606)$, which is (ii), and $1/(4S_{0})$ follows. For orientation (not part of the proof): $S_{1/2} = 0.346573590279972654708616060729\ldots$, and at slopes other than the one (R) and (Q) fix the half-offset sum is not $\tfrac12\ln 2$ (at $x_{k} = (k + \tfrac12)\pi$ it is $1.0275\ldots$, at $x_{k} = 4\pi(k + \tfrac12)$ it is $0.02715\ldots$).

\emph{(iii)} Under the hypothesis of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy}, $\sum s = A/4$ over the counted units, with the counted units taken to be whole arrays, each contributing $S_{\delta}$, the number of arrays is $A/(4S_{\delta})$, that is $1/(4S_{\delta})$ per Planck area per modular period. By (i), for $\delta = \tfrac12$ this is $1/(2\ln 2)$ up to a relative error below $10^{-56}$, which is twice $1/(4\ln 2)$, the capacity-convention residue, so two arrays carry $\ln 2$. For $\delta = 0$ the ratio to $1/(4\ln 2)$ is $\ln 2/S_{0} \in (0.96, 0.97)$, an interval containing no $p/q$ with $q \le 4$; the script checks this with the same bounds.

\emph{The sentence after (iii).} The flow acts by $\tau_{t}(\psi_{k}) = e^{-J\omega_{k}t}\psi_{k}$, with $J = e_2e_3$ the complex unit of the boundary modes, which commutes with the mode operators (\claimref{synthesis.transverse-bivector-is-the-complex-unit-of-the-radial-atom}), so at $t = 2\pi/\kappa$ it multiplies $\psi_{k}$ by $e^{-2\pi J(k + \delta)}$, which is $1$ for $\delta = 0$ and $-1$ for $\delta = \tfrac12$; the general classification is clause (iv) of the result filed alongside, synthesis.q-splits-maximum-entropy-affine-weights. By Proposition \claimref{state-selection.where-fermi-dirac-comes}, one Euclidean period is the rotor $R_{2\pi} = -1$, acting as $-1$ on the odd sector. The script checks $R_{2\pi} = -1$ in $\Cl(2, 0)$ as $R(\pi)^{2} = B^{2} = -1$ for the rotation bivector $B = e_{1}e_{2}$, and, on all $16$ basis states of a four-mode window, that $e^{2\pi JK}$ is $(-1)^{N}$ for the weights $j + \tfrac12$ and $1$ for the weights $j$.

\emph{(i), exact value.} The classical inputs, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-theta-function-identities} (Whittaker and Watson, Ch.~21; Mumford, Tata Lectures on Theta I), read as complex analysis of scalar functions with numbers in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$ (two units act in this proof, and are not identified: $J$ on the array's modes, $I_4$ in the theta functions, whose values here are real): with $q = e^{2\pi I_4\tau}$, $\eta = q^{1/24}\prod_{n \geq 1}(1 - q^{n})$, $\vartheta_{3} = \prod_{n \geq 1}(1 - q^{n})(1 + q^{n - 1/2})^{2}$, $\vartheta_{2} = 2q^{1/8}\prod_{n \geq 1}(1 - q^{n})(1 + q^{n})^{2}$, $\vartheta_{4} = \prod_{n \geq 1}(1 - q^{n})(1 - q^{n - 1/2})^{2}$; (a) $\vartheta_{3}(-1/\tau) = \sqrt{-I_4\tau}\,\vartheta_{3}(\tau)$, $\vartheta_{2}(-1/\tau) = \sqrt{-I_4\tau}\,\vartheta_{4}(\tau)$, $\eta(-1/\tau) = \sqrt{-I_4\tau}\,\eta(\tau)$; (b) $\vartheta_{3}^{4} = \vartheta_{2}^{4} + \vartheta_{4}^{4}$; (c) $\vartheta_{2}\vartheta_{3}\vartheta_{4} = 2\eta^{3}$. For $\delta = \tfrac12$ and slope $y$ (the occupations at $x_{k} = y(k + \tfrac12)$, $y = 2\pi$ here) the array is a product of modes with Boltzmann factors $e^{-y(n - 1/2)}$, $n \geq 1$, each value twice (particles above the sea, holes below), so with $\tau = I_4y/2\pi$ its grand-canonical partition function is $Z = \prod_{n \geq 1}(1 + q^{n - 1/2})^{2} = q^{1/24}\,\vartheta_{3}/\eta$. The entropy of a product of thermal modes is $S = (1 - y\,\partial_{y})\log Z$, and the factor $q^{1/24} = e^{-y/24}$ contributes $-y/24 + y/24 = 0$, so $S(y) = (1 - y\,\partial_{y})f(y)$ with $f(y) = \log(\vartheta_{3}/\eta)(I_4y/2\pi)$. By (a), $f(y) = f(4\pi^{2}/y)$; differentiating at the fixed point $y = 2\pi$ gives $f'(2\pi) = -f'(2\pi)$, so $f'(2\pi) = 0$ and $S_{1/2} = f(2\pi) = \log(\vartheta_{3}(I_4)/\eta(I_4))$. At $\tau = I_4$, (a) gives $\vartheta_{2}(I_4) = \vartheta_{4}(I_4)$, so (b) gives $\vartheta_{4}(I_4)^{2} = \vartheta_{3}(I_4)^{2}/\sqrt{2}$ (all three values are positive), and (c) gives $\vartheta_{3}(I_4)^{3}/\sqrt{2} = 2\eta(I_4)^{3}$, that is $\vartheta_{3}(I_4)/\eta(I_4) = \sqrt{2}$. Hence $S_{1/2} = \tfrac12\ln 2$. synthesis.hawking-page-test-on-schwarzsc.formal:
Let $\Lambda = -3/\ell^{2} < 0$, in units $\hbar = c = G = 1$, and for $M > 0$ consider the Schwarzschild-anti-de Sitter gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) in the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand gauge $\hb = 1 - \beta P$, $\beta^{2} = 2M/r - r^{2}/\ell^{2}$, whose static Killing field $K = \hb^{-1}(e_t)$ has $Q(K) = f(r) = 1 - 2M/r + r^{2}/\ell^{2}$. Write $r_{h}$ for a positive zero of $f$ and $x = r_{h}/\ell$. Suppose
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(T)] the horizon is at the temperature $T = f'(r_{h})/4\pi$ of the flow of $K$, the value that (R) gives at $\Lambda = 0$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.quarter-from-temperature}); for $\Lambda < 0$ no stored premise supplies it and it is assumed, as (T) is in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.sds-clausius-fixes-area-constant};
\item[(Cl)] the horizon obeys the Clausius relation $dM = T\,dS$ along the family at fixed $\Lambda$;
\item[(FE)] (Hawking and Page's criterion, not a stored premise) at a given temperature the field with the smaller free energy $F = M - TS$ is the equilibrium one, the horizonless field ($M = 0$, no horizon locus) being taken with $F = 0$.
\end{enumerate}
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(o)] \emph{(The chart.)} $\beta^{2} \ge 0$ exactly on $0 < r \le r_{*}$, with $r_{*}^{3} = 2M\ell^{2}$, where $Q(K) = 1$; so the gauge as stored does not cover $r > r_{*}$. $f$ is increasing with exactly one positive zero, and $r_{h} < \min(2M, r_{*})$: the horizon locus lies inside the chart, and every clause below uses only the horizon locus.
\item[(i)] \emph{(The quarter.)} $M = \tfrac12 r_{h}(1 + x^{2})$ and $4\pi T = (1 + 3x^{2})/r_{h}$. Under (T) and (Cl), $S = \pi r_{h}^{2} + c$ with $c$ independent of $M$, and (Z), $S \to 0$ as $M \to 0$, holds if and only if $c = 0$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The branches.)} $T \ge T_{\min} = \sqrt{3}/(2\pi\ell)$, with equality only at $x^{2} = \tfrac13$. For $T < T_{\min}$ there is no black hole; for $T > T_{\min}$ there are exactly two, a small one ($x^{2} < \tfrac13$, $dM/dT < 0$) and a large one ($x^{2} > \tfrac13$, $dM/dT > 0$).
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The transition under (Z).)} With $c = 0$, $F = \tfrac14 r_{h}(1 - x^{2})$: positive on the whole small branch, and on the large branch negative exactly when $r_{h} > \ell$. Under (FE) the horizonless field is the equilibrium one for $T < T_{\mathrm{HP}}$ and the large black hole for $T > T_{\mathrm{HP}}$, with
\[
T_{\mathrm{HP}} = \frac{1}{\pi\ell}, \qquad \frac{T_{\mathrm{HP}}}{T_{\min}} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}},
\]
the mass jumping from $0$ to $\ell$ and the entropy from $0$ to $\pi\ell^{2}$ (so $\Delta M = T_{\mathrm{HP}}\,\Delta S$). This is Hawking and Page's transition.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Dimension $d \ge 4$.)} For the field with $f = 1 - \mu/r^{d-3} + r^{2}/\ell^{2}$ on flat $\R^{1,d-1}$, assume (T), the entropy $S = \tfrac14\Omega_{d-2}r_{h}^{d-2}$ (a quarter of the area of the cross-section, $\Omega_{d-2}$ the area of the unit sphere) and let $M$ be the Clausius energy, $dM = T\,dS$ with $M = 0$ at $r_{h} = 0$. Then $4\pi T = \bigl((d-3) + (d-1)x^{2}\bigr)/r_{h}$, $16\pi M = (d-2)\Omega_{d-2}r_{h}^{d-3}(1 + x^{2})$ and
\[
F = \frac{\Omega_{d-2}\,r_{h}^{d-3}}{16\pi}\,(1 - x^{2}), \qquad T_{\min} = \frac{\sqrt{(d-1)(d-3)}}{2\pi\ell}, \qquad T_{\mathrm{HP}} = \frac{d-2}{2\pi\ell},
\]
the transition again at $r_{h} = \ell$. For $d = 5$: $T_{\min} = \sqrt{2}/(\pi\ell)$ and $T_{\mathrm{HP}} = 3/(2\pi\ell)$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Under the Wald constant.)} Assume in place of (Z) the hypothesis (W) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.euler-term-horizon-entropy-shift}(ii), the Wald entropy of the MacDowell-Mansouri action as written (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-wald-noether-charge-entropy}). Then $c = -3\pi\chi/2\Lambda = +\pi\ell^{2}$ ($\chi = 2$), $S \to \pi\ell^{2}$ as $M \to 0$, and
\[
F_{W} = F - \pi\ell^{2}\,T = -\,\frac{\ell\,(1 + x^{2})^{2}}{4x} < 0
\]
for every black hole of the family, on both branches. Under (FE) a black hole is then preferred to the horizonless field at every temperature at which one exists, $T \ge T_{\min}$, and nothing happens at $T = 1/(\pi\ell)$. Since $c > 0$, nonnegativity of the entropy does not exclude this constant for $\Lambda < 0$ (it does for $\Lambda > 0$, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.sds-clausius-fixes-area-constant}(v)); (Z) does. So for $\Lambda < 0$ Hawking and Page's transition is reproduced under (Z) and not under (W).
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.hawking-page-test-on-schwarzsc.technical:
The hypotheses of the stored Schwarzschild-de Sitter result, horizon temperature equal to surface gravity over $2\pi$ for the flow of the gauge's Killing field (T) and Hawking's Clausius relation along the family (Cl), are carried to $\Lambda < 0$, where the store had no black-hole result. The Painlev\'e-Gullstrand gauge with flat slices is real only out to the radius $r_{*}$ at which free fall from rest turns round, $r_{*}^{3} = 2M\ell^{2}$; the horizon locus is always inside it, which is all the result uses. (T) and (Cl) give a quarter of the area plus a constant, as for $\Lambda > 0$. The temperature has a minimum at $r_{h} = \ell/\sqrt{3}$, with a small branch of negative heat capacity and a large branch of positive heat capacity above it.

The additive constant is what the test discriminates. With the store's normalisation (Z), zero entropy at zero mass, the free energy $M - TS$ is $r_{h}(1 - r_{h}^{2}/\ell^{2})/4$, it changes sign at $r_{h} = \ell$, and with Hawking and Page's comparison of free energies (a hypothesis here, labelled (FE)) the transition sits at $T = 1/(\pi\ell)$; in five dimensions the same computation gives $3/(2\pi\ell)$ and $T_{\min} = \sqrt{2}/(\pi\ell)$, the standard values. With the Wald entropy of the series' action as written, the Euler term adds $+\pi\ell^{2}$, the free energy of every black hole is negative, and the transition at $r_{h} = \ell$ disappears. For $\Lambda > 0$ that constant was negative and excluded by nonnegativity; for $\Lambda < 0$ it is positive and only (Z), or the transition itself, speaks against it.

Scope: (T) is assumed, not derived, for $\Lambda < 0$; (FE) is not a stored premise; the series' frozen point has $\Lambda > 0$, so this is a test of the horizon thermodynamics on a field the series does not say is realised. The quarter follows from (T) and (Cl) alone, so the test does not reach the series' density of counted boundary modes.
synthesis.hawking-page-test-on-schwarzsc.lay: In a universe with a negative cosmological constant, a famous calculation by Hawking and Page shows that hot radiation suddenly prefers to become a large black hole once the temperature passes a definite value. This result checks whether the framework's rules for horizon temperature and entropy, which were set up for our universe and for ordinary black holes, give the same answer when applied there. Assuming the usual temperature of a horizon, the ordinary law linking heat and entropy, and Hawking and Page's rule that the state of lower free energy wins, they do, in four dimensions and in five: black holes exist only above a minimum temperature, come in a small unstable kind and a large stable kind, and the large kind takes over at exactly the standard temperature. The check is not strong evidence for the framework, because any theory with the usual temperature and heat law passes it. What it does decide is a detail the framework had already had to settle: its own form of the gravitational action, read literally, adds a fixed amount of entropy to every black hole, and with that extra amount the transition would not occur where Hawking and Page found it. The framework's choice to leave that amount out is the one that gives the standard result.

proofs.main:
\emph{(o).} $\beta^{2} = (2M\ell^{2} - r^{3})/(r\ell^{2})$ is nonnegative on $r > 0$ exactly for $r^{3} \le 2M\ell^{2} = r_{*}^{3}$, and $Q(K) = 1 - \beta^{2}$ in this gauge (the form of the gauge and of $K$ are those of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.sds-clausius-fixes-area-constant}, with the sign of the $r^{2}/\ell^{2}$ term reversed), so $Q(K) = f$ and $Q(K) = 1$ at $r_{*}$. $f'(r) = 2M/r^{2} + 2r/\ell^{2} > 0$, $f \to -\infty$ as $r \to 0$ and $f \to +\infty$ as $r \to \infty$, so there is exactly one positive zero $r_{h}$. At it $\beta^{2} = 1 - f = 1 > 0$, so $r_{h} < r_{*}$ since $\beta^{2}$ is decreasing; and $2M/r_{h} = 1 + r_{h}^{2}/\ell^{2} > 1$ gives $r_{h} < 2M$.

\emph{(i).} $f(r_{h}) = 0$ is $2M = r_{h}(1 + r_{h}^{2}/\ell^{2})$, and substituting it in $f'$ gives $f'(r_{h}) = r_{h}^{-1}(1 + 3r_{h}^{2}/\ell^{2})$. Along the family at fixed $\ell$, $r_{h}$ is an increasing function of $M$ with $dM/dr_{h} = \tfrac12(1 + 3x^{2})$, and by (T), $T\,d(\pi r_{h}^{2}) = \tfrac{1}{4\pi}r_{h}^{-1}(1 + 3x^{2})\,2\pi r_{h}\,dr_{h} = dM$. So $S = \pi r_{h}^{2}$ satisfies (Cl), and since (Cl) fixes $dS/dr_{h}$ on the connected interval $M > 0$, every solution is $\pi r_{h}^{2} + c$. As $M \to 0$, $r_{h} < 2M \to 0$, so $S \to c$. At $\ell \to \infty$ this is the computation of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.quarter-from-temperature}.

\emph{(ii).} $4\pi\ell T = \tau(x) := (1 + 3x^{2})/x$, with $\tau'(x) = (3x^{2} - 1)/x^{2}$ and $\tau^{2} - 12 = (1 - 3x^{2})^{2}/x^{2} \ge 0$. So $\tau$ decreases from $+\infty$ on $0 < x < 1/\sqrt{3}$ to its minimum $2\sqrt{3}$ and increases to $+\infty$ beyond: each value above the minimum is taken exactly twice, once on each side. Since $dM/dx > 0$, the sign of $dM/dT$ is the sign of $\tau'$.

\emph{(iii).} $F = M - TS = \tfrac12 r_{h}(1 + x^{2}) - \tfrac{1}{4}r_{h}(1 + 3x^{2}) = \tfrac14 r_{h}(1 - x^{2})$. On the small branch $x^{2} < \tfrac13 < 1$, so $F > 0$; on the large branch $F < 0$ exactly for $x > 1$. $\tau(1) = 4$ gives $T_{\mathrm{HP}} = 1/(\pi\ell)$, above $T_{\min}$ by the factor $4/2\sqrt{3}$. Under (FE) the equilibrium field at temperature $T$ is the one of least $F$ among the horizonless field ($F = 0$) and the black holes at that temperature: for $T < T_{\mathrm{HP}}$ every black hole has $F > 0$ (the large one because $\tau$ is increasing there, so $T < T_{\mathrm{HP}}$ is $x < 1$), and for $T > T_{\mathrm{HP}}$ the large one has $F < 0$. At $x = 1$, $M = \ell$ and $S = \pi\ell^{2}$.

\emph{(iv).} The zero of $f$ gives $\mu = r_{h}^{d-3}(1 + x^{2})$ and $f'(r_{h}) = (d-3)\mu/r_{h}^{d-2} + 2r_{h}/\ell^{2} = r_{h}^{-1}\bigl((d-3) + (d-1)x^{2}\bigr)$. With $dS/dr_{h} = \tfrac14(d-2)\Omega_{d-2}r_{h}^{d-3}$, $T\,dS = \tfrac{(d-2)\Omega_{d-2}}{16\pi}\bigl((d-3)r_{h}^{d-4} + (d-1)r_{h}^{d-2}/\ell^{2}\bigr)dr_{h}$, whose integral from $0$ is the stated $M$. Then $16\pi F/\Omega_{d-2}r_{h}^{d-3} = (d-2)(1 + x^{2}) - (d-3) - (d-1)x^{2} = 1 - x^{2}$. The minimum of $\bigl((d-3) + (d-1)x^{2}\bigr)/x$ is at $x^{2} = (d-3)/(d-1)$, with value $2\sqrt{(d-1)(d-3)}$, below the zero of $F$ at $x = 1$, where $4\pi\ell T = 2(d-2)$; the argument of (ii) and (iii) applies unchanged.

\emph{(v).} By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.euler-term-horizon-entropy-shift}(ii), which holds on both branches of $\Lambda$ and rests on Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-wald-noether-charge-entropy}, under (W) a spherical cross-section has $S = A/4 - 3\pi\chi/2\Lambda$ with $\chi = 2$, that is $c = \pi\ell^{2}$, a constant of the kind allowed by (i). Then $F_{W} = \tfrac14 r_{h}(1 - x^{2}) - \tfrac14\ell^{2}r_{h}^{-1}(1 + 3x^{2}) = -\tfrac{\ell}{4x}\bigl(x^{4} + 2x^{2} + 1\bigr)$, negative for every $x > 0$. So under (FE) each black hole has lower free energy than the horizonless field, on both branches, and $F_{W}$ has no zero. At equal temperature the two radii satisfy $x_{s}x_{l} = \tfrac13$ (the two roots of $3x^{2} - \tau x + 1 = 0$), and with $g(x) = (1 + x^{2})^{2}/x$ one has $g(x_{l}) - g(x_{s}) = (3x_{l}^{2} - 1)^{3}/27x_{l}^{3} > 0$, so the large black hole has the lower $F_{W}$. The constant is positive, so $S \ge 0$ places no restriction on it; $S \to \pi\ell^{2} \ne 0$ as $M \to 0$ violates (Z).

\emph{Orientation, not used.} With $\beta = 1/T$, the script confirms $\beta F_{W} = -\tfrac{\ell^{2}}{64\pi}\,\beta\cdot 4\pi\!\int_{r_{h}}^{\infty}\!\tfrac{48M^{2}}{r^{6}}\,r^{2}dr$ for every sampled $x$: the Wald free energy is, up to that factor, the integral of the square of the Weyl part $48M^{2}/r^{6}$ of the field strength over the Euclidean exterior, which is what an action that is a square of the Cartan curvature evaluates to on a field whose Cartan curvature is its Weyl part. The coefficient $\tfrac{1}{64\pi}$ is matched, not derived, here.

The script checks exactly, at six rational horizon radii and four values of $\ell$: the zero of $f$, its monotonicity at sample points, $\beta^{2} = 1$ at the horizon locus and $r_{h}^{3} < r_{*}^{3}$, the temperature and the Clausius identity as rational functions; the sign of $\tau'$ on each branch, the identity $\tau^{2} - 12 = (1 - 3x^{2})^{2}/x^{2}$, the free energy and its sign and zero; for $d = 4, \dots, 7$ the Clausius energy, the free energy and the values at $x = 1$ and at the minimum; the Wald constant from $\chi = 2$ and $\Lambda = -3/\ell^{2}$, the closed form and sign of $F_{W}$, and the orientation identity.

check_branches_and_free_energy.omits: Sign of the derivative of 4 pi ell T at three points on each branch, the identity tau^2 - 12 = (1 - 3x^2)^2/x^2 at five points, F and its sign and zero at six points, the values at x = 1; (FE) is a hypothesis and is not tested; "exactly two black holes" is the proof's monotonicity argument

check_dimension_d.omits: d = 4 to 7 only, at the sample radii; the entropy r^{d-2}/4 per unit of sphere area is assumed as in the statement; the minimum is tested by its value at x^2 = (d-3)/(d-1), not as a minimum

synthesis.hole-mass-is-ground-energy-lab.technical: The energy tension says that counted modes holding the entropy $A/4$ carry less than $TS = M/2$ of Killing energy, and none at the registered zero weight, so something else must carry the hole's mass $M$. This result treats the hole at fixed mass as a thermal (Gibbs) state of some Hamiltonian at the series' temperature, with mean energy $M$ and entropy $A/4$. The free energy is then $M - TS = M/2$, so the partition function is $e^{-A/4}$, less than one. A Hamiltonian whose lowest energy is zero always has partition function at least one, so the Hamiltonian must contain a positive constant, its ground energy, larger than $M/2$. The excitations above that ground carry less than $M/2$; at zero weight they carry nothing and the ground energy is all of $M$. Because a fixed Hamiltonian's mean energy falls as the inverse temperature rises, while the hole's mass rises with it (the familiar negative heat capacity), the ground energy must change with the mass: it behaves as a label of the state. The partition function $e^{-A/4}$ is the Gibbons-Hawking value of the Euclidean action; what is new is the reading of it as a lower bound $M/2$ on the ground energy, reached by nothing and approached by the excitations only from below, with the whole mass in the ground energy exactly at zero weight. The bound does not depend on the ordering chosen for the counted modes' generator.
synthesis.hole-mass-is-ground-energy-lab.lay: A black hole has a temperature, an entropy and a mass. The series' counted boundary modes can hold all of the entropy, but in its favoured case they carry no energy at all, which raised the question of where the mass lives. If the hole is assumed to be an ordinary system in thermal equilibrium at its own temperature (the result's hypothesis), that answers it: the numbers force more than half of the mass, and in the favoured case all of it, to be a fixed baseline energy of the whole system rather than the energy of any particles or excitations. That baseline grows with the hole, so it acts like a label saying which hole this is. No collection of particles at the hole's temperature holding at most the hole's entropy, outside or at the boundary, can supply half the mass or more.

proofs.main:
Throughout, $T = 1/8\pi M$ and $S = 4\pi M^{2} = A/4$ are those of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.quarter-from-temperature}, so $TS = M/2$ and $\beta = 8\pi M$.

\textbf{(i).} For a Gibbs state $\varrho = e^{-\beta H}/Z$ with $e^{-\beta H}$ of trace class, $-\ln\varrho = \beta H + \ln Z$, so $S(\varrho) = -\tr\varrho\ln\varrho = \beta\langle H\rangle + \ln Z$ (on finite blocks this is the Gibbs form of Theorem \claimref{singularity.kms-uniqueness-factor}). With $\langle H_M\rangle = M$ and $S = A/4$: $\ln Z_M = A/4 - \beta M = 4\pi M^{2} - 8\pi M^{2} = -4\pi M^{2} = -A/4$, and $F := -T\ln Z_M = M/2 = M - TS$. This is the Gibbons-Hawking value: their Euclidean action of the Schwarzschild section is $I = \beta M/2 = 4\pi M^{2}$ and $\ln Z = -I$ (G.\,W.~Gibbons and S.\,W.~Hawking, Phys.\ Rev.\ D 15 (1977) 2752, cited from memory); the content here is only its rewriting in the series' variables.

\textbf{(ii).} Since $H_M = E_0 + H'_M$, $Z_M = e^{-\beta E_0}Z'_M$ and $\langle H_M\rangle = E_0 + \langle H'_M\rangle$. The Gibbs identity for $H'_M$ (the same state) gives $S = \beta\langle H'_M\rangle + \ln Z'_M$. As $H'_M \geq 0$ with $0$ in its spectrum and $e^{-\beta H'_M}$ trace class, $0$ is an eigenvalue of finite multiplicity $g_0 \geq 1$ and $Z'_M = g_0 + \sum_{\lambda > 0}g_\lambda e^{-\beta\lambda} \geq 1$, with equality only if the spectrum is the single nondegenerate eigenvalue $0$; then $\varrho_M$ is pure and $S = 0$, contradicting $S = A/4 > 0$. Hence $Z'_M > 1$, $\ln Z'_M > 0$, and $\beta\langle H'_M\rangle = S - \ln Z'_M < S$, that is $\langle H'_M\rangle < TS = M/2$; so $E_0 = M - \langle H'_M\rangle > M/2$, while $\langle H'_M\rangle \geq 0$ gives $E_0 \leq M$. Equivalently $E_0 = F + T\ln Z'_M > F = M/2$. The same identity applied to any sector whose Hamiltonian has ground energy $0$, in a Gibbs state at $\beta$, gives energy $< T\cdot(\text{its entropy})$; with entropy at most $A/4$ this is $< M/2$. For one fermion mode of weight $\omega$ it is the inequality $\beta\omega n < s(x)$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy}(v), $s(x) - x\,n(x) = \ln(1 + e^{-x}) > 0$ by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boundary-mode-thermal-entropy}. In the symmetric ordering $\omega(N - \tfrac12)$ the mode carries $\beta E = x(n - \tfrac12)$; with $u = e^{-x}$, $n - \tfrac12 = -(1 - u)/(2(1 + u)) = -\tfrac12\tanh\tfrac{x}{2}$, so $\beta E = -\tfrac{x}{2}\tanh\tfrac{x}{2} \leq 0 < s(x)$; the change of ordering is the constant shift $E_0 \mapsto E_0 - \omega/2$, which leaves $\langle H_M\rangle$, $S$ and the bounds on $E_0$ for the given $H_M$ unchanged.

\textbf{(iii).} $E_0 = M$ if and only if $\langle H'_M\rangle = 0$; since $\varrho_M$ is faithful on the range of $e^{-\beta H_M}$ (every eigenvector has positive weight), $\tr(\varrho_M H'_M) = 0$ with $H'_M \geq 0$ forces $H'_M = 0$, so $H_M = E_0$ on the support. For $H_M = E_0 + \sum_j\omega_jv_j^{*}v_j$ on the Fock space of $J$, the Gibbs state is the product of the single-mode Gibbs states (the marginals of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boundary-mode-thermal-entropy}), $\langle H'_M\rangle = E = \sum_j\omega_jn_j$ and $E_0 = M - E$. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy}(ii) the equality case $\kappa_c = 1/(4\ln 2)$ is all $\omega_j = 0$, which is $H'_M = 0$, $E = 0$, $E_0 = M$, $Z'_M = 2^{|J|}$, $S = |J|\ln 2$; then $\ln Z_M = -\beta E_0 + |J|\ln 2 = -S$ gives $\beta E_0 = 2|J|\ln 2 = 2S$, the Smarr relation $M = 2TS$ for the ground energy. At positive weights $Z'_M = \prod_j(1 + e^{-x_j}) > 1$ and $E > 0$, so $M/2 < E_0 < M$.

\textbf{(iv).} By (ii), $M/2 < E_0(M) \leq M$ for every $M$, so $E_0(M) \to 0$ as $M \to 0$ and $E_0(M) \to \infty$ as $M \to \infty$; no constant satisfies both bounds on $(0, \infty)$. For a fixed $H$ with $e^{-\beta H}$ trace class on an interval of $\beta$, $\frac{d}{d\beta}\langle H\rangle_\beta = -(\langle H^{2}\rangle_\beta - \langle H\rangle_\beta^{2}) \leq 0$ (differentiate $\tr(He^{-\beta H})/\tr e^{-\beta H}$), whereas along the family $M = \beta/8\pi$ increases with $\beta$; so no fixed Hamiltonian has $\langle H\rangle_\beta = M(\beta)$ on any interval, and $H_M$ depends on $M$. This is the standard negative heat capacity of the Schwarzschild family (Hawking, 1976, cited from memory), $dM/dT = -1/(8\pi T^{2})$, read as a statement about the Hamiltonian: the dependence on $M$ cannot be absorbed into a fixed dynamics and is a dependence on the state's label.

\textbf{Check.} The script verifies, in exact rational-function arithmetic in $u = e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$, that $Z' > 1$ on $(0, 1)$ for spectra with more than one state (one fermion mode, the Fock space of weights $1, 2$, a truncated oscillator, a degenerate ground) and $Z' = 1$ for a single nondegenerate level; the variance identity $u\,d\langle H\rangle/du = \operatorname{Var}(H)$ with $\operatorname{Var} > 0$ on $(0, 1)$, which is $d\langle H\rangle/d\beta = -\varepsilon\operatorname{Var} < 0$; the zero-weight sector $Z' = 2^{|J|}$, $\langle H'\rangle = 0$ for $|J| = 1, \ldots, 6$ with $e^{-\beta E_0} = (e^{-S})^{2} = 4^{-|J|}$; and $Z' = (1 + u)(1 + u^{2})$, $\langle H'\rangle > 0$ at weights $1, 2$; and the symmetric-ordering identity $n - \tfrac12 = -(1 - u)/(2(1 + u))$ with $n - \tfrac12 < 0$ on $(0, 1)$. The analytic step (the Gibbs identity) is in the text; positivity on $(0, 1)$ is certified by Bernstein coefficients.

synthesis.imported-gibbons-hawking-entro.formal:
In units $\hbar = c = k_{B} = 1$, the event horizon of a static observer in the de Sitter gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) of Hubble rate $H = \sqrt{\Lambda/3}$ has the entropy
\[
S_{\Lambda} \;=\; \frac{A_{\Lambda}}{4G}, \qquad A_{\Lambda} \;=\; \frac{4\pi}{H^{2}},
\]
a quarter of the area of a cross-section of the cosmological horizon locus $r = 1/H$ in the static Painlev\'e-Gullstrand chart of de Sitter space ($\hb = 1 - \beta P$, $\beta = -rH$, the expanding chart, whose free-fall observers have $dr/dt = Hr$ and which contains the static observer's future horizon), of area $4\pi/H^{2}$, on which the static Killing field is null and normal with surface gravity $H$, in Planck units, at the temperature $H/2\pi$ \cite{GibbonsHawking1977cosmo}.

The bifurcation surface itself, where the boost flow has its fixed points, lies beyond one flat chart (it is the meeting of the four regions of the maximal extension); the chart contains the future horizon, on whose cross-sections the area, the surface gravity and the boost flow are those stated.
synthesis.imported-gibbons-hawking-entro.technical: Gibbons and Hawking showed that the horizon of an observer in de Sitter space carries thermodynamics like a black hole's: the temperature $H/2\pi$ and an entropy equal to a quarter of the horizon's area in Planck units. In Gauge Theory Gravity the de Sitter field on flat spacetime has, in its static Painlev\'e-Gullstrand chart, a horizon locus at $r = 1/H$; each cross-section of it is a sphere of radius $1/H$, so its area is $4\pi/H^{2}$, and there the static Killing field is null with surface gravity $H$. The bifurcation sphere itself lies beyond one flat chart; the chart's cross-sections carry the same area.
synthesis.imported-gibbons-hawking-entro.lay: In a universe with a positive cosmological constant, each observer's horizon behaves like the surface of a black hole: it has a temperature and an entropy, and the entropy is a quarter of the horizon's area measured in the smallest natural units of area. This is a standard result of 1977, taken here from the literature.

imported_from.citation: G. W. Gibbons and S. W. Hawking, Cosmological event horizons, thermodynamics, and particle creation, Phys. Rev. D 15 (1977), 2738--2751.

synthesis.imported-haar-moments-of-rando.formal:
Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a unit vector of $\C^{D}$ (an abstract Hilbert space, its numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$, conventions U1; the source writes the complex numbers for that field) drawn from the unitarily invariant probability measure. For every $n \ge 1$,
\[
\bigl\langle (\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})^{\otimes n} \bigr\rangle \;=\; \frac{\Pi_{\mathrm{sym}}}{\dim \mathrm{Sym}^{n}\C^{D}} \;=\; \frac{\sum_{\sigma \in S_{n}} P_{\sigma}}{D(D + 1)\cdots(D + n - 1)},
\]
with $P_{\sigma}$ the operator permuting the $n$ tensor factors: the average commutes with $U^{\otimes n}$ for every unitary $U$ and is supported on the symmetric power, which is irreducible under $U(D)$ (Schur-Weyl duality), so by Schur's lemma it is the normalised projection onto it. Consequently, for $D = d_{A}d_{B}$ and $\rho_{A} = \operatorname{Tr}_{B}\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}$,
\[
\bigl\langle \operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{n} \bigr\rangle \;=\; \frac{\sum_{\sigma \in S_{n}} d_{A}^{\#(\sigma^{-1}\eta)}\, d_{B}^{\#(\sigma)}}{D(D + 1)\cdots(D + n - 1)},
\]
with $\eta$ the cyclic permutation $(1\,2\,\cdots\,n)$ and $\#(\cdot)$ the number of cycles. At $n = 2$ the average is $(\mathbb{1} + F)/(D(D + 1))$, $F$ the swap of the two copies, and the mean purity is
\[
\bigl\langle \operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2} \bigr\rangle \;=\; \frac{d_{A} + d_{B}}{d_{A}d_{B} + 1}, \qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad \bigl\langle \operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A} - \mathbb{1}/d_{A})^{2} \bigr\rangle \;=\; \frac{d_{A}^{2} - 1}{d_{A}(d_{A}d_{B} + 1)},
\]
symmetric in $d_{A}$ and $d_{B}$, for all dimensions $d_{A}, d_{B} \geq 1$: the classical value of Lubkin \cite{Lubkin1978}, prior art, imported here as the case $n = 2$. For $d_{A}$, $d_{B}$ powers of two the same value is derived in the store as a finite average (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.quarter-turn-rotors-of-the-even-subalgebra-form-a-state-design-of-order-three}); for other dimensions it rests on this Fact. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Chapter 9]{GoodmanWallach2009}; \cite{Harrow2013}; \cite{Lubkin1978} for $n = 2$.
synthesis.imported-haar-moments-of-rando.technical: For a random pure state of a large system, the average of $n$ copies of its projector is fixed by symmetry: it commutes with every unitary acting the same way on each copy and lives on the symmetric part of the $n$-fold product, which is irreducible, so it is the projector onto that part divided by its dimension, a sum over all permutations of the copies. Splitting the system in two and taking the partial trace turns each permutation into a power of the two dimensions, counted by cycles, which gives every Renyi moment of a random subsystem. The first case, two copies, is the mean purity $(d_{A} + d_{B})/(d_{A}d_{B} + 1)$ of a part, computed by Lubkin in 1978: it lies between $1/\min(d_{A}, d_{B})$, the value for a maximally mixed smaller part, and $1/d_{A} + 1/d_{B}$, and is the second-moment counterpart of Page's average entropy. The store derives that value by a finite average when both dimensions are powers of two and takes it from this Fact otherwise; it is the random-state reference of the abstract tensor-product column in the comparison of the eviction mechanism with the replica-wormhole computation.
synthesis.imported-haar-moments-of-rando.lay: If you pick a quantum state of a large system completely at random, the average amount of entanglement between two of its parts can be computed exactly. Symmetry does all the work: the answer is a sum over the ways of reshuffling copies of the state, each weighted by the sizes of the two parts. This is the standard formula behind Page's result on the entropy of a random subsystem.

imported_from.citation: R. Goodman and N. R. Wallach, Symmetry, Representations, and Invariants, Graduate Texts in Mathematics 255, Springer (2009), Chapter 9 (Schur-Weyl duality).
A. W. Harrow, The church of the symmetric subspace, arXiv:1308.6595 (2013).
E. Lubkin, Entropy of an n-system from its correlation with a k-reservoir, J. Math. Phys. 19 (1978), 1028.
