synthesis.light-ray-good-part-of-a-spino.technical:
The registered residue holds, at the weights $\kappa(k + \tfrac12)$ of Premise (Q) version 3, exactly when a counted unit is two s-wave arrays, and the store had no reason why arrays come in pairs. This result looks at where the arrays come from. (Q) version 3 reads its offset from the boundary modes being spinor fields of boost weight $\tfrac12$ on the horizon's light rays. In the spacetime algebra a spinor is an even multivector acted on from one side by rotors. On the horizon's null plane, with generators along $k$ and second null direction $m$, the flux of the Dirac current through the plane is twice the squared norm of $\Lambda(m)\psi$, $\Lambda(m) = m\gamma_{0}/2$: that half of the spinor, of real dimension four, is the canonical part on the plane, and the other half, the spinor of plane waves moving along $k$, carries no flux there. The boost of the generator scales the canonical values by the square root of the inverse of its factor on $k$, which together with the stretching of the affine parameter is the unitary dilation of weight $\tfrac12$, the boost of the series' continuum carrier.

The chirality splits the canonical part into two complex channels, one of each chirality. On these channels the rotation about the generators acts as minus the chirality: helicity about the generator direction is minus the chirality, an algebraic identity there and false on the whole spinor. Hence one massless species with both chiralities, a Dirac field, gives two channels on each light ray, of opposite helicities, and a Weyl field gives one. With one array per channel, two arrays carry exactly $\ln 2$ at the Hawking temperature. Counting per light ray, with the counted unit a bookkeeping total over all the horizon's fields, the registered unit of $\ln 2$ is two arrays of the total, and one Dirac species is exactly one unit. Vector fields, acted on by conjugation, carry integer weights and so would give the other offset.
synthesis.light-ray-good-part-of-a-spino.lay: The series counts quantum modes on a black hole's horizon, and it needs each counted unit to hold exactly one bit of entropy. With its current assumption about the modes' energies, one ladder of modes holds half a bit, so a counted unit must be two ladders, and nothing explained why. This result traces the ladders to the particles that would carry them. Particles of spin one half, like electrons and neutrinos, are described by spinors. On the surface swept out by the horizon's light rays only half of a spinor's components carry particles across it, and those split into two channels, the two handednesses of the particle, with the spin about the light rays fixed by the handedness. So a spin-one-half particle that has both handednesses, as the electron does, supplies exactly two ladders per light ray, one bit; a particle with one handedness only supplies half a bit. The horizon's total is then counted in bits, two ladders to a bit, over all its fields.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} Every statement is about linear maps and quadratic forms on the real vector space $\Cl^{+}(1,3)$ with basis $1$, $\gamma_{0}\gamma_{i}$, $\gamma_{i}\gamma_{j}$ ($i < j$), $I$. The script builds the $8 \times 8$ rational matrices of $L_{B}$, $L_{J}$, $L_{I}$, $L_{m}$ (into the odd part), $i_{H} = R_{I\sigma_{3}}$, $\Gamma$, of the projectors $\Lambda(k) = \tfrac12(1 + L_{B})$, $\Lambda(m) = \tfrac12(1 - L_{B})$, and the Gram matrices of the flux forms $\psi \mapsto \langle\psi\gamma_{0}\tilde{\psi}a\rangle_{0}$ for $a = k, m$. It decides each identity and each dimension by exact rank computation. A rotor carrying $\gamma_{0} \pm \gamma_{3}$ to another pair of null directions conjugates every map below to the corresponding map and preserves ranks, so the choice of $k$ and $m$ is no loss.

\emph{(i).} The algebra of this clause is Theorem \claimref{synthesis.canonical-part-of-a-spinor-on-a-null-plane}, clauses (i) and (ii), where its argument (formerly given here) now stands: $k\gamma_{0} = 1 + B$ and $m\gamma_{0} = 1 - B$, so $\Lambda(k) = \tfrac12(1 + B)$ and $\Lambda(m) = \tfrac12(1 - B)$ (Theorem \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(1) at $a_{0} = 1$); the Gram matrix of $\psi \mapsto J_{\psi}\cdot k$ is $2\Lambda(m)^{T}\Lambda(m)$ exactly, so $J_{\psi}\cdot k = 2|\Lambda(m)\psi|^{2}$, positive definite on the image of $\Lambda(m)$ (rank $4$) and zero on that of $\Lambda(k)$, and the flux through $N_{m}$ is $2|\Lambda(k)\psi|^{2}$; $\ker L_{m}$ and the $(-1)$-eigenspace of $L_{B}$ coincide, of dimension $4$. The script of this result still recomputes these identities. The canonical anticommutator of a spinor field on $N_{k}$ is the one of the components that carry the flux through $N_{k}$; this is the content of clause (i) of the result filed alongside, synthesis.boost-evolution-on-generators-is-one-unitary-group, which compresses the stored anticommutator $\chi(\nabla D)\gamma_{0}$ (Theorem \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(2)) to $\Lambda(m)$ and finds only the derivative along the generators, so $\Lambda(m)\psi$ is the canonical component with kernel a multiple of $\delta(u - v)\delta^{2}(x_{\perp} - y_{\perp})\Lambda(m)$. The spinor $\Lambda(k)$ of a plane wave of momentum $k$ (Theorem \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(1)) is constant along the generators of $N_{k}$, and its canonical data live on $N_{m}$. (This is the good component of light-front quantisation, Kogut and Soper, cited from memory as orientation.)

\emph{(ii).} With $B_{\lambda} = c + sB$, $c = \cosh\tfrac{\lambda}{2}$, $s = \sinh\tfrac{\lambda}{2}$, $B_{\lambda}\psi = (c \mp s)\psi$ on the $\mp1$ eigenspaces of $L_{B}$, that is $e^{-\lambda/2}$ on the image of $\Lambda(m)$ and $e^{\lambda/2}$ on that of $\Lambda(k)$. The script takes $c = \tfrac54$, $s = \tfrac34$ ($e^{\lambda/2} = 2$), checks $B_{\lambda}\tilde{B}_{\lambda} = 1$ and $B_{\lambda}k\tilde{B}_{\lambda} = 4k = e^{\lambda}k$, and checks $L_{B_{\lambda}}\Lambda(m) = \tfrac12\Lambda(m)$ and $L_{B_{\lambda}}\Lambda(k) = 2\Lambda(k)$ as matrix identities. The covariant action $\psi(x) \mapsto B_{\lambda}\psi(\tilde{B}_{\lambda}xB_{\lambda})$ transports the generator's affine parameter by $u \mapsto e^{-\lambda}u$, which multiplies $\delta(u - v)$ by $e^{\lambda}$. The anticommutator of the transformed field is therefore multiplied by the square of the value factor times $e^{\lambda}$: $(c - s)^{2}e^{\lambda} = 1$ on $\Lambda(m)$ and $(c + s)^{2}e^{\lambda} = e^{2\lambda}$ on $\Lambda(k)$ (the script: $1$ and $16$). On the canonical part the action is the unitary dilation $\psi_{m}(u) \mapsto e^{-\lambda/2}\psi_{m}(e^{-\lambda}u)$, and at $\lambda = -\kappa t$, with the inverse rotor acting on values by $e^{+\kappa t/2}$ (checked), it is the carrier's boost $\beta_{t}(\psi(u)) = e^{\kappa t/2}\psi(e^{\kappa t}u)$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-vacuum-on-a-horizon-generator}(i), whose weight $\tfrac12$ is the one that preserves the anticommutator. The same factorisation is clause (ii) of the result filed alongside.

\emph{(iii).} $\Gamma^{2}\psi = I(I\psi I\sigma_{3})I\sigma_{3} = I^{2}\psi(I\sigma_{3})^{2} = \psi$, since $I$ is central in $\Cl^{+}(1,3)$ (Theorem \claimref{field-theory.where-each-lives}(1)) and $I^{2} = (I\sigma_{3})^{2} = -1$. Left and right multiplications commute, and $I$ is central in the even subalgebra, so $\Gamma$ commutes with every $L_{X}$, $X$ even (the script checks all eight basis elements), with $R_{I\sigma_{3}}$ and with $L_{I}$. Both units square to $-1$ (checked). By exact rank, $\ker(\Gamma \mp 1)$ has real dimension $4$ and its intersection with the $(-1)$-eigenspace of $L_{B}$ has real dimension $2$ for each sign. Each intersection is invariant under both units, so it is one complex dimension under either.

\emph{(iv).} $IB = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}\gamma_{3}\gamma_{0} = -\gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\gamma_{0} = -\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}$, so $J = -IB$ (checked). On all of $\Cl^{+}(1,3)$, $\Gamma i_{H}\psi = I(\psi I\sigma_{3})I\sigma_{3} = -I\psi$, so $\Gamma i_{H} = -L_{I}$. On the $(-1)$-eigenspace of $L_{B}$, $L_{J}\psi = -IB\psi = I\psi$, so $L_{J} = L_{I} = -\Gamma i_{H}$ there; on the $(+1)$-eigenspace $L_{J} = -L_{I} = \Gamma i_{H}$. The script checks $(L_{J} + \Gamma i_{H})\Lambda(m) = 0$, $(L_{J} - L_{I})\Lambda(m) = 0$, $(L_{J} - \Gamma i_{H})\Lambda(k) = 0$, that $(L_{J} + \Gamma i_{H})\Lambda(k) \neq 0$, and $L_{J} \neq \pm L_{I}$. On the canonical channel of chirality $\epsilon$ the rotor $e^{-J\phi/2} = \cos\tfrac{\phi}{2} - J\sin\tfrac{\phi}{2}$ acts as $\cos\tfrac{\phi}{2} + \epsilon\,i_{H}\sin\tfrac{\phi}{2} = e^{\epsilon i_{H}\phi/2}$: helicity $-\epsilon/2$ about $k$, which is helicity $\epsilon/2$ about $m$. With the central unit both canonical channels are complex-linear for $L_{J} = L_{I}$, that is, both carry the same sign relative to that unit; the opposite helicity of the second chirality appears in the conjugate, which is Theorem \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(4) (with the unit $I_{4}$ one chirality enters complex-linearly, the other conjugated). The channel count does not depend on the unit.

\emph{(v).} A Weyl spinor field takes values in one $W_{\pm}$, and by (iii) its canonical part on $N_{k}$ is one complex channel; a Hestenes spinor field (all of $\Cl^{+}(1,3)$, a Dirac field) has both, of opposite chirality and so, by (iv), of opposite helicity. The script also counts channels from the flux form itself: the rank of the flux Gram matrix is $4$ (two complex channels), and its restriction to one Weyl half has rank $2$ (one).

\emph{(vi).} With $R = \tfrac54 + \tfrac34 B$: $R\gamma_{1}\tilde{R} = \gamma_{1}$ and $R\gamma_{2}\tilde{R} = \gamma_{2}$ since $B$ commutes with them; $Rk\tilde{R} = 4k$, $Rm\tilde{R} = \tfrac14 m$, and $R(k\wedge\gamma_{j})\tilde{R} = 4\,k\wedge\gamma_{j}$ for $j = 1, 2$, the transverse null components of a field strength (checked). The one-sided action on the canonical spinor $\tfrac12(1 - B)$ gives $\tfrac12 = e^{-\lambda/2}$. $J^{2} = -1$ is the rotor of a full turn in the transverse plane ($e^{J\pi/2} = J$), which acts as $-1$ on spinors and as the identity by conjugation on $\gamma_{1}$. So integer weights belong to conjugation-acted fields and give the offset $0$ of the stored classification (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.half-integer-weight-array-carries-half-ln2}, the sentence after (iii)); weight $\tfrac12$, hence version 3's offset, belongs to spinors.

\emph{(vii).} Read version 3 of Premise (Q) (\claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave}) with one array per complex canonical channel of a spinor field on a light ray, the array being the discretised modes of that channel. By (v) a Dirac species has two arrays and a Weyl field one; by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.half-integer-weight-array-carries-half-ln2}(i) each array carries $\tfrac12\ln 2$ at the Hawking temperature, so a Dirac species on one light ray carries $\ln 2$ and a Weyl field $\tfrac12\ln 2$. Counting per light ray, with the counted unit a bookkeeping total over all horizon fields, the arrays on a light ray number $2n_{D} + n_{W}$ and carry $(n_{D} + \tfrac12 n_{W})\ln 2$, so the registered unit of $\ln 2$ is two arrays of the total (the script evaluates this for several $(n_{D}, n_{W})$). Under the hypothesis of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy} the residue per counted unit is $1/(4\langle s\rangle)$ (its (i)), which for units of two arrays is $1/(4\ln 2)$; a unit of one array would give $1/(2\ln 2)$. The script recomputes the channel counts $2$ and $1$ from the ranks and both residues in units of $1/(4\ln 2)$.

\emph{What is and is not derived.} (i) to (vi) are exact identities in $\Cl(1,3)$. They show that the arrays are the chirality channels of the spinor fields' canonical parts on the horizon's null plane, that two of them are the light-ray content of one massless Dirac species, and that on them helicity about the generators is minus the chirality. They do not fix the horizon's field content: the number of registered units per light ray is half the number of canonical chirality channels summed over all horizon fields, which is what the bookkeeping count records.

synthesis.mode-split-of-the-clifford-alg.formal:
Let $\Cl(\ell,\ell)$ have generators $e_{k}$, $f_{k}$ ($1 \le k \le \ell$) with $Q(e_{k}) = 1$, $Q(f_{k}) = -1$, and null pairs $v_{k} = \tfrac12(e_{k} + f_{k})$, $w_{k} = \tfrac12(e_{k} - f_{k})$, the $\ell$ modes of Proposition \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors}; put $p_{k} = 1 - 2w_{k}v_{k} = f_{k}e_{k}$ (the parity of mode $k$, $p_{k}^{2} = 1$), $\Gamma_{X} = \prod_{k \in X}p_{k}$ for a set $X$ of modes and $\Gamma = \Gamma_{\{1,\dots,\ell\}}$. Coefficients are real, or lie in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ with $I_{4}$ commuting with every generator; $x \mapsto x^{\dagger}$ is the anti-automorphism fixing each $e_{k}$, negating each $f_{k}$ (and $I_{4}$), which exchanges $v_{k}$ and $w_{k}$; $\operatorname{tr} = 2^{\ell}\langle\cdot\rangle_{0}$. A \emph{state} is a sum $\rho = \sum_{r}x_{r}x_{r}^{\dagger}$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho = 1$; it is \emph{pure} if $\rho^{2} = \rho$ and \emph{even} if $\Gamma\rho = \rho\Gamma$, that is, if it is fixed by $x \mapsto \tfrac12(x + \Gamma x\Gamma)$, the average of Theorem \claimref{singularity.descent-parity-average} with the total parity $\Gamma$ in place of the single-mode $\sigma$; that theorem is stated for one mode and the $\ell$-mode form is a definition here. For a set $A$ of $a$ modes with complement $B$ of $b \ge 1$ modes ($a \ge 1$, $d_{A} = 2^{a}$, $d_{B} = 2^{b}$, $D = d_{A}d_{B}$) let $\Cl(A) \cong \Cl(a,a)$ be the subalgebra generated by the $e_{k}, f_{k}$ with $k \in A$, $E_{A}$ the linear projection onto its blades, $\rho_{A} = d_{B}E_{A}(\rho)$ and $\operatorname{tr}_{A} = d_{A}\langle\cdot\rangle_{0}$ on $\Cl(A)$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The split; proved.)} Homogeneous $x \in \Cl(A)$, $y \in \Cl(B)$ satisfy $xy = (-1)^{|x||y|}yx$, and multiplication $\Cl(A) \otimes \Cl(B) \to \Cl(\ell,\ell)$ is a linear bijection that is multiplicative for the graded product only. $E_{A}$ is the one linear map onto $\Cl(A)$ with $\langle E_{A}(x)y\rangle_{0} = \langle xy\rangle_{0}$ for all $y \in \Cl(A)$; it satisfies $E_{A}(yxy') = yE_{A}(x)y'$ for $y, y' \in \Cl(A)$ and $E_{A}(x^{\dagger}) = E_{A}(x)^{\dagger}$, and $\rho_{A}$ is a state of $\Cl(A)$, with purity $\operatorname{tr}_{A}\rho_{A}^{2} = d_{A}d_{B}^{2}\langle E_{A}(\rho)^{2}\rangle_{0}$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The Klein twist; proved.)} $\Gamma_{A}^{2} = 1$; $\Gamma_{A}$ anticommutes with the generators of $\Cl(A)$ and commutes with $\Cl(B)$. The twisted generators $y\Gamma_{A}$, $y \in \{e_{k}, f_{k} : k \in B\}$, keep their squares, anticommute with each other and commute with $\Cl(A)$; the algebra $B'$ they generate is isomorphic to $\Cl(b,b)$, and multiplication $\Cl(A) \otimes B' \to \Cl(\ell,\ell)$ is an isomorphism of algebras for the ordinary tensor product (Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies}, with ground algebra $\Cl(B)$ and the planes of $A$). The even part of $B'$ is the even part of $\Cl(B)$, and its odd part is $\Gamma_{A}$ times the odd part of $\Cl(B)$. If $K$ commutes with $\Cl(B)$ and every $yK$ commutes with $\Cl(A)$ and has the square of $y$, then $K = \pm\Gamma_{A}$ (compare Theorem \claimref{synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-a-klein-convention-on-the-composite-space}(iv)).
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Reductions; proved.)} For every $x$, the partial trace of the tensor split of (ii) over $B'$ is $d_{B}E_{A}(x)$: the reduction to $A$ is the same for the two splits, for every state. The partial trace over $\Cl(A)$ is $d_{A}E_{B'}(x)$, with $E_{B'}$ the projection onto the blades $e_{T}$ ($|T|$ even) and $\Gamma_{A}e_{T}$ ($|T|$ odd), $e_{T}$ the blades of $\Cl(B)$; so $E_{B'}(x) = E_{B}(x)$ exactly when $x$ has no component on $e_{T}$ or $\Gamma_{A}e_{T}$ with $|T|$ odd, in particular for every even $x$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Even states; proved.)} If $\rho$ is even, $\rho_{A}$ and $\rho_{B}$ are even, $\rho_{B}$ is the reduced state of the tensor split as well, and $\rho_{A}$ commutes with $\Gamma_{A}$. If moreover $\rho$ is pure, then $\operatorname{tr}_{A}\rho_{A}^{n} = \operatorname{tr}_{B}\rho_{B}^{n}$ for every $n \ge 1$ (equal nonzero spectra), and $\Gamma\rho = \pm\rho$: the state lies in a parity sector, of dimension $D/2$, which in the tensor split is $(\text{even} \otimes \text{even}) \oplus (\text{odd} \otimes \text{odd})$ or $(\text{even} \otimes \text{odd}) \oplus (\text{odd} \otimes \text{even})$ and not a tensor product. For a pure state that is not even the equality can fail: at $\ell = 2$, $\rho = \tfrac14(1 + e_{1} - f_{1}e_{2} + f_{1}e_{1}e_{2}) = \tfrac12(1 + e_{1})\,\tfrac12(1 + e_{2}p_{1})$ has $\rho_{A} = \tfrac12(1 + e_{1})$, of purity $1$, and $\rho_{B} = \tfrac12$, of purity $\tfrac12$.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Products of even states; proved.)} If $P_{1}, \dots, P_{r}$ are disjoint sets of modes with union all modes and $\rho_{j}$ is an even state of $\Cl(P_{j})$, the $\rho_{j}$ commute, $\rho = \prod_{j}\rho_{j}$ is an even state, pure if every $\rho_{j}$ is, $\rho_{A} = \prod_{j}(\rho_{j})_{A \cap P_{j}}$, and $\operatorname{tr}_{A}\rho_{A}^{n} = \prod_{j}\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{j})_{A \cap P_{j}}^{n}$: for even states the tensor product is the product in the algebra, with no twist. The pair state with amplitudes $c$ on $\ket{00}$ and $s$ on $\ket{11}$ ($c^{2} + s^{2} = 1$, $r = c^{2} - s^{2}$) of modes $k$, $k'$ is
\[
\rho_{kk'} = \tfrac14(1 + p_{k}p_{k'})(1 + rp_{k}) + cs\,(w_{k}w_{k'} + v_{k'}v_{k}) ,
\]
a pure even state with reduction $\tfrac12(1 + rp_{k})$ on mode $k$, of purity $\tfrac12(1 + r^{2}) = c^{4} + s^{4}$. Reading the pairs of Theorem \claimref{singularity.eviction-window-thermal-product-radiation-entropy} as these pair states, its state is a pure even state, its window is the product $\prod_{k \in W}\tfrac12(1 + r_{k}p_{k})$, and the radiation has the same nonzero spectrum.
\item[(vi)] \emph{(Renyi moments of a parity sector; proved, the two upper bounds computed.)} For a unit vector drawn from the unitarily invariant measure of a parity sector, $\langle\operatorname{tr}_{A}\rho_{A}^{n}\rangle = 2\sum_{\sigma \in S_{n}}(d_{A}/2)^{\#(\sigma^{-1}\eta)}(d_{B}/2)^{\#(\sigma)}/\prod_{l=0}^{n-1}(D/2 + l)$, with $\eta$, $\#$ as in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.eviction-keeps-one-of-catalan-many-replica-saddles} and the average that of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-haar-moments-of-random-pure-state} on the sector; this formula is clause (iv) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.finite-normaliser-averages-leave-the-haar-moments-at-order-four-and-on-a-parity-sector}, cited and not reproved here. At $n = 2$ it is $(d_{A} + d_{B})/(D + 2)$, strictly between $\max(1/d_{A}, 1/d_{B})$ and the unrestricted $(d_{A} + d_{B})/(D + 1)$, and below $1/d_{A} + 1/d_{B}$ by $2(d_{A} + d_{B})/(D(D + 2))$. At $d_{A} = d_{B} = d$, with $N_{n,g}$ the number of $\sigma$ with $\#(\sigma) + \#(\sigma^{-1}\eta) = n + 1 - 2g$,
\[
d^{\,n-1}\langle\operatorname{tr}\rho^{n}\rangle_{\mathrm{sector}} = \frac{\sum_{g}N_{n,g}(4/d^{2})^{g}}{\prod_{l<n}(1 + 2l/d^{2})}
\qquad\text{against}\qquad
\frac{\sum_{g}N_{n,g}\,d^{-2g}}{\prod_{l<n}(1 + l/d^{2})}
\]
for the unrestricted average: both tend to $N_{n,0} = C_{n}$, and the coefficient of $d^{-2}$ is $-(C_{n}n(n-1) - 4N_{n,1})$ against $-(\tfrac12 C_{n}n(n-1) - N_{n,1})$. The sector value exceeds $d^{1-n}$ for all $n$, $d$ (proved); it is below the unrestricted one, itself below $C_{n}d^{1-n}$, for $2 \le n \le 6$ and $d = 2, \dots, 32$ (computed; $N_{n,1} = 0, 1, 10, 70, 420$).
\item[(vii)] \emph{(Mean entropy of a parity sector; proved from Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-page-average-entropy-subsystem} and the background named in the note.)} For $m = d_{A} \le n = d_{B}$ the same average of the entropy of $\rho_{A}$ is
\[
\langle S_{A}\rangle_{\mathrm{sector}} = \sum_{k = n/2 + 1}^{mn/2}\frac1k - \frac{m - 2}{2n} ,
\]
which exceeds the Fact's $\sum_{k=n+1}^{mn}\tfrac1k - \tfrac{m-1}{2n}$ by the rational number $\Delta(m,n) = \tfrac{1}{2n} - \sum_{k=mn/2+1}^{mn}\tfrac1k + \sum_{k=n/2+1}^{n}\tfrac1k$, with $\tfrac{1}{2mn} < \Delta(m,n) < \tfrac{1}{2(mn+1)} + \tfrac{1}{2n(n+1)}$ (sector value $\tfrac12$ against the Fact's $\tfrac13$ at $m = n = 2$, $\Delta = \tfrac16$; sector value $\tfrac{271}{280}$ at $m = n = 4$, $\Delta = \tfrac{6553}{144144}$). The deficit $\delta_{\mathrm{sec}} = \ln m - \langle S_{A}\rangle_{\mathrm{sector}}$ satisfies
\[
\frac{m-2}{2n} + \frac{2(m-1)}{2mn + m + 1} \;<\; \delta_{\mathrm{sec}}(m,n) \;<\; \frac{m}{2n} - \frac{1}{mn} ,
\]
so it is positive, below $\tfrac12$, in $(\tfrac25, \tfrac12)$ at the crossing $m = n \ge 4$, above $(m-1)/(2n)$ for $m \ge 4$ and below it for $m = 2$.
\end{enumerate}
Fate of the stored comparisons on this split, for the even states they use. Theorem \claimref{singularity.eviction-window-thermal-product-radiation-entropy}: all four clauses unchanged, its tensor product read as the product of (v) and $S_{R} = S_{L}$ by (iv). Theorem \claimref{synthesis.eviction-keeps-one-replica-saddle} at version 3: (i), (ii), (v) unchanged; in (iii), (iv) the random-state value on a sector is $(m + n)/(mn + 2)$, at the crossing $2m/(m^{2} + 2)$, below the eviction value in $S_{2}$ by $\ln 2 - \ln(1 + 2m^{-2}) \in (\ln 2 - 2m^{-2}, \ln 2)$: leading term $\ln 2$ unchanged, the term of order $m^{-2}$ doubled. Theorem \claimref{synthesis.eviction-keeps-one-of-catalan-many-replica-saddles} at version 3: (i), (ii) unchanged; (iii) with the sector formula of (vi), limit $C_{n}$ and gap $\ln C_{n}/(n-1)$ of (iv) unchanged. Theorem \claimref{synthesis.eviction-deficit-against-page-deficit} at version 4 (version 5 carries the sector column itself): (ii), (iii) unchanged; (i) with the bounds of (vii), half a nat at the crossing unchanged, the lower bound $(m-1)/(2n)$ lost at $m = 2$ only. Fact \claimref{singularity.assembled-page-curve-up-typicality}: unchanged at the order it states. None fails; each stored statement about an abstract tensor product remains true as stated.
synthesis.mode-split-of-the-clifford-alg.technical:
The eviction comparisons of the series divide a set of fermionic modes into window and radiation and compare the reduced state with that of a random pure state. As stored they use a tensor product of two abstract spaces. In the Clifford algebra of the modes the natural split is different: each side is the sub-Clifford algebra generated by its own modes, and reduction is the projection onto its blades. The two sub-Clifford algebras do not commute (their odd elements anticommute), so together they are a graded tensor product. The stored commuting-copies twist repairs this: multiplying the generators of one side by the parity blade of the other gives a commuting copy, and the pair (untwisted side, twisted side) is an ordinary tensor product. The projection onto the untwisted side is exactly the partial trace of that tensor product, for every state; the projection onto the other side differs from the partial trace only on odd blades. So for even states, the states fixed by the total-parity average, both reductions coincide with the tensor-product ones, the two sides of a pure state have the same spectrum, and products of even states are plain products in the algebra. For a pure state that is not even the two sides can have different purities, so evenness is the exact hypothesis under which the stored arguments transfer.

What does change is the ensemble behind the word "typical". A pure even state lies in one parity sector, half the dimension, and a sector is a sum of two tensor products, not one. The random-state columns of the comparisons, recomputed on a sector, keep every leading term: the Renyi-2 gap $\ln 2$, the gap $\ln C_{n}/(n-1)$ at index $n$, half a nat of entropy at the crossing. Below leading order they move: the mean purity is $(m + n)/(mn + 2)$, a permutation of genus $g$ in the moment sum is weighted by $4^{g}$ relative to the unrestricted average, and the mean entropy is larger than Page's by a rational amount between $1/(2mn)$ and $1/(2mn) + 1/(2n^{2})$, about $3/(4m^{2})$ at the crossing. The eviction side does not move at all, since its state is an even product of pair states. The mean entropy uses Page's Fact on the two blocks of a sector and is the two-block case of a known formula for random states on a direct sum of tensor products; the moment formula uses the imported all-moment Fact on the sector. Both are conditional on those imports.
synthesis.mode-split-of-the-clifford-alg.lay: When physicists ask how much two parts of a system share, they usually treat the two parts as independent building blocks glued together in the simplest way. For particles like electrons that picture is slightly off, because operations on one part can pick up a sign from the other. This result does the bookkeeping directly in the algebra the series uses for such particles and shows precisely how it relates to the usual picture: a simple relabelling by a sign factor turns one into the other. For the states the series actually uses, in which the total number of particles is even or odd but never a mixture of both, the two pictures give the same answers for each part, and all of the series' statements about its own radiation mechanism stand as they were. What shifts slightly is the benchmark of a "random state": with the even-or-odd restriction a random state is a little more mixed than without it. The main terms of every comparison stay the same, and only small corrections change, by amounts given exactly, using two textbook averages the collection holds as imports. For states that mix even and odd the two pictures can disagree, and an example is given.

proofs.main:
\emph{Preliminaries.} The blades $e_{S}$ are a basis, $e_{S}e_{T} = \pm e_{S \triangle T}$, and two blades commute or anticommute according to the form $b(S,T) = |S||T| + |S \cap T|$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.blade-square-signs-f2-quadratic-form}(ii)). For a blade, $e_{S}^{\dagger}$ is its reverse times $(-1)^{\#f}$, $\#f$ the number of generators $f_{k}$ in it, and the product of a blade with its reverse is the product of the squares of its generators, $(-1)^{\#f}$; so $e_{S}e_{S}^{\dagger} = 1$, the blades are orthonormal for $\langle xy^{\dagger}\rangle_{0}$, and $\langle xx^{\dagger}\rangle_{0} \ge 0$ with equality only for $x = 0$. From $v_{k}w_{k} + w_{k}v_{k} = 1$ (Proposition \claimref{tower.ladder-pairs-satisfy-car-vectors}) and $w_{k}v_{k} = \tfrac14(e_{k} - f_{k})(e_{k} + f_{k}) = \tfrac12(1 + e_{k}f_{k})$, $p_{k} = 1 - 2w_{k}v_{k} = f_{k}e_{k}$ and $p_{k}^{2} = -f_{k}^{2}e_{k}^{2} = 1$.

\emph{(i).} Generators of $\Cl(A)$ and of $\Cl(B)$ are distinct orthogonal vectors and anticommute, which gives the sign $(-1)^{|x||y|}$ on products of generators and so on homogeneous elements. A blade factors uniquely, up to sign, as a blade of $\Cl(A)$ times a blade of $\Cl(B)$, so multiplication is a bijection of bases; it carries the ordinary product $(x \otimes y)(x' \otimes y') = xx' \otimes yy'$ to $xx'yy'$, while $(xy)(x'y') = (-1)^{|y||x'|}xx'yy'$, so it is multiplicative only with that sign. Since $\langle e_{S}e_{T}\rangle_{0} = 0$ unless $S = T$, the pairing $\langle xy\rangle_{0}$ with $y \in \Cl(A)$ sees only the components of $x$ on blades of $\Cl(A)$ and is nondegenerate there: this is the characterisation of $E_{A}$. Multiplication by a blade of $\Cl(A)$ permutes the blades up to sign and preserves the set of blades of $\Cl(A)$ and its complement, whence $E_{A}(yxy') = yE_{A}(x)y'$; $\dagger$ preserves each blade up to sign, whence $E_{A}(x^{\dagger}) = E_{A}(x)^{\dagger}$. For $\rho = \sum_{r}x_{r}x_{r}^{\dagger}$ and $z \in \Cl(A)$, $\langle z^{\dagger}E_{A}(\rho)z\rangle_{0} = \langle E_{A}(z^{\dagger}\rho z)\rangle_{0} = \sum_{r}\langle(z^{\dagger}x_{r})(z^{\dagger}x_{r})^{\dagger}\rangle_{0} \ge 0$; $\Cl(A)$ with coefficients in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ is a full matrix algebra on which $\operatorname{tr}_{A}$ is the trace and $\dagger$ the adjoint (the Fock module built on the vacuum of the $v_{k}$, $k \in A$), and an element $h = h^{\dagger}$ with $\operatorname{tr}_{A}(zz^{\dagger}h) \ge 0$ for all $z$ is positive, hence a sum of terms $xx^{\dagger}$. Finally $\operatorname{tr}_{A}\rho_{A} = d_{A}d_{B}\langle\rho\rangle_{0} = 1$, and the purity is the definition written out.

\emph{(ii).} $\Gamma_{A}$ is a product of the commuting elements $p_{k}$ of square $1$, so $\Gamma_{A}^{2} = 1$; each $p_{k} = f_{k}e_{k}$ anticommutes with $e_{k}$ and $f_{k}$ and commutes with the other generators, so $\Gamma_{A}$ anticommutes with the generators of $\Cl(A)$ and commutes with those of $\Cl(B)$. For generators $y, y'$ of $\Cl(B)$ and $x$ of $\Cl(A)$: $(y\Gamma_{A})^{2} = y^{2}\Gamma_{A}^{2} = Q(y)$; $y\Gamma_{A}y'\Gamma_{A} = yy'$, so the twisted generators anticommute as the untwisted do; and $x\,y\Gamma_{A} = -yx\Gamma_{A} = y\Gamma_{A}x$. With $\omega_{k} = e_{k}f_{k} = -p_{k}$ the twisted generators are $\pm y\,\omega_{k_{1}}\cdots\omega_{k_{a}}$, those of Theorem \claimref{tower.commuting-copies} for the ground algebra $\Cl(B) \cong \Cl(b,b)$ and the $a$ planes of $A$ (the sign does not change the algebra generated), and that theorem gives $B' \cong \Cl(b,b)$, commuting with the algebra of the planes, $\Cl(A)$, and the isomorphism $\Cl(A) \otimes B' \to \Cl(\ell,\ell)$. A product of $t$ twisted generators is $\pm e_{T}\Gamma_{A}^{t}$, which is $\pm e_{T}$ for $t$ even and $\pm\Gamma_{A}e_{T}$ for $t$ odd: the statement on even and odd parts. Uniqueness: $yK$ commutes with a generator $x$ of $\Cl(A)$ exactly when $K$ anticommutes with $x$, so each blade $e_{U}$ occurring in $K$ anticommutes with the $2a$ generators of $A$ and commutes with the $2b$ generators of $B$. By the form $b$, a generator $g$ and $e_{U}$ anticommute exactly when $|U| + [g \in U]$ is odd. If $|U|$ is even, $U$ contains every generator of $A$ and none of $B$, the blade of $\Gamma_{A}$; if $|U|$ is odd, $U$ contains no generator of $A$ and all $2b$ of $B$, which is an even number, a contradiction. So $K$ is a multiple of $\Gamma_{A}$, and $(yK)^{2} = Q(y)K^{2}$ forces the multiple to be $\pm 1$; this is the count of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-a-klein-convention-on-the-composite-space}(iv) for a general pair of sets of modes.

\emph{(iii).} In a tensor product of matrix algebras the partial trace over the second factor is the map $T$ into the first with $\operatorname{tr}_{A}(T(x)y) = \operatorname{tr}(xy)$ for all $y$ in the first. By (i), $\operatorname{tr}_{A}(d_{B}E_{A}(x)y) = d_{A}d_{B}\langle xy\rangle_{0} = \operatorname{tr}(xy)$, so $T = d_{B}E_{A}$. The same argument with the roles exchanged gives $d_{A}$ times the projection onto the blades of $B'$, which by (ii) are the $e_{T}$ with $|T|$ even and the $\Gamma_{A}e_{T}$ with $|T|$ odd; $E_{B}$ keeps all $e_{T}$ instead. The two projections agree on the even $e_{T}$ and on every blade outside both lists, and differ exactly on the components listed. A blade $e_{T}$ or $\Gamma_{A}e_{T}$ with $|T|$ odd is odd ($\Gamma_{A}$ has $2a$ generators), so an even element has no such component.

\emph{(iv).} Evenness is invariance under $x \mapsto \tfrac12(x + \Gamma x\Gamma)$, the average of Theorem \claimref{singularity.descent-parity-average} with the total parity $\Gamma$ in place of the single-mode $\sigma$; that theorem is stated for one mode, and the $\ell$-mode form is a definition here (applied mode by mode it would erase the coherence of the pair state of (v), which is odd in one mode alone). A projection onto blades preserves evenness, so $\rho_{A}$, $\rho_{B}$ are even; an even element of $\Cl(A)$ commutes with $\Gamma_{A}$; and $\rho_{B} = d_{A}E_{B}(\rho) = d_{A}E_{B'}(\rho)$ by (iii). For $\rho$ pure, the Schmidt decomposition in the tensor split $\Cl(A) \otimes B'$ gives equal nonzero spectra of the two partial traces, and the trace of $B'$ restricted to the common even part is $d_{B}\langle\cdot\rangle_{0}$, as for $\Cl(B)$; so the moments agree. A pure $\rho$ is a projector of rank one; commuting with the involution $\Gamma$, its range is an eigenline of $\Gamma$. $\Gamma = \Gamma_{A}\Gamma_{B}$ with $\Gamma_{B} \in B'$ even, so in the tensor split $\Gamma = \Gamma_{A} \otimes \Gamma_{B}$, and since $\operatorname{tr}_{A}\Gamma_{A} = 0$ each of its eigenspaces is the sum of two products of half-dimensional eigenspaces. The example: $e_{1}$ and $e_{2}p_{1} = e_{2}f_{1}e_{1}$ are commuting elements of square $1$ fixed by $\dagger$, so $\tfrac12(1 + e_{1})\tfrac12(1 + e_{2}p_{1})$ is a projector of trace $1$; expanding, $e_{1}e_{2}f_{1}e_{1} = -f_{1}e_{2}$ and $e_{2}f_{1}e_{1} = f_{1}e_{1}e_{2}$. Its blades in $\Cl(\{1\})$ are $1, e_{1}$ and in $\Cl(\{2\})$ only $1$. The check computes these, and the moments of an even and of a non-even pure state of three modes.

\emph{(v).} Even elements of the algebras of disjoint sets of modes commute by (i). A product of blades $e_{S_{j}}$ of the $\Cl(P_{j})$ is $\pm$ the blade on $\bigcup S_{j}$, which is scalar only if every $S_{j}$ is empty and lies in $\Cl(A)$ only if every $e_{S_{j}}$ does; hence $\langle\prod x_{j}\rangle_{0} = \prod\langle x_{j}\rangle_{0}$ and $E_{A}(\prod x_{j}) = \prod E_{A \cap P_{j}}(x_{j})$ for $x_{j} \in \Cl(P_{j})$. So $\operatorname{tr}\rho = 1$, $\rho_{A} = \prod(\rho_{j})_{A \cap P_{j}}$ (the factors $2^{|P_{j} \setminus A|}$ multiply to $d_{B}$), and since the reduced factors are even and commute, $\rho_{A}^{n} = \prod(\rho_{j})_{A \cap P_{j}}^{n}$ and the traces multiply. $\rho$ is a sum of terms $xx^{\dagger}$ because the commuting positive $\rho_{j}$ have commuting positive square roots in the even parts; it is a projector if every $\rho_{j}$ is. The pair state: with $\Omega = v_{k}w_{k}v_{k'}w_{k'}$ the vacuum projector and $\psi = c + s\,w_{k}w_{k'}$, $\psi\Omega\psi^{\dagger}$ is the projector on $c\ket{00} + s\ket{11}$; expanding with $v_{k}w_{k} = \tfrac12(1 + p_{k})$ gives the displayed form, in which $p_{k}$, $p_{k'}$, $p_{k}p_{k'}$ carry the diagonal and $w_{k}w_{k'} + v_{k'}v_{k} = -\tfrac12(e_{k}f_{k'} + f_{k}e_{k'})$ the coherence. Its blades inside $\Cl(\{k\})$ are $\tfrac14(1 + rp_{k})$, so the reduction is $\tfrac12(1 + rp_{k})$, with $\operatorname{tr}(\tfrac12(1 + rp_{k}))^{2} = \tfrac12(1 + r^{2})$. Reading the pairs of Theorem \claimref{singularity.eviction-window-thermal-product-radiation-entropy} as these pair states, its state is the product of such pair states over the injected pairs (window member and radiated partner, or both halves in the radiation after an eviction), so the statements follow from the first part and (iv). The check verifies the displayed form against the Fock construction, the product, the reductions and the purities at $c^{2} = \tfrac{9}{25}, \tfrac{25}{169}$ and at zero weight.

\emph{(vi).} By (iv) $\rho_{A}$ is the partial trace of the tensor split, so $\operatorname{tr}_{A}\rho_{A}^{n} = \operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho^{\otimes n}(P^{A}_{\eta} \otimes 1)\bigr)$ as in the proof of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.eviction-keeps-one-of-catalan-many-replica-saddles}(iii). In the tensor split a parity sector is the span of the products of an even with an even and of an odd with an odd state (an eigenspace of $\Gamma = \Gamma_{A} \otimes \Gamma_{B}$; for the other eigenspace exchange even and odd in one factor, which changes no count), of dimension $D/2$, which is the space of clause (iv) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.finite-normaliser-averages-leave-the-haar-moments-at-order-four-and-on-a-parity-sector}; that clause, which rests on Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-haar-moments-of-random-pure-state} applied to the sector, is the formula, with $\tau = \sigma^{-1}\eta$: the term of $\sigma$ is $2(d_{A}/2)^{\#(\tau)}(d_{B}/2)^{\#(\sigma)}$. The check confirms the count behind it by enumeration at six cases. At $n = 2$: $2\cdot\tfrac18 d_{A}d_{B}(d_{A} + d_{B})/(\tfrac14 D(D + 2))$. The inequalities at $n = 2$: with $d_{A} \le d_{B}$, $d_{A}(d_{A} + d_{B}) > D + 2$ since $d_{A}^{2} \ge 4$; the others are immediate. At $d_{A} = d_{B} = d$ a permutation with $\#(\sigma) + \#(\tau) = n + 1 - 2g$ contributes $2(d/2)^{n+1-2g}/(d^{2}/2)^{n} = 4^{g}d^{1-n-2g}$ before the factor $\prod_{l}(1 + 2l/d^{2})^{-1}$, and $d^{n+1-2g}/d^{2n}$ in the unrestricted average; $g$ is an integer because the signs of $\sigma$, $\tau$ multiply to that of $\eta$, and $g \ge 0$ with $N_{n,0} = C_{n}$ by clause (ii) of the stored theorem. The limits and the coefficients of $d^{-2}$ follow ($\sum_{l<n}2l = n(n-1)$). Lower bound: $\rho_{A}$ is a state on $d$ dimensions, so $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{n} \ge d^{1-n}$, with equality only for the flat spectrum, which is not almost sure. The two upper comparisons are verified exactly in the stated range and not proved in general.

\emph{(vii).} In the tensor split a sector is $H_{+} \oplus H_{-}$, each summand the product of an eigenspace of $\Gamma_{A}$ (dimension $m/2$) with one of $\Gamma_{B}$ (dimension $n/2$); put $k_{0} = mn/4$. A unit vector is $\sqrt{t}\,\psi_{+} + \sqrt{1-t}\,\psi_{-}$ with unit $\psi_{\pm} \in H_{\pm}$. The partial trace of a cross term $\psi_{+}\psi_{-}^{\dagger}$ vanishes, the two $B$ eigenspaces being orthogonal, so $\rho_{A} = t\rho_{+} \oplus (1-t)\rho_{-}$ on the two eigenspaces of $\Gamma_{A}$ and $S(\rho_{A}) = h(t) + tS(\rho_{+}) + (1-t)S(\rho_{-})$, $h(t) = -t\ln t - (1-t)\ln(1-t)$. Under the invariant measure (the law of a normalised Gaussian vector), $t$ is the ratio of two independent Gamma variables of shape $k_{0}$, a Beta law with parameters $(k_{0}, k_{0})$, independent of $\psi_{+}$ and $\psi_{-}$, which are independent and invariantly distributed on their summands. Hence $\langle S_{A}\rangle = \langle h(t)\rangle + \langle S\rangle_{m/2,\,n/2}$, the last term given by Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-page-average-entropy-subsystem} (zero for $m = 2$). For the Beta law $\langle t^{1+s}\rangle = \Gamma(k_{0}+1+s)\Gamma(2k_{0})/(\Gamma(k_{0})\Gamma(2k_{0}+1+s))$, whose derivative at $s = 0$ is $\langle t\ln t\rangle = \tfrac12(\psi(k_{0}+1) - \psi(2k_{0}+1)) = -\tfrac12\sum_{k=k_{0}+1}^{2k_{0}}1/k$, so $\langle h(t)\rangle = \sum_{k=mn/4+1}^{mn/2}1/k$. Adding the Fact's $\sum_{k=n/2+1}^{mn/4}1/k - (m/2 - 1)/n$ gives the formula. The difference from the Fact's value at $(m,n)$ is rational by inspection; with $a_{N} = \sum_{k=N+1}^{2N}1/k$ it is $\Delta = \tfrac{1}{2n} - (a_{mn/2} - a_{n/2})$, and $a_{N+1} - a_{N} = 1/((2N+1)(2N+2))$ lies strictly between $\tfrac12(\tfrac{1}{2N+1} - \tfrac{1}{2N+3})$ and $\tfrac12(\tfrac{1}{2N} - \tfrac{1}{2N+2})$; summing over $n/2 \le N < mn/2$ telescopes to $\tfrac12(\tfrac{1}{n+1} - \tfrac{1}{mn+1}) < a_{mn/2} - a_{n/2} < \tfrac12(\tfrac1n - \tfrac{1}{mn})$, the stated bounds on $\Delta$ (the upper one is below $\tfrac{1}{2mn} + \tfrac{1}{2n^{2}}$). The closed form is the two-block case of a known formula for random states on a direct sum of tensor products (note); it is rederived here from the Fact. For the deficit, convexity of $1/x$ gives $1/k < \int_{k-1/2}^{k+1/2}dx/x$ and $\int_{k-1}^{k}dx/x < \tfrac12(\tfrac{1}{k-1} + \tfrac1k)$; summing over $n/2 < k \le mn/2$: $\ln m - \tfrac{m-1}{mn} < \sum 1/k < \ln\frac{mn+1}{n+1}$, so $\delta_{\mathrm{sec}} > \tfrac{m-2}{2n} + \ln\bigl(1 + \tfrac{m-1}{mn+1}\bigr)$ and $\delta_{\mathrm{sec}} < \tfrac{m-2}{2n} + \tfrac{m-1}{mn} = \tfrac{m}{2n} - \tfrac{1}{mn}$; with $\ln(1+u) > 2u/(2+u)$ the lower bound becomes the stated one. At $m = n$: the upper bound is $\tfrac12 - m^{-2}$; the lower one is $\tfrac14 + \tfrac{6}{37}$ at $m = 4$, $\tfrac38 + \tfrac{14}{137}$ at $m = 8$ and at least $\tfrac12 - \tfrac1m \ge \tfrac{7}{16}$ from $m = 16$, all above $\tfrac25$. The lower bound exceeds $(m-1)/(2n)$ exactly when $n(2m - 4) > m + 1$, true for $m \ge 4$; for $m = 2$ the upper bound is $\tfrac{1}{n} - \tfrac{1}{2n} = \tfrac{1}{2n} = (m-1)/(2n)$, so the deficit is below it. The check evaluates the closed form, the block decomposition, the difference and all bounds for $m, n \le 64$, with $\ln 2$ bracketed by partial sums of $\sum 1/(k2^{k})$, and compares the moments of the Beta law at $m = 2$ with the formula of (vi).

\emph{The fate of the stored comparisons.} Each eviction-side clause uses only: the window is a product of thermal marginals, the joint state is pure, the two sides have equal spectra, purities and entropies of products multiply or add. These are (v) and (iv), and they cover the eviction clauses of Theorems \claimref{synthesis.eviction-keeps-one-replica-saddle}, \claimref{synthesis.eviction-keeps-one-of-catalan-many-replica-saddles} and \claimref{synthesis.eviction-deficit-against-page-deficit}; the assembly of Fact \claimref{singularity.assembled-page-curve-up-typicality} uses the typical branch only to the order at which (vii) agrees with the imported value. Each random-state clause is recomputed in (vi), (vii): for the Renyi-2 crossing, $2m/(m^{2}+2)$ has ratio $2 - 4/(m^{2}+2)$ to $1/m$, so the gap is $\ln 2 - \ln(1 + 2m^{-2})$, in $(\ln 2 - 2m^{-2}, \ln 2)$ because $0 < \ln(1+u) < u$. $\square$

synthesis.no-spin-independent-modulus-le.formal:
Let $0 < a < M$ and take the Kerr gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) in the Kerr-Schild gauge of Fact \claimref{interior.imported-kerr-schild-form-kerr-gauge}, with the notation of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.kerr-ring-count-misses-area-law}: gauge field $\hb(b) = b + H\,(b\cdot k)\,k$, $H = Mr/\Sigma$, $\Sigma = r^{2} + a^{2}u^{2} = |z|^{2}$, $z = r - I_{4}au$, oblate coordinates $(t, r, u, \phi)$ of the flat background, $u = \cos\theta$, horizon loci $r_{\pm} = M \pm \sqrt{M^{2} - a^{2}}$, and curvature scale of modulus $|\mathfrak M| = M|z|^{-3}$ (Proposition \claimref{interior.complex-scale-inverse-cube-killing-spinor}). Fix $\rho$ with $\rho \le M/3$ and let $0 < a \le \tfrac45\rho$; put $\varepsilon = a^{2}/\rho^{2} \le \tfrac{16}{25}$ and $\delta = \tfrac52\,a^{2}/(\rho(2M - \rho))$. The Planck level set of Postulate \claimref{singularity.c1-curvature-cutoff}, $\rho = \rho_{c} = (2M)^{1/3}$, is in this range when $M \ge 8$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(Where the level set is.)} On the sheet $r > 0$ the level set $|z| = \rho$ of the curvature scale is the surface $r = R(u) := \sqrt{\rho^{2} - a^{2}u^{2}}$, $u \in [-1, 1]$, times the orbits of $\partial_{t}$ and $\partial_{\phi}$. It is closed and lies strictly between the horizon loci: $r_{-} \le a^{2}/M < \tfrac35\rho \le R(u) \le \rho < M \le r_{+}$. At $a = 0$ it is the Schwarzschild slice $r = \rho$.
\item \emph{(Determinant lemma, and the geometry of the level set.)} Let $r = R(u)$, $u \in (-1, 1)$, be any surface invariant under the two Killing flows, in any region where $\Sigma \neq 0$, and let $h$ be the metric the derived metric induces on it in the coordinates $(t, u, \phi)$: the Gram matrix of the physical tangent vectors $\hb^{-1}(\partial_{t})$, $\hb^{-1}(\partial_{u} + R'\partial_{r})$, $\hb^{-1}(\partial_{\phi})$, in the source's signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Then, with $\Delta(r) = r^{2} - 2Mr + a^{2}$,
\[
\det h \;=\; -\Sigma\,\bigl[\Delta(R) + (1 - u^{2})\,R'^{2}\bigr] ,
\]
identically in $M$, $a$, $u$, $R$ and $R'$, and also with $\partial_{t}$ replaced by any Killing flow $\partial_{t} + \Omega\,\partial_{\phi}$, $\Omega$ constant. In the store's product, which reverses the sign of every product, the Gram determinant is $+\Sigma[\Delta(R) + (1 - u^{2})R'^{2}]$. On the level set of item 1, $\Sigma = \rho^{2}$ and $R' = -a^{2}u/R$, so
\[
\det h \;=\; \rho^{2}\,B(u), \qquad B(u) \;=\; R\,(2M - R) - a^{2} - \frac{(1 - u^{2})\,a^{4}u^{2}}{R^{2}} ,
\]
and $(1 - \delta)\,R\,(2M - \rho) \le B \le R\,(2M - \rho)$ with $B > 0$, so the level set is spacelike, as the Schwarzschild slice is. With $R = \rho\cos\psi$, $au = \rho\sin\psi$ this is the expression of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.kerr-ring-count-misses-area-law}(2), which states it for $\rho \le a$; here it is proved directly, for $\rho > a$ as well.
\item \emph{(Its volume rate.)} The three-volume per unit Killing time, $V'(M, a, \rho) = 2\pi\int_{-1}^{1}\sqrt{\det h}\,du$, satisfies
\[
(1 - \delta)\Bigl(1 - \frac{\varepsilon}{3}\Bigr) \;\le\; \frac{V'(M, a, \rho)}{V'(M, 0, \rho)} \;\le\; 1 - \frac{\varepsilon}{12}, \qquad V'(M, 0, \rho) = 4\pi\rho^{3/2}\sqrt{2M - \rho},
\]
the last being the Schwarzschild slice volume, $8\pi M\sqrt{1 - \rho_{c}/2M}$ at $\rho = \rho_{c}$ (Proposition \claimref{singularity.stretched-singularity-count}). More precisely $V'(M, a, \rho)/V'(M, 0, \rho)$ lies between $(1 - \delta)\,G(\varepsilon)$ and $G(\varepsilon)$, $G(\varepsilon) = \tfrac12\int_{-1}^{1}(1 - \varepsilon u^{2})^{1/4}\,du$.
\item \emph{(The count.)} Count $\nu$ modes per Planck cell of the level set over the outer modular period $2\pi/\kappa_{+}$ (the rule of Proposition \claimref{singularity.stretched-singularity-count} with the epoch of Theorem \claimref{scrambling.epoch-modular-period-two-unknowns-become}, read with the Kerr surface gravity of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-kerr-surface-gravity-entropy}): $N = \nu V'\cdot 2\pi/\kappa_{+}$, and write $Q(M, a) = N/(A_{+}/4) = 2\nu V'/\sqrt{M^{2} - a^{2}}$. Then
\[
\frac{Q(M, a)}{Q(M, 0)} \;\le\; \frac{1 - \varepsilon/12}{\sqrt{1 - a^{2}/M^{2}}} \;<\; 1 ,
\]
whatever $\nu$. So no density $\nu$ and no level set $\rho(M) \le M/3$ chosen independently of the spin give the Kerr entropy $A_{+}/4$ both at $a = 0$ and at any $a$ with $0 < a \le \tfrac45\rho(M)$. The area law needs $V'(M, a, \rho)/V'(M, 0, \rho) = \sqrt{1 - a^{2}/M^{2}}$, a function of $a/M$; the count's ratio is at most $1 - a^{2}/(12\rho^{2})$ and, up to the factor $1 - \delta$, is the function $G(a^{2}/\rho^{2})$. The equality asked for is exact. At the stored density $\nu = 1/16\pi$ and $\rho = \rho_{c}$ the Schwarzschild count is $Q(M, 0) = \sqrt{1 - \rho_{c}/2M}$, equal to $1$ at leading order only. By item 3 the spin lowers $Q$ by a factor between $(1 - \delta)(1 - \varepsilon/3)/\sqrt{1 - a^{2}/M^{2}}$ and $(1 - \varepsilon/12)/\sqrt{1 - a^{2}/M^{2}}$: for $a/\rho$ bounded below this is a miss at leading order in $1/M$ (the deficit is at least $1 - (1 - \varepsilon/12)/\sqrt{1 - a^{2}/M^{2}}$, which tends to $\varepsilon/12$ as $\rho/M \to 0$), and for $a/\rho \to 0$ the count agrees with $A_{+}/4$ at leading order. At the Planck level set with $a = \tfrac45\rho_{c}$ the ratio $Q(M, a)$ is at most $\tfrac{71}{75}/\sqrt{1 - a^{2}/M^{2}}$ times its Schwarzschild value $Q(M, 0)$ for every $M \ge 8$, while the spin there is $a/M = \tfrac45(2M)^{1/3}/M$, which tends to zero as $M$ grows.
\end{enumerate}
The regime is that of slow rotation in the sense $a \le \tfrac45\rho$; with Theorem \claimref{synthesis.kerr-ring-count-misses-area-law}, which treats $a \ge 2\rho_{c}^{2}$, the literal cutoff count is shown to miss the area law at both ends of the spin range, and the window $\tfrac45\rho_{c} < a < 2\rho_{c}^{2}$ between is not treated. Only level sets of the modulus of the curvature scale are covered, and only level sets with $\rho \le M/3$. Reading Postulate \claimref{singularity.c1-curvature-cutoff} on Kerr through the modulus is the reading of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.kerr-ring-count-misses-area-law}; it is one choice among the algebraic curvature scalars of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.c1-c2-forms-forced-one-number}, which on Kerr are not functions of $|z|$ alone.
synthesis.no-spin-independent-modulus-le.technical:
For a Kerr field of mass $M$ and spin parameter $a$, take the surface on which the modulus of the curvature scale, $M|z|^{-3}$, has a fixed value, $|z| = \rho$, with $\rho \le M/3$ and $0 < a \le \tfrac45\rho$. It is a closed spacelike surface between the two horizon loci, $r = \sqrt{\rho^{2} - a^{2}u^{2}}$, and the determinant of its induced metric is $\rho^{2}[R(2M - R) - a^{2} - (1 - u^{2})a^{4}u^{2}/R^{2}]$ exactly, the case $R' = -a^{2}u/R$ of the general formula $-\Sigma[\Delta(R) + (1 - u^{2})R'^{2}]$ for a Killing-invariant surface $r = R(u)$.

Its three-volume per unit Killing time is at most $1 - a^{2}/(12\rho^{2})$ times the Schwarzschild value $4\pi\rho^{3/2}\sqrt{2M - \rho}$ and at least $(1 - \delta)(1 - a^{2}/(3\rho^{2}))$ times it, $\delta = \tfrac52 a^{2}/(\rho(2M - \rho))$. Counted with any fixed density over the outer modular period, the ratio of the count to $A_{+}/4$ is therefore smaller than its Schwarzschild value by the factor $(1 - a^{2}/12\rho^{2})/\sqrt{1 - a^{2}/M^{2}} < 1$ or more.

So, in this regime of slow rotation and for level sets of the modulus of the curvature scale with $\rho \le M/3$, no density and no level set chosen independently of the spin reproduce the Kerr entropy exactly at zero and at nonzero spin: the count depends on the spin through $a/\rho$ (and weakly through $\rho/M$), the area law through $a/M$. The equality refuted is exact; the Schwarzschild count itself meets the area law only at leading order. For $a/\rho$ bounded below the miss is of leading order in $1/M$, at least $\varepsilon/12$ in the limit; for $a/\rho \to 0$ the lower bound shows the count still agrees with $A_{+}/4$ at leading order. For the Planck level set $\rho_{c} = (2M)^{1/3}$ this holds for $M \ge 8$. With the stored result for $a \ge 2\rho_{c}^{2}$ the literal count misses the area law at both ends of the spin range; the window between is not treated.
synthesis.no-spin-independent-modulus-le.lay: The series counts a black hole's quantum modes on an inner surface where the gravitational field strength reaches a fixed value, and for a non-rotating hole that count matches the hole's entropy. An earlier result showed the same rule fails for fast-spinning holes. This one treats very slow rotation, assuming the same counting rule, and any fixed value of the field strength, not only the Planck one: the counting surface is then a slightly flattened closed surface inside the hole, and its volume, hence the count, drops with spin on a far smaller scale of spin than the entropy does. So no version of the rule of the kind covered here (surfaces on which the size of the field strength is fixed, lying deep inside the hole, at spins small compared with the size of that surface) reproduces the entropy of rotating holes exactly, and the shortfall is a few per cent when the spin parameter is comparable to the surface's size, however large the hole. For still smaller spin the shortfall shrinks to nothing. Rules that use the direction as well as the size of the field strength, and a middle range of spins, are not covered.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} The Kerr gauge field, its derived metric $g = \eta + 2H\,k\otimes k$ in oblate coordinates $(t, r, u, \phi)$ and the source's signature $(-,+,+,+)$, and the curvature scale of modulus $M|z|^{-3}$, $|z|^{2} = \Sigma = r^{2} + a^{2}u^{2}$, are those of Fact \claimref{interior.imported-kerr-schild-form-kerr-gauge} and Proposition \claimref{interior.complex-scale-inverse-cube-killing-spinor}. Throughout $\rho \le M/3$ and $0 < a \le \tfrac45\rho$.

\emph{(1).} $|z| = \rho$ with $r > 0$ is $r = R(u) = \sqrt{\rho^{2} - a^{2}u^{2}}$. Since $a^{2}u^{2} \le a^{2} \le \tfrac{16}{25}\rho^{2}$, $R \ge \tfrac35\rho$, and $R \le \rho \le M/3 < M \le r_{+}$. The horizon loci are the roots of $r^{2} - 2Mr + a^{2}$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-kerr-surface-gravity-entropy}), so $r_{+}r_{-} = a^{2}$ and $r_{-} = a^{2}/r_{+} \le a^{2}/M \le \tfrac{16}{25}\rho^{2}/M \le \tfrac{16}{75}\rho < \tfrac35\rho$. The surface is closed because $R > 0$ on all of $[-1, 1]$. For $\rho = \rho_{c}$, $\rho_{c} \le M/3$ reads $27\cdot 2M \le M^{3}$, that is $M^{2} \ge 54$, which holds for $M \ge 8$.

\emph{(2), the determinant lemma.} Let $r = R(u)$ be a surface invariant under both Killing flows and put $F = r - R(u)$. The coordinates $(t, F, u, \phi)$ have unit Jacobian against $(t, r, u, \phi)$, their coordinate vectors are $\partial_{t}$, $\partial_{r}$, $\partial_{u} + R'\partial_{r}$, $\partial_{\phi}$, and the induced metric $h$ on $F = 0$ in $(t, u, \phi)$ is the block of $g$ complementary to $F$. By the cofactor rule for the inverse matrix, $\det h = \det g\cdot g^{-1}(dF, dF)$. In the Kerr-Schild gauge $g = \eta + 2H\,k\otimes k$ with $k$ null for $\eta$ (Fact \claimref{interior.imported-kerr-schild-form-kerr-gauge}), so by the rank-one rule $\det g = \det\eta\,(1 + 2H\,\eta^{-1}(k, k)) = \det\eta = -\Sigma^{2}$, and $g^{-1} = \eta^{-1} - 2H\,k^{\sharp}\otimes k^{\sharp}$ with $k^{\sharp} = \eta^{-1}k = (1, -1, 0, a/P)$. Hence $g^{rr} = P/\Sigma - 2Mr/\Sigma = \Delta/\Sigma$, $g^{uu} = (1 - u^{2})/\Sigma$, $g^{ru} = 0$, and, with $dF = dr - R'du$,
\[
\det h = -\Sigma^{2}\bigl[g^{rr} + R'^{2}g^{uu}\bigr] = -\Sigma\bigl[\Delta(R) + (1 - u^{2})R'^{2}\bigr] .
\]
Replacing $\partial_{t}$ by $\partial_{t} + \Omega\,\partial_{\phi}$ is a shear of the tangent frame, of unit determinant, so the Gram determinant is unchanged. In the store's product every inner product changes sign, and a $3 \times 3$ determinant with it. On the level set, $\Sigma = \rho^{2}$ and $R' = -a^{2}u/R$, so
\[
\det h = \rho^{2}\Bigl[2MR - R^{2} - a^{2} - \frac{(1 - u^{2})a^{4}u^{2}}{R^{2}}\Bigr] = \rho^{2}B(u) .
\]
The check computes the Gram determinant directly from the Kerr-Schild components at 25 rational points, for $\partial_{t}$ and for $\partial_{t} + \Omega\partial_{\phi}$, and once in $\Cl(1,3)$ with the store's product from the gauge field $\hb^{-1}(b) = b - H\,(b\cdot k)\,k$; these are consistency checks of the identity just proved. With $R = \rho\cos\psi$, $au = \rho\sin\psi$ the expression is that of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.kerr-ring-count-misses-area-law}(2) multiplied by $(du/d\psi)^{2}$; that theorem states it for $\rho \le a$, and it is proved here directly. Upper bound: $R(\rho - R) = R\,a^{2}u^{2}/(\rho + R) \le a^{2}u^{2} \le a^{2}$, so $R(2M - R) - a^{2} \le R(2M - \rho)$, and the last term of $B$ is not positive; hence $B \le R(2M - \rho)$. Lower bound: $R(2M - R) \ge R(2M - \rho)$, and, with $u^{2}(1 - u^{2}) \le \tfrac14$ and $R^{2} \ge \tfrac{9}{25}\rho^{2} \ge \tfrac{9}{16}a^{2}$, $a^{2} + (1 - u^{2})a^{4}u^{2}/R^{2} \le a^{2}(1 + \tfrac49) = \tfrac{13}{9}a^{2}$; dividing by $R(2M - \rho) \ge \tfrac35\rho(2M - \rho)$ gives $B \ge R(2M - \rho)(1 - \tfrac{65}{27}a^{2}/(\rho(2M - \rho))) \ge (1 - \delta)R(2M - \rho)$. Finally $\delta \le \tfrac52\cdot\tfrac{16}{25}\rho/(2M - \rho) \le \tfrac85\cdot\tfrac15 < 1$ because $2M - \rho \ge 5\rho$, so $B > 0$ and $\det h > 0$: the induced metric is positive definite, since a nondegenerate three-plane of a metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ has signature $(+,+,+)$ or $(-,+,+)$ and only the first has positive determinant.

\emph{(3).} $V' = 2\pi\int_{-1}^{1}\rho\sqrt{B}\,du$, the $\phi$ integral giving $2\pi$. By (2), with $\sqrt{1 - \delta} \ge 1 - \delta$,
\[
(1 - \delta)\,2\pi\rho\sqrt{2M - \rho}\int_{-1}^{1}R^{1/2}du \;\le\; V' \;\le\; 2\pi\rho\sqrt{2M - \rho}\int_{-1}^{1}R^{1/2}du ,
\]
and $\int_{-1}^{1}R^{1/2}du = \rho^{1/2}\int_{-1}^{1}(1 - \varepsilon u^{2})^{1/4}du = 2\rho^{1/2}G(\varepsilon)$, so $V'$ lies between $(1 - \delta)G(\varepsilon)$ and $G(\varepsilon)$ times $4\pi\rho^{3/2}\sqrt{2M - \rho}$, which is $V'(M, 0, \rho)$ ($B = \rho(2M - \rho)$ at $a = 0$). For $0 \le x \le 1$: $(1 - x/4)^{4} - (1 - x) = x^{2}(\tfrac38 - \tfrac{x}{16} + \tfrac{x^{2}}{256}) \ge 0$, so $(1 - x)^{1/4} \le 1 - x/4$; and $(1 - x)^{1/4} \ge 1 - x$. With $x = \varepsilon u^{2}$ and $\int_{-1}^{1}u^{2}du = \tfrac23$: $1 - \varepsilon/3 \le G(\varepsilon) \le 1 - \varepsilon/12$. On $\rho^{3} = 2M$, $4\pi\rho^{3/2}\sqrt{2M - \rho} = 4\pi\sqrt{2M}\sqrt{2M}\sqrt{1 - \rho/2M} = 8\pi M\sqrt{1 - \rho/2M}$, the slice volume of Proposition \claimref{singularity.stretched-singularity-count}.

\emph{(4).} The count rule is that of Proposition \claimref{singularity.stretched-singularity-count}, $\nu$ modes per Planck cell of the surface per unit Killing time, and the epoch is the modular period of Theorem \claimref{scrambling.epoch-modular-period-two-unknowns-become}, read on Kerr with the outer surface gravity. By Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-kerr-surface-gravity-entropy}, $\kappa_{+} = \sqrt{M^{2} - a^{2}}/(2Mr_{+})$ and $A_{+}/4 = 2\pi Mr_{+}$, so $N/(A_{+}/4) = \nu V'\cdot(4\pi Mr_{+}/\sqrt{M^{2} - a^{2}})/(2\pi Mr_{+}) = 2\nu V'/\sqrt{M^{2} - a^{2}}$, and $Q(M, a)/Q(M, 0) = (V'(M, a, \rho)/V'(M, 0, \rho))\cdot M/\sqrt{M^{2} - a^{2}} \le (1 - \varepsilon/12)/\sqrt{1 - a^{2}/M^{2}}$ by (3); $\nu$ cancels. Strictness: as $\varepsilon \le \tfrac{16}{25}$, $\varepsilon^{2}/144 \le \varepsilon/225$, so $(1 - \varepsilon/12)^{2} \le 1 - \varepsilon(\tfrac16 - \tfrac1{225})$, while $a^{2}/M^{2} = \varepsilon\rho^{2}/M^{2} \le \varepsilon/9 < \varepsilon(\tfrac16 - \tfrac1{225})$; hence $(1 - \varepsilon/12)^{2} < 1 - a^{2}/M^{2}$. If a density $\nu$ and a level set $\rho(M)$, both independent of $a$, gave $Q(M, 0) = 1$ and $Q(M, a) = 1$ for some $0 < a \le \tfrac45\rho(M)$, the ratio would be $1$, against the strict inequality. At $a = \tfrac45\rho_{c}$, $1 - \varepsilon/12 = 1 - \tfrac{16}{300} = \tfrac{71}{75}$.

synthesis.number-diagonal-dynamics-sprea.technical:
Every generator the locality premise (L$_{E}$) allows is diagonal in the joint number basis. For such a generator the Heisenberg evolution of a mode operator is exact and elementary: $v_{j}(t) = v_{j}e^{-2JtH_{1}}$, where $H_{1}$ collects the terms of the generator that contain $\sigma_{j}$, stripped of it. The evolved operator is $v_{j}$ dressed by a diagonal unitary of the modes coupled directly to $j$, and nothing else.

So operator support never travels along chains: a mode that is reached only through a chain of couplings is never reached at any time, and out-of-time-order correlators with such modes stay constant. Support does grow onto the directly coupled modes: for two-body couplings the dressing is a product of single-mode rotations, and the average operator size is $\sum_{k}\sin^{2}2g_{jk}t$, bounded by the number of direct couplings and recurring towards zero. With uniform all-to-all couplings it reaches half the window at $t = \pi/(8g)$, independently of the number of modes: support growth in a time that does not grow with $n$, but no exponential growth of size, commutators or out-of-time-order correlators, all of which are almost periodic.

A hop, which (L$_{E}$) excludes, does propagate support one mode per order. Hence the fast-scrambling law's exponential growth step, already read as an imaginary-time rotor-flow step for quadratic generators, has no real-time reading for any dynamics (L$_{E}$) admits: the law $t_{*} = \kappa^{-1}\ln N$ in real time and (L$_{E}$) cannot both hold.
synthesis.number-diagonal-dynamics-sprea.lay: The series models a black hole's boundary as a collection of quantum bits and claims that information spreads through them as fast as physics allows. The series also assumes that the bits' internal dynamics never moves anything from one bit to another; it may only make each bit's phase depend on its neighbours' states. This result shows that such dynamics spreads a disturbance only to the bits it is directly wired to, which may be all of them, never onward to their neighbours in turn, and that its reach oscillates instead of growing exponentially. So the exponential spreading law the series describes cannot happen in real time under its own locality assumption; one of the two must give.

proofs.main:
\emph{Relations.} By Theorem \claimref{singularity.modular-structure-completed-pair}, $\sigma_{j} = 2N_{j} - 1$ with $N_{j} = v_{j}^{*}v_{j}$. Since $v_{j}N_{j} = v_{j}(1 - v_{j}v_{j}^{*}) = v_{j}$ and $N_{j}v_{j} = v_{j}^{*}v_{j}v_{j} = 0$, we get $v_{j}\sigma_{j} = v_{j}$ and $\sigma_{j}v_{j} = -v_{j}$. For $k \neq j$, $\sigma_{k}$ is a product of two odd elements of mode $k$, each anticommuting with $v_{j}$, so $\sigma_{k}$ commutes with $v_{j}$. The decomposition $H = H_{0}^{(j)} + \sigma_{j}H_{1}^{(j)}$ exists and is unique because $\mathcal{D}$ is spanned by the monomials $\sigma_{S}$, $S \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}$, linearly independent, and those containing $\sigma_{j}$ are $\sigma_{j}$ times those not containing it; $H = H^{*}$ makes $H_{0}^{(j)}, H_{1}^{(j)}$ self-adjoint.

\emph{(i)} $Hv_{j} = H_{0}^{(j)}v_{j} + \sigma_{j}H_{1}^{(j)}v_{j} = v_{j}H_{0}^{(j)} + \sigma_{j}v_{j}H_{1}^{(j)} = v_{j}H_{0}^{(j)} - v_{j}H_{1}^{(j)}$ and $v_{j}H = v_{j}H_{0}^{(j)} + v_{j}\sigma_{j}H_{1}^{(j)} = v_{j}H_{0}^{(j)} + v_{j}H_{1}^{(j)}$, so $\operatorname{ad}_{H}(v_{j}) = -2v_{j}H_{1}^{(j)}$. Since $H_{1}^{(j)}$ commutes with $H$ (both lie in the abelian $\mathcal{D}$), $\operatorname{ad}_{H}(v_{j}Y) = \operatorname{ad}_{H}(v_{j})Y$ for $Y \in \mathcal{D}$, and induction gives $\operatorname{ad}_{H}^{m}(v_{j}) = v_{j}(-2H_{1}^{(j)})^{m}$. Summing the exponential series in finite dimension, $e^{JtH}v_{j}e^{-JtH} = \sum_{m}\tfrac{(Jt)^{m}}{m!}\operatorname{ad}_{H}^{m}(v_{j}) = v_{j}e^{-2JtH_{1}^{(j)}}$. The script builds four modes in $\Cl(4,4)$, checks $v\sigma = v$ and $\sigma v = -v$, and verifies the closed form of $\operatorname{ad}_{H}^{m}(v_{0})$ for $m = 1, \dots, 5$ with a field on mode $0$, chain couplings $\sigma_{0}\sigma_{1}$, $\sigma_{1}\sigma_{2}$, $\sigma_{2}\sigma_{3}$ and a field on mode $3$, with and without a three-body term $\sigma_{0}\sigma_{1}\sigma_{2}$.

\emph{(ii)} $e^{-2JtH_{1}^{(j)}}$ is a polynomial in the $\sigma_{k}$, $k \in N(j)$, so the evolved operator involves only modes in $\{j\}\cup N(j)$. For $l \notin \{j\}\cup N(j)$, $v_{l}$ anticommutes with $v_{j}$ and commutes with every $\sigma_{k}$, $k \neq l$, hence anticommutes with $v_{j}e^{-2JtH_{1}^{(j)}}$; likewise $v_{l}^{*}$. An out-of-time-order correlator $\omega(X(t)^{*}W^{*}X(t)W)$ with $X = v_{j}$ and $W \in \{v_{l}, v_{l}^{*}\}$ then equals $-\omega(X(t)^{*}X(t)W^{*}W)$ and $X(t)^{*}X(t) = e^{2JtH_{1}}N_{j}e^{-2JtH_{1}} = N_{j}$, so it is constant in $t$. The script checks that $\operatorname{ad}_{H}^{m}(v_{0})$ never involves mode $3$, involves mode $2$ exactly when the three-body term is present, and, with the exact unitary $U = \cos\theta + J\sin\theta\,\sigma_{0}\sigma_{1}$ ($\cos\theta = \tfrac35$, $\sin\theta = \tfrac45$, Gaussian-rational coefficients), that $Uv_{0}U^{-1}$ anticommutes with $v_{3}$ and $v_{3}^{*}$ and not with $v_{1}$.

\emph{(iii)} With $H_{1}^{(j)} = h_{j} + \sum_{k}g_{jk}\sigma_{k}$ the terms commute and $\sigma_{k}^{2} = 1$, so $e^{-2JtH_{1}^{(j)}} = e^{-2Jh_{j}t}\prod_{k}(\cos 2g_{jk}t - J\sin 2g_{jk}t\,\sigma_{k})$. Expanding, $v_{j}(t) = e^{-2Jh_{j}t}\sum_{S}c_{S}v_{j}\sigma_{S}$ with $c_{S} = \prod_{k \notin S}\cos 2g_{jk}t\prod_{k \in S}(-J\sin 2g_{jk}t)$. In the trace inner product, $(v_{j}\sigma_{S})^{*}v_{j}\sigma_{T} = N_{j}\sigma_{S}\sigma_{T}$, whose trace vanishes unless $S = T$ (the $\sigma_{k}$, $k \neq j$, are traceless, independent and commute with $N_{j}$), so the $v_{j}\sigma_{S}$ are orthogonal of equal norm and $|c_{S}|^{2}$ is the weight on $S$; these weights sum to $\prod_{k}(\cos^{2} + \sin^{2}) = 1$ and the mean of $|S|$ is $\sum_{k}\sin^{2}2g_{jk}t \le |N(j)|$, a finite sum of periodic functions, hence almost periodic, and zero at $t = 0$. For $n - 1$ couplings equal to $g$ it is $(n-1)\sin^{2}2gt$, first equal to $(n-1)/2$ at $2gt = \pi/4$. The script checks, with all-to-all couplings of mode $0$ to modes $1, 2, 3$ and $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta) = (\tfrac35, \tfrac45)$, that the exact $U = \prod_{k}(\cos\theta + J\sin\theta\,\sigma_{0}\sigma_{k})$ is unitary, that $Uv_{0}U^{-1} = v_{0}\prod_{k}(\cos 2\theta - J\sin 2\theta\,\sigma_{k})$ with $(\cos 2\theta, \sin 2\theta) = (-\tfrac{7}{25}, \tfrac{24}{25})$, and that the size weights sum to $1$ with mean $3\sin^{2}2\theta = \tfrac{1728}{625}$.

\emph{(iv)} With $H = 2\sigma_{0}\sigma_{1} + (v_{1}^{*}v_{2} + v_{2}^{*}v_{1}) + (v_{2}^{*}v_{3} + v_{3}^{*}v_{2})$ the script finds the highest mode in $\operatorname{ad}_{H}^{m}(v_{0})$ to be $1, 2, 3$ for $m = 1, 2, 3$: a hop carries support one mode per order.

\emph{Consequence.} Proposition \claimref{singularity.number-diagonal-dynamics-models-scrambling-derived} puts every generator (L$_{E}$) admits in $\mathcal{D}$. By (i) to (iii) no such generator moves support along a chain of couplings. Support does grow onto the directly coupled modes, and with all-to-all couplings the mean size reaches half the window at $t = \pi/(8g)$ for every $n$, a time that does not depend on the number of modes. No exponential growth occurs: $e^{-2JtH_{1}^{(j)}}$ is a finite sum of terms $e^{-2J\lambda t}P_{\lambda}$ over the eigenvalues $\lambda$ of $H_{1}^{(j)}$ with spectral projections $P_{\lambda}$, so every matrix element of $v_{j}(t)$, every matrix element of a commutator $[v_{j}(t), W]$ and every out-of-time-order correlator of $v_{j}(t)$ with a fixed $W$ is a finite combination of $e^{J\omega t}$ with real $\omega$, hence bounded and almost periodic, and the commutator norm stays below $2\|W\|$. The expansion step of Proposition \claimref{scrambling.spreading-law-chaos-bound-saturated}, an amplitude at mode distance $d$ growing as $e^{\kappa t}$, needs support at distance $d \ge 2$, which by (ii) is zero in real time; for quadratic generators Theorem \claimref{synthesis.phase-flow-is-time-rotor-flow-kms-continuation}(iii) already shows the unitary flow is trigonometric, and the present result removes the non-quadratic diagonal generators as well.

synthesis.quadratic-flows-cannot-thermal.formal:
Let $\mathfrak{A}$ be the boundary-mode CAR algebra, realised on each window by null pairs ($a_{j}$, $a_{j}^{*}$ with $\{a_{i}, a_{j}^{*}\} = \delta_{ij}$; Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-algebra-boundary-modes-car-algebra}), its numbers and one-particle matrices read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$, $J = e_{2}e_{3}$ the complex unit of the radial atom from which the boundary modes descend (\claimref{synthesis.transverse-bivector-is-the-complex-unit-of-the-radial-atom}), and $\omega_{I}$ the I-state at $\beta$ with occupations $n_{j}^{I} = (1 + e^{\beta\omega_{j}})^{-1}$ (Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state}). Hypothesis (T): the time evolution of a window is generated either by a quadratic element $H = H^{*}$, or by an element of the abelian algebra generated by the $\sigma_{k} = 2N_{k} - 1$ (the generators (L$_E$) permits, Proposition \claimref{singularity.number-diagonal-dynamics-models-scrambling-derived}), or by a sum of the boost generator $\sum_{j}\omega_{j}N_{j}$ and such an element.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Conserved charges.)} For a Hermitian one-particle matrix $k$ and $X_{k} = \sum_{ij}k_{ij}a_{i}^{*}a_{j}$, every $Q_{n} := X_{k^{n}}$ ($n \ge 0$) commutes with $X_{k}$, so $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{JtX_{k}})$ conserves the occupations of the eigenmodes of $k$; for the boost dynamics ($k = \operatorname{diag}(\omega_{j})$) these are the $N_{j}$. Every element of the algebra generated by the $\sigma_{k}$, alone or added to the boost generator, also commutes with every $N_{j}$ (for example $\sigma_{1}\sigma_{3}$). A term that moves occupation between modes, such as $(a_{1}^{*}a_{2} + a_{2}^{*}a_{1})N_{3}$, does not commute with $N_{1}$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(No relaxation.)} Under (T), for every state $\omega$ of the descent and every $t$, the conserved occupations keep their initial values, and $\omega\circ\alpha_{t} \to \omega_{I}$ on a window, in any sense that implies convergence of the expectations of the $N_{j}$ (of the eigenmode occupations, for a quadratic $H$ with eigenmodes other than the $a_{j}$), holds only if those occupations already have their I-state values. For a quasi-free $\omega$ with one-particle correlation matrix $C$, a quadratic evolution acts as $C \mapsto UCU^{*}$ with $U$ unitary, which keeps the spectrum of $C$ and every $\operatorname{tr}(k^{n}C)$; under the boost dynamics it keeps the diagonal of $C$ and multiplies the coherence $C_{ij} = \omega(a_{j}^{*}a_{i})$ by $e^{-J(\omega_{i} - \omega_{j})t}$ and the pairing $\omega(a_{i}a_{j})$ by $e^{-J(\omega_{i} + \omega_{j})t}$. Gauge invariance can be reached by dephasing; the Fermi-Dirac symbol cannot.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Restriction reaches it.)} The pure pair state $c\ket{00} + s\ket{11}$ of a mode and a partner restricts on the mode to the gauge-invariant state with occupation $s^{2}$, the Gibbs state at $e^{-\beta\omega} = s^{2}/c^{2}$; it is the I-state's restriction to that mode if and only if $s^{2} = n^{I}$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(For the descent.)} Relaxing a non-equilibrium descent state to the I-state therefore needs dynamics that moves occupation between modes, which (L$_E$) excludes. So, under (T), and in particular under (L$_E$), the descent must deposit the Fermi-Dirac occupations directly, mode by mode, for instance as the restriction of pure pair states as in (iii) (the thermofield double on a horizon pair).
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.quadratic-flows-cannot-thermal.technical:
Assume the time evolution of a window is generated by a quadratic element, or by the number-diagonal generators that the locality premise (L$_E$) permits, or by the boost generator plus such terms. A quadratic flow with one-particle matrix $k$ conserves the occupations of $k$'s eigenmodes; for the boost dynamics these are the mode occupations themselves, and number-diagonal products such as $\sigma_{1}\sigma_{3}$ conserve every mode occupation too. So under any of these dynamics a state of the descent keeps its occupations for ever: if they are not the Fermi-Dirac values of the I-state at $\beta$, it never relaxes to the I-state. What these flows change is phases: coherences and pairings rotate and, in a large system, dephase, which can restore gauge invariance but not the thermal symbol. Only a term that moves occupation between modes, such as a hop weighted by a third occupation, breaks the conservation, and (L$_E$) excludes such terms.

The I-state is reached instead by restriction: a pure pair of a mode and a partner with amplitudes $c$, $s$ restricts to the Gibbs state at $e^{-\beta\omega} = s^{2}/c^{2}$, as the thermofield double does on a horizon pair. So, under these hypotheses, the descent must deposit the thermal occupations directly.
synthesis.quadratic-flows-cannot-thermal.lay: After the descent, the framework's black-hole-like modes sit in a particular thermal state. A natural guess is that the descent leaves them out of equilibrium and they then settle into that thermal state, as a hot cup of coffee cools. This result shows that, assuming the modes evolve only by the kinds of motion the framework allows, they cannot settle: those motions never change how many particles sit in each mode, so a state that starts with the wrong numbers keeps them for ever. Only the relative phases between modes wash out. Settling would need an interaction that moves occupation between modes, which the framework's locality premise excludes. The thermal state can still arise, but in a different way: as one half of a larger pure state, which is how the thermal radiation of a horizon arises. So the descent must produce the thermal numbers directly.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i)} With $X_{k} = \sum_{ij}k_{ij}a_{i}^{*}a_{j}$ and the CAR of the null pairs (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-algebra-boundary-modes-car-algebra}), $[a_{i}^{*}a_{j}, a_{l}^{*}a_{m}] = \delta_{jl}a_{i}^{*}a_{m} - \delta_{im}a_{l}^{*}a_{j}$, so $[X_{k}, X_{k'}] = X_{[k, k']}$. Since $[k, k^{n}] = 0$, $[X_{k}, Q_{n}] = 0$ for every $n$. If $k = \sum_{\alpha}\epsilon_{\alpha}P_{\alpha}$ is its spectral decomposition, the $Q_{n} = \sum_{\alpha}\epsilon_{\alpha}^{n}X_{P_{\alpha}}$ span the eigenmode occupations $X_{P_{\alpha}}$ (Vandermonde), which are therefore conserved. For $k = \operatorname{diag}(\omega_{j})$ the $X_{P_{\alpha}}$ are sums of the $N_{j} = a_{j}^{*}a_{j}$ with equal frequency, and $[X_{k}, N_{j}] = 0$ directly. The check realises the CAR in $\Cl(3,3)$ by null pairs, $a_{j} = \tfrac12(e_{j} + f_{j})$, $a_{j}^{*} = \tfrac12(e_{j} - f_{j})$, $e_{j}^{2} = 1$, $f_{j}^{2} = -1$, and verifies the relations, $[X_{k}, Q_{n}] = 0$ for $n \le 3$ with a generic rational $k$, $[X_{k}, N_{1}] \neq 0$ (site occupations move), $[\sum_{j}\omega_{j}N_{j}, N_{l}] = 0$, all exactly. The products of the $\sigma_{k} = 2N_{k} - 1$ are polynomials in commuting number operators, so they commute with every $N_{j}$, alone or added to $\sum_{j}\omega_{j}N_{j}$, as Proposition \claimref{singularity.number-diagonal-dynamics-models-scrambling-derived} records under (L$_E$); the check verifies $[\sum_{j}\omega_{j}N_{j} + \sigma_{j}\sigma_{k}, N_{l}] = 0$ for all $j < k$ and $l$, and $[(a_{1}^{*}a_{2} + a_{2}^{*}a_{1})N_{3}, N_{1}] = (a_{2}^{*}a_{1} - a_{1}^{*}a_{2})N_{3} \neq 0$.

\emph{(ii)} A $*$-automorphism $\alpha$ with $\alpha(X) = X$ for a conserved $X$ gives $\omega(\alpha(X)) = \omega(X)$, so $\omega\circ\tau_{t}(N_{j}) = \omega(N_{j})$ for the boost dynamics of Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics}. If $\omega\circ\tau_{t}$ converged to $\omega_{I}$ on a window in a sense implying convergence of the expectation of $N_{j}$, the constant sequence $\omega(N_{j})$ would converge to $\omega_{I}(N_{j}) = n_{j}^{I}$ (Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state}(1)), so $\omega(N_{j}) = n_{j}^{I}$. For quasi-free states, a quadratic time evolution is a Bogoliubov unitary $U$ on the one-particle space (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.phase-flow-is-time-rotor-flow-kms-continuation}(iii)), and $C_{ij} = \omega(a_{j}^{*}a_{i})$ goes to $UCU^{*}$; $\operatorname{tr}((UCU^{*})^{m}) = \operatorname{tr}(C^{m})$ and $\operatorname{tr}(k^{n}UCU^{*}) = \operatorname{tr}(k^{n}C)$ when $U$ commutes with $k$. For $U = e^{-Jtk}$ with $k$ diagonal, $(UCU^{*})_{ij} = e^{-J(\omega_{i} - \omega_{j})t}C_{ij}$ and the pairing $\omega(a_{i}a_{j})$ acquires $e^{-J(\omega_{i} + \omega_{j})t}$. The check replaces $e^{-Jtk}$ by its Cayley form $(1 - Jsk)(1 + Jsk)^{-1}$, which is exactly unitary over $\mathbb{Q}(J) = \mathrm{span}_{\mathbb{Q}}\{1, J\}$ and commutes with $k$, and verifies on a three-mode state with occupations $(\tfrac12, 0, \tfrac13)$ and nonzero coherences that the diagonal is unchanged over repeated steps and never equals the Fermi-Dirac values $(\tfrac14, \tfrac18, \tfrac1{16})$ (at $e^{\beta\omega_{j}} = 3, 7, 15$), that coherence moduli are kept while their phases move, and that for a generic $k$ the invariants $\operatorname{tr}(k^{n}C)$ and $\operatorname{tr}(C^{m})$ are kept while the site occupations change. That the coherences and pairings average to zero in an infinite window with continuous frequency spectrum (Riemann-Lebesgue), leaving the gauge-invariant state with the conserved occupations, is the standard dephasing of free fermions towards the generalized Gibbs ensemble (Rigol, Dunjko, Yurovsky and Olshanii, 2007; for quasi-free fermions Gluza, Eisert and Farrelly, 2019; both cited from memory); only the finite-window statements are proved here.

\emph{(iii)} In the basis $\ket{00}, \ket{01}, \ket{10}, \ket{11}$ (mode, partner) the pure state $c\ket{00} + s\ket{11}$, $c^{2} + s^{2} = 1$, has reduced density matrix $\operatorname{diag}(c^{2}, s^{2})$ on the mode: no coherence, occupation $s^{2}$, ratio $s^{2}/c^{2}$, which is the Gibbs state of $\omega N$ at $e^{-\beta\omega} = s^{2}/c^{2}$ and has $s^{2} = (1 + e^{\beta\omega})^{-1}$. The check verifies this at three rational points.

\emph{(iv)} Hypothesis (T) is a hypothesis, not a theorem of the store: Lemma \claimref{scrambling.clock-inventory-boundary-modes}(i) shows that the intrinsic (grade-preserving inner) flows are bivector-generated, hence quadratic, and Proposition \claimref{synthesis.phase-flow-is-time-rotor-flow-kms-continuation}(iii) shows that a quadratic $H = H^{*}$ generates a $*$-automorphic Bogoliubov flow, but neither asserts that a window's time evolution is quadratic; the number-diagonal alternative is the class of generators (L$_E$) admits (Proposition \claimref{singularity.number-diagonal-dynamics-models-scrambling-derived}), which includes quartic cross-point products. For gauge-invariant quadratic $H$, (i) and (ii) apply as stated; with pairing terms the same argument runs in the doubled (Nambu) one-particle space, where the flow is a Bogoliubov unitary commuting with the doubled one-particle matrix and conserves the quasi-particle occupations of its eigenmodes. For number-diagonal generators every $N_{j}$ is conserved, so (ii) applies with the $N_{j}$ themselves. In each case the descent state relaxes to $\omega_{I}$ only if the conserved occupations already have their I-state values, which (iii) shows a pure pair state can supply by restriction. A generator that changes some conserved occupation must contain terms off-diagonal in the joint number basis of the conserved modes, that is, terms moving occupation between modes, which is what (L$_E$) excludes. The statement is a no-go for relaxation under (T), not a determination of the descent state.
