synthesis.quarter-from-temperature.formal:
Assume (P) (Premise \claimref{singularity.p-univalence}) and (R) (Premise \claimref{singularity.r-regularity-fixed-locus}), so that the boundary modes of a Schwarzschild hole of mass $M$ are thermal at $T(M) = \kappa/2\pi = 1/8\pi M$ (Theorem \claimref{singularity.rate-discharge-hypothesis-iii}, Proposition \claimref{singularity.plane-rate}). Suppose, as Hawking did, that the hole is a thermodynamic system along the Schwarzschild family at this temperature: its internal energy is $M$ (not the boundary modes' Killing energy, which is below $TS = M/2$), its entropy $S(M)$ obeys the Clausius relation $dS = dM/T$, and $S \to 0$ as $M \to 0$. Then
\[
S(M) \;=\; \int_{0}^{M} 8\pi M'\,dM' \;=\; 4\pi M^{2} \;=\; \frac{A}{4}, \qquad A = 16\pi M^{2},
\]
the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy with its quarter, and no calibration enters. Equivalently, along the family $dM = (\kappa/8\pi)\,dA$ identically, so $dS = dA/4$. The quarter is fixed by the period of (R), $2\pi/\kappa$, and by nothing else: had (R) fixed a period $p$ in place of $2\pi/\kappa$, the entropy would be $S = (p\kappa/2\pi)\,A/4$.
synthesis.quarter-from-temperature.technical: The singularity paper fixes the black hole's temperature at $1/8\pi M$, given its regularity premise (R). If the hole is an ordinary thermodynamic system at that temperature, its mass the internal energy and its entropy changing by $dM/T$ when the mass changes, then integrating gives exactly $4\pi M^{2}$, a quarter of the horizon area. This is Hawking's original argument for the quarter, run on the series' own temperature, and it is standard physics rather than a new result. What it shows for the series is that the quarter is not a separate calibration: it is fixed by the period in (R). It does not say which modes carry the entropy. A different period would rescale the entropy by the same factor.
synthesis.quarter-from-temperature.lay: The famous factor of one quarter in a black hole's entropy is not an extra number the framework has to supply. Once the framework fixes the hole's temperature, as it does under one smoothness assumption, the ordinary law linking heat, energy and entropy gives the entropy as a quarter of the horizon's area, provided the hole behaves as an ordinary thermodynamic system; this is Hawking's argument, and it does not by itself say which modes carry the entropy.

proofs.main: By Theorem \claimref{singularity.rate-discharge-hypothesis-iii}, under (P, \claimref{singularity.p-univalence}) and (R, \claimref{singularity.r-regularity-fixed-locus}) every boundary mode is thermal at $T = \kappa/2\pi$, and $\kappa = 1/4M$ (Proposition \claimref{singularity.plane-rate}), so $T(M) = 1/8\pi M$ and $1/T = 8\pi M$. The Clausius relation along the family, the hypothesis of Hawking's argument, gives $dS/dM = 8\pi M$, and with $S(0) = 0$, $S(M) = 4\pi M^{2}$. The horizon is at $r = 2M$, of area $A = 4\pi(2M)^{2} = 16\pi M^{2}$, so $S = A/4$. Along the family $dA/dM = 32\pi M$ and $\kappa/8\pi = 1/32\pi M$, so $dM = (\kappa/8\pi)\,dA$ identically and $dS = dM/T = (2\pi/\kappa)(\kappa/8\pi)\,dA = dA/4$. If the period were $p$ instead of $2\pi/\kappa$, then $1/T = p$ and $dS = p\,dM = p(\kappa/8\pi)\,dA$, so $S = (p\kappa/2\pi)\,A/4$: the quarter is the period of (R) and nothing else.

synthesis.quarter-turn-rotors-of-the-eve.formal:
Let $\Cl(p,q)$ have $p + q = 2N \ge 4$ generators $e_{1}, \dots, e_{2N}$ with $N + q$ odd, so that the pseudoscalar $I = e_{1}\cdots e_{2N}$ has $I^{2} = -1$ ($\Cl(1,3)$, $\Cl(3,1)$, $\Cl(6,0)$, $\Cl(7,1)$ are examples); $I$ commutes with the even subalgebra $E$. Put $D = 2^{N-1}$. Call two even blades $e_{S}$, $e_{T}$ (notation of \claimref{synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra}) equivalent when $T = S$ or $T$ is the complement of $S$; since $Ie_{S} = \pm e_{S^{c}}$ and $(Ie_{S})^{2} = -e_{S}^{2}$, each class $c$ contains, up to sign, exactly one element $h_{c}$ of square $+1$, its \emph{unit}; $h_{0} = 1$. The classes form the $\mathbb{F}_{2}$-space $V$ of even subsets modulo the full set, of dimension $2N - 2$, with $D^{2}$ elements, and $b(c,d) \in \mathbb{F}_{2}$, equal to $1$ exactly when $h_{c}$ and $h_{d}$ anticommute, is the polar form of that theorem restricted to even subsets; it is alternating and nondegenerate on $V$. The $h_{c}$ and $Ih_{c}$ form a basis of $E$; $h_{c}h_{d} = \pm h_{c+d}$ when $b(c,d) = 0$ and $\pm Ih_{c+d}$ when $b(c,d) = 1$; for $b(c,d) = 0$, $c \ne d$, write $h_{c}h_{d} = \epsilon(c,d)h_{c+d}$. A \emph{state} is an idempotent $\rho = D^{-1}\bigl(1 + \sum_{c \ne 0}x_{c}h_{c}\bigr)$ of $E$ with rational or real coordinates $x_{c} = D\langle\rho h_{c}\rangle_{0}$. Let $\Gamma$ be the group of automorphisms of $E$ generated by the conjugations by the \emph{quarter-turn elements} $R_{c} = 1 + k_{c}$, $k_{c} = Ih_{c}$ a blade with $k_{c}^{2} = -1$, $c \ne 0$ (unnormalised; $R_{c}^{-1} = \tfrac12(1 - k_{c})$), and for a function $f$ of states let $\langle f\rangle_{\Gamma}(\rho)$ be the mean of $f(g\rho g^{-1})$ over $g \in \Gamma$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The group; proved, the two orders computed.)} Conjugation by $R_{c}$ fixes $I$ and $h_{d}$ when $b(c,d) = 0$ and sends $h_{d}$ to $-Ih_{d}h_{c} = \pm h_{c+d}$ when $b(c,d) = 1$: on $V$ it is the transvection $d \mapsto d + b(c,d)c$. $\Gamma$ is finite, contains the conjugation by every $h_{c}$ (which is $R_{c}^{2}$ up to the central factor $2I$), carries states to states, and acts transitively on the nonzero classes and on the ordered pairs $(c,d)$ of distinct nonzero classes with $b(c,d) = 0$. For $N = 2$ it has order $24$ (in $\Cl(1,3)$ the $R_{c}$ are $1$ plus the spatial bivectors and $\Gamma$ is the rotation group of the cube acting on the relative vectors) and for $\Cl(6,0)$ order $11520$ (both computed; they equal $2^{2N-2}$, the sign flips, times the order of the symplectic group of $V$, given the classical theorem, not used here, that transvections generate it). $R_{c}$ is a rotor exactly when $k_{c}$ is a bivector: every generator for $2N \le 6$ ($\Cl(1,3)$, $\Cl(3,1)$, $\Cl(6,0)$). For $2N \ge 8$ the generators include blades of grade $4$ or $6$, which are not versors, and for grade $4$ ($\Cl(7,1)$: $35$ of $63$) $R_{c}\tilde R_{c} = 2k_{c}$ is not a scalar; the bivector rotors alone are not transitive on the classes ($\Cl(7,1)$: orbits $7$, $21$, $35$; $\Cl(10,0)$: $45$, $210$; computed) and are not a design. The statement is for signatures with $I^{2} = -1$, where the unit of the averages is the pseudoscalar.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Two identities of a state; proved.)} $\sum_{c \ne 0}x_{c}^{2} = D - 1$, and for every $u \ne 0$, $\sum\epsilon(c,d)x_{c}x_{d} = (D - 2)x_{u}$, the sum over the $\tfrac12D^{2} - 2$ ordered pairs of nonzero classes with $c + d = u$ and $b(c,d) = 0$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Moments to order three; proved.)} For every state and all nonzero classes $c, d, e$:
\[
\langle x_{c}\rangle_{\Gamma} = 0, \qquad \langle x_{c}x_{d}\rangle_{\Gamma} = \frac{\delta_{cd}}{D + 1}, \qquad \langle x_{c}x_{d}x_{e}\rangle_{\Gamma} = \begin{cases}\dfrac{2\,\epsilon(c,d)}{(D + 1)(D + 2)} & e = c + d,\ c \ne d,\ b(c,d) = 0,\\[1ex] 0 & \text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
\]
The values do not depend on the state averaged. \emph{Corollary (a set of modes on a parity sector).} For a proper subset $A$ of $2a$ of the generators the even blades of $A$ are $\tfrac12 d_{A}^{2}$ distinct classes, $d_{A} = 2^{a}$, and the purity of a state on the even part of $A$ is $d_{A}^{-1}\sum x_{c}^{2}$ over them; by the second moment its mean is $d_{A}^{-1}\bigl(1 + (\tfrac12 d_{A}^{2} - 1)/(D + 1)\bigr) = (d_{A} + d_{B})/(d_{A}d_{B} + 2)$ with $d_{A}d_{B} = 2D$: $\tfrac23$ at four generators. It follows from (iii) and not from (v).
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Every invariant measure to order three; proved; the imported Fact is a cross-check.)} Since the $\Gamma$-mean of every monomial of degree at most three is the same number for every state, every probability measure on states that is invariant under $\Gamma$ has the moments of (iii): its moment is the integral of the $\Gamma$-mean. The unitarily invariant measure is one such measure, so for $D$ a power of two its moments to order three are derived here. Identify $E$ with the $D \times D$ matrices over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I\}$, the $h_{c}$ Hermitian of square one and trace $D\langle h_{c}\rangle_{0}$, a state with $\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}$, $x_{c} = \bra{\psi}h_{c}\ket{\psi}$. The values of (iii) are those that Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-haar-moments-of-random-pure-state} gives for $n \le 3$, $\sum_{\sigma}\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(P_{\sigma}\,h_{c}\otimes h_{d}\otimes h_{e}\bigr)/(D(D+1)(D+2))$ and its analogue with two factors. Since the monomials of degree at most three in the $x_{c}$ span the polynomials of degree at most three in $\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}$, the $\Gamma$-orbit of every state is a design of order three: the mean of $(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})^{\otimes n}$ over the orbit is the invariant mean for $n = 1, 2, 3$. Each $\Gamma$-orbit is itself such a measure. No statement is made at order four.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Mean purity of a matrix factor; proved.)} Let $W \subset V$ be a subspace of dimension $2r$ on which $b$ is nondegenerate, $m = 2^{r}$ and $n = D/m$; the $h_{c}$, $c \in W$, span over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I\}$ a subalgebra isomorphic to the $m \times m$ matrices, and the purity of a state on it is $P_{W} = m^{-1}\sum_{c \in W}x_{c}^{2}$ (with $x_{0} = 1$). Then for every state
\[
\langle P_{W}\rangle_{\Gamma} = \frac1m\Bigl(1 + \frac{m^{2} - 1}{D + 1}\Bigr) = \frac{m + n}{mn + 1},
\]
the mean purity of the unitarily invariant measure on $\C^{m}\otimes\C^{n}$ by (iv), the value that Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-haar-moments-of-random-pure-state} states at $n = 2$ (Lubkin's mean purity, there imported for all dimensions), here a finite sum, for dimensions $m$, $n$ that are powers of two and for no others: a comparison stated for all $m$, $n$ can rest on this clause only where its dimensions are powers of two. The even blades of a proper subset of the generators do not form such a $W$ (they are $\tfrac12 m^{2}$ classes, not $m^{2}$), and their purity is not covered by this clause.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.quarter-turn-rotors-of-the-eve.technical: The even subalgebra of a Clifford algebra with an even number $2N$ of generators and a pseudoscalar of square $-1$ is a complex matrix algebra whose imaginary unit is the pseudoscalar. Its even blades, taken up to that unit, are the Pauli operators of $N - 1$ qubits, and each has a version $k$ of square $-1$, so $1 + k$ is a real invertible element, a quarter turn about the blade $k$; it is a rotor exactly when $k$ is a bivector, which is every case up to six generators and not beyond. The conjugations by these elements form a finite group (the Clifford group of quantum information, modulo phases). The result is that averaging any pure state over this group gives the first three moments of every measure invariant under the group, the unitarily invariant one among them, with a proof that uses three facts only: conjugation by a blade flips signs, the quarter-turn elements act on the classes of blades as the transvections of a nondegenerate alternating form and so mix them transitively, and a pure state is an idempotent. The second moment gives Lubkin's mean purity $(m + n)/(mn + 1)$ for a matrix factor as a finite sum, for dimensions that are powers of two. Orders four and above, and the parity-superselected purity of a set of modes, are outside the statement.
synthesis.quarter-turn-rotors-of-the-eve.lay: Several entropy comparisons in the store borrow, from the literature, the average behaviour of a quantum state chosen completely at random. A completely random choice means an average over a continuous infinity of states. This result shows that for the quantities of second and third order, which include the average purity those comparisons use, the same numbers come out of an average over a finite list of states: the ones reached from any starting state by quarter turns about the blades of the algebra (rotations in planes when there are at most six generators). For two qubits the list has at most 11520 entries. The finite average is carried out inside the algebra the series already uses, with its own unit in place of the imaginary number. It reproduces the borrowed numbers exactly up to third order and makes no claim beyond that.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} For $2N$ generators $I^{2} = (-1)^{N(2N-1)}(-1)^{q} = (-1)^{N+q}$, so $I^{2} = -1$ exactly when $N + q$ is odd; $I$ anticommutes with every $e_{i}$ and commutes with $E$. By clause (ii) of \claimref{synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra}, $e_{S}e_{T} = \pm e_{S\triangle T}$, $e_{S}^{2} = \pm 1$ and $e_{S}e_{T} = (-1)^{b(S,T)}e_{T}e_{S}$ with $b(S,T) = |S||T| + |S\cap T| \bmod 2$. $Ie_{S} = \pm e_{S^{c}}$ and $(Ie_{S})^{2} = I^{2}e_{S}^{2} = -e_{S}^{2}$, so of $e_{S}$ and $Ie_{S}$ exactly one has square $+1$. For even $S$, $T$ the form $b(S,T) = |S\cap T| \bmod 2$ is alternating, the full set is in its radical, and by clause (iii) of that theorem the radical of $b$ on all subsets is trivial for an even number of generators, so the radical on even subsets (the orthogonal complement of the full set) is the full set alone: $b$ is nondegenerate on $V$. The $2D^{2} = 2^{2N-1}$ elements $h_{c}$, $Ih_{c}$ are the even blades up to sign, a basis of $E$. If $b(c,d) = 0$, $(h_{c}h_{d})^{2} = 1$, so $h_{c}h_{d} = \pm h_{c+d}$; if $b(c,d) = 1$, $(h_{c}h_{d})^{2} = -1$, so $h_{c}h_{d} = \pm Ih_{c+d}$. Hence $\langle h_{c}h_{d}\rangle_{0} = \delta_{cd}$, and $x_{c} = D\langle\rho h_{c}\rangle_{0}$.

\emph{(i).} Put $k = Ih_{c}$, $k^{2} = -1$. If $h_{d}$ commutes with $h_{c}$ it commutes with $R_{c}$. If it anticommutes, $R_{c}h_{d}R_{c}^{-1} = \tfrac12(1 + k)h_{d}(1 - k) = \tfrac12 h_{d}(1 - k)^{2} = -h_{d}k = -Ih_{d}h_{c}$, which is $\pm h_{c+d}$ by the setting. So conjugation by $R_{c}$ permutes the set $\{\pm h_{d}\}$ and fixes $I$; an automorphism in $\Gamma$ is determined by its action on that finite set, so $\Gamma$ is finite. $R_{c}^{2} = 2k$ and $I$ is central in $E$, so conjugation by $h_{c}$ lies in $\Gamma$; it multiplies $h_{d}$ by $(-1)^{b(c,d)}$. An automorphism carries idempotents to idempotents and $\Gamma$ preserves the real span of the $h_{c}$ and the scalar part, so states go to states. Transitivity. Write $t_{c}$ for the transvection of $c$. If $c \ne c'$ are nonzero and $b(c,c') = 1$, $t_{c+c'}(c) = c'$. If $b(c,c') = 0$, the functionals $b(\cdot,c)$, $b(\cdot,c')$ are independent, so there is $w$ with $b(w,c) = b(w,c') = 1$, and $t_{w+c'}t_{c+w}(c) = c'$. For pairs: given $(c,d)$ and $(c',d')$ with $b = 0$, first move $c$ to $c'$; then $d$, $d'$ lie in $c'^{\perp}\setminus\{0, c'\}$ and it suffices to move $d$ to $d'$ by transvections $t_{v}$ with $b(v,c') = 0$, which fix $c'$. If $b(d,d') = 1$, $v = d + d'$ does it. If $b(d,d') = 0$ and $d \ne d'$, choose $w$ with $b(w,c') = 0$, $b(w,d) = b(w,d') = 1$: the three functionals are independent unless $d' = d + c'$, in which case the third condition follows from the first two and $c'$, $d$ are independent; then $t_{w+d'}t_{d+w}$ carries $d$ to $d'$ and both factors fix $c'$. The orders $24$ and $11520$ are computed by closing the signed permutations (check). A generator with $k_{c}$ a bivector is a rotor; for $k_{c}$ of grade four the reverse fixes $k_{c}$ and $R_{c}\tilde R_{c} = (1 + k_{c})^{2} = 2k_{c}$; the orbits of the bivector generators alone in $\Cl(7,1)$ and $\Cl(10,0)$ are computed in the check.

\emph{(ii).} The scalar part of $\rho^{2} = \rho$ is $D^{-2}(1 + \sum_{c\ne0}x_{c}^{2}) = D^{-1}$. The coefficient of $h_{u}$, $u \ne 0$, in $\rho^{2}$ is $D^{-2}\bigl(2x_{u} + \sum_{c+d=u}x_{c}x_{d}\,[h_{c}h_{d}]_{h_{u}}\bigr)$ over nonzero $c$, $d$; pairs with $b(c,d) = 1$ contribute to $Ih_{u}$ only, and there $(c,d)$ and $(d,c)$ cancel, as they must since $\rho$ has no $Ih_{u}$ part. Equating with $x_{u}/D$ gives the second identity. The pairs: $c \in u^{\perp}\setminus\{0, u\}$, and $|u^{\perp}| = \tfrac12D^{2}$.

\emph{(iii).} Write $\langle\cdot\rangle$ for $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\Gamma}$; it is invariant under replacing $\rho$ by $g\rho g^{-1}$, $g \in \Gamma$. The coordinates of $g\rho g^{-1}$ are $x_{c}(g\rho g^{-1}) = D\langle\rho\,g^{-1}(h_{c})\rangle_{0}$. \emph{Sign flips.} For a monomial $x_{c_{1}}\cdots x_{c_{j}}$ with $c_{1} + \dots + c_{j} \ne 0$ there is $u$ with $b(u, c_{1} + \dots + c_{j}) = 1$, and conjugation by $h_{u}$ multiplies the monomial by $-1$: its mean is $0$. This gives $\langle x_{c}\rangle = 0$, $\langle x_{c}x_{d}\rangle = 0$ for $c \ne d$, and $\langle x_{c}x_{d}x_{e}\rangle = 0$ unless $e = c + d$ (in particular it vanishes when two of the three classes coincide, the third being nonzero). \emph{Second moment.} By transitivity on nonzero classes $\langle x_{c}^{2}\rangle = a$ does not depend on $c$ (a $g^{-1}$ carrying $h_{c}$ to $\pm h_{c'}$ gives $x_{c}^{2}(g\rho g^{-1}) = x_{c'}^{2}(\rho)$), and the first identity of (ii) gives $(D^{2} - 1)a = D - 1$, $a = 1/(D+1)$. \emph{Third moment, anticommuting.} Let $e = c + d$, $b(c,d) = 1$; then $b(c,e) = b(d,e) = 1$. Conjugation by $R_{e}$ sends $h_{c} \mapsto -Ih_{c}h_{e} = sh_{d}$, $h_{d} \mapsto -Ih_{d}h_{e} = s'h_{c}$ and fixes $h_{e}$; multiplying, $ss'h_{d}h_{c} = I^{2}h_{c}h_{e}h_{d}h_{e} = h_{c}h_{d} = -h_{d}h_{c}$, so $ss' = -1$ and $x_{c}x_{d}x_{e}$ changes sign: its mean is $0$. \emph{Third moment, commuting.} Let $b(c,d) = 0$, $c \ne d$, $e = c + d$ and $T(c,d) = \epsilon(c,d)x_{c}x_{d}x_{c+d}$. If $g^{-1}(h_{c}) = \sigma h_{c'}$ and $g^{-1}(h_{d}) = \tau h_{d'}$ then $g^{-1}(h_{c+d}) = \epsilon(c,d)\sigma\tau\,h_{c'}h_{d'} = \epsilon(c,d)\epsilon(c',d')\sigma\tau\,h_{c'+d'}$, so $T(c,d)(g\rho g^{-1}) = T(c',d')(\rho)$. By transitivity on commuting pairs $\langle T(c,d)\rangle = \kappa$ for all of them. Multiply the second identity of (ii) by $x_{u}$ and average: $(\tfrac12D^{2} - 2)\kappa = (D - 2)a$, so for $D > 2$, $\kappa = 2/((D+1)(D+2))$; for $D = 2$ there is no commuting pair. All values are independent of $\rho$.

\emph{Corollary to (iii).} For a proper subset $A$ of $2a$ generators no even subset of $A$ has its complement in $A$, so the $2^{2a-1} = \tfrac12d_{A}^{2}$ even subsets are distinct classes, the empty one being $0$; the restriction of a state to the algebra they span has purity $d_{A}^{-1}\sum x_{c}^{2}$ in the trace of the $d_{A}$-dimensional module of $A$, and (iii) gives the mean $d_{A}^{-1}(1 + (\tfrac12d_{A}^{2} - 1)/(D+1)) = (D + \tfrac12d_{A}^{2})/(d_{A}(D+1)) = (d_{B} + d_{A})/(d_{A}d_{B} + 2)$ with $D = \tfrac12d_{A}d_{B}$.

\emph{(iv).} With $I^{2} = -1$ and $I$ central, $E$ is a central simple algebra over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I\}$ of dimension $D^{2}$, the $D\times D$ matrices; the adjoint is the real-linear map fixing every $h_{c}$ and negating every $Ih_{c}$; it is an anti-automorphism because $h_{c}h_{d} = \pm h_{c+d}$ for commuting and $\pm Ih_{c+d}$ for anticommuting units, and $\langle xx^{\dagger}\rangle_{0}$ is the sum of the squared coefficients of $x$; the trace is $D$ times the part along $1$ and $I$. \emph{Invariant measures.} Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on states invariant under $\Gamma$ and $f$ a monomial of degree at most three. Then $\int f\,d\mu = \int\langle f\rangle_{\Gamma}\,d\mu$ by invariance, and $\langle f\rangle_{\Gamma}$ is by (iii) a constant, so $\int f\,d\mu$ is that constant. The unitarily invariant measure is invariant under conjugation by every invertible element that preserves the adjoint up to scale, the $R_{c}$ among them ($R_{c}R_{c}^{\dagger} = (1 + k_{c})(1 - k_{c}) = 2$). What follows compares with the imported formula as a cross-check. The formula of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-haar-moments-of-random-pure-state} is the sum over permutations of the products of cycle traces, divided by $D(D+1)\cdots(D+n-1)$. For two factors $\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}h_{c}\operatorname{Tr}h_{d} + \operatorname{Tr}h_{c}h_{d}\bigr)/(D(D+1)) = \delta_{cd}/(D+1)$. For three factors every term of the sum over $S_{3}$ containing the trace of a single unit vanishes, the transpositions give $\operatorname{Tr}(h_{c}h_{d})\operatorname{Tr}h_{e} = 0$, and the two three-cycles give $\operatorname{Tr}(h_{c}h_{d}h_{e}) + \operatorname{Tr}(h_{c}h_{e}h_{d})$, which is $2\epsilon(c,d)D$ for a commuting pair with $e = c + d$, zero for an anticommuting pair with $e = c + d$ (the two orders differ by a sign) and zero otherwise; divided by $D(D+1)(D+2)$ these are the values of (iii). A polynomial of degree $n$ in the entries of $\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}$ is a combination of products of $n$ numbers $\operatorname{Tr}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}h_{c})$, $c \in V$, because the $h_{c}$ span the matrices; so equality on monomials of degree at most three, including those with $x_{0} = 1$, is the design property of order three. The check recomputes both sides independently.

\emph{(v).} A subspace $W$ on which $b$ is nondegenerate has a symplectic basis; the corresponding units generate $r$ mutually commuting copies of the algebra of two anticommuting units of square one, the $2\times2$ matrices over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I\}$, so the $h_{c}$, $c \in W$, span the $m\times m$ matrices, a factor with commutant the $n\times n$ matrices. The reduced state of $\rho$ on it is $m^{-1}\sum_{c\in W}x_{c}h_{c}$ (it has the same expectation on every $h_{c}$, $c \in W$), with purity $m^{-1}\sum_{c\in W}x_{c}^{2}$. By (iii), $\langle P_{W}\rangle = m^{-1}(1 + (m^{2} - 1)/(D + 1)) = (D + m^{2})/(m(D + 1)) = (m + n)/(mn + 1)$ with $D = mn$. This is the value that Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-haar-moments-of-random-pure-state} states at $n = 2$, at $(d_{A}, d_{B}) = (m, n)$. The even blades of a proper subset $A$ of the generators, $|A| = 2a$, are $2^{2a-1}$ distinct classes, half of $m^{2}$ for $m = 2^{a}$, and do not span a matrix factor.

outside_ga.why: Clauses (i) to (iii) and the factor purity of clause (v) are statements in the even subalgebra with the pseudoscalar as unit. Clause (iv) and the last sentence of (v) compare them with imported Facts that are stated for an abstract Hilbert space and the invariant measure on its unit sphere; the comparison needs the identification of the even subalgebra with the matrices over span{1, I} acting on that space, which is written in matrix language to match the imports.

synthesis.residue-common-weight-particle.technical:
The calibration residue was re-expressed as the reciprocal of four times the counted modes' mean entropy, with the registered value exactly when every counted mode has zero Killing weight. This result asks what happens if the counted modes are the matrix modes on which the series built its fuzzy sphere, carrying the principal $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, and both the Killing generator and the state respect rotations. Then, by the multiplicity-free decomposition of the matrix algebra, the generator, if quasi-free, is one common weight times the total number, and the state, if quasi-free, has one common occupation. So the residue reduces to one number.

A tempting next step fails. The total number commutes with every gauge-invariant bilinear, so a common weight acts trivially on them; but this is true for every weight, and every common occupation then restricts to a tracial state, which is KMS for the trivial flow at any temperature. The gauge-invariant algebra cannot see the weight. What does fix the registered value is a symmetry of the state: the principal representation is self-dual (through a symmetric form for integer spin, a symplectic one for half-integer spin), so there is a particle-hole map that commutes with the rotations and exchanges occupation $q$ with $1 - q$. The registered residue is exactly the case in which the counted state is particle-hole invariant. The s-wave weights of (Q), placed on a principal window, are a rotation generator's spectrum and violate rotation invariance.
synthesis.residue-common-weight-particle.lay: The series needs to know how much energy each counted boundary mode carries, because a mode holds a full bit of information only when it carries none. Suppose the counted modes form the single round "fuzzy sphere" the series already uses, that nothing singles out a direction, and that the state and the energy assignment are of the simplest kind, built from independent modes (quasi-free). Then every mode must carry the same energy, which reduces the open question to one number. One tempting argument says that number must be zero because ordinary observables cannot see it; that argument fails, since those observables cannot see it whatever its value. What does pin the value at zero is a symmetry: if the state treats filled and empty modes alike, the energy is zero and the registered value follows. The series' existing energy assignment breaks the round symmetry.

proofs.main:
Write $L_{a}$ ($a = 1, 2, 3$) for the principal $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ on $\C^{n}$ of Theorem \claimref{scrambling.principality-indifference-sphere}, irreducible of spin $j = (n-1)/2$, and $\hat{X} = \sum_{ij}X_{ij}E_{ij}$. By the $\mathfrak{gl}(n)$ relations of Proposition \claimref{scrambling.boundary-mode-space-matrix}, $[\hat{X}, \hat{Y}] = \widehat{[X, Y]}$, and $X \mapsto \hat{X}$ is injective (it restricts to $X$ on the one-particle space).

(i) By $[\hat{h}, \hat{L}_{a}] = \widehat{[h, L_{a}]}$ and injectivity, $\hat{h}$ commutes with every $\hat{L}_{a}$ exactly when $h$ commutes with every $L_{a}$, that is, when $h$ is an invariant of the adjoint action on $\Mat_{n}$. By Fact \claimref{scrambling.imported-kostant-madore-partition-data}(ii) that action is $\bigoplus_{\ell=0}^{n-1}(2\ell+1)$ with a single spin-$0$ summand, which contains $\id$; so the invariants are $\C\,\id$ and $h = \omega\,\id$, $\hat{h} = \omega N_{\mathrm{tot}}$. A gauge-invariant quasi-free state is fixed by its symbol $Q$, $\omega(\psi_{i}^{\dagger}\psi_{j}) = Q_{ji}$ (Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-quasi-free-states-car-algebra}); a rotation $u = e^{J\theta^{a}L_{a}}$ acts on the modes as a one-particle unitary and on the symbol by $Q \mapsto uQu^{\dagger}$, so invariance under all rotations makes $Q$ an adjoint invariant, $Q = q\,\id$, and the state is $\rho_{q}$. Every counted mode then has the marginal $\operatorname{diag}(1 - q, q)$; if it is KMS for $\omega N_{\mathrm{tot}}$ at $\beta = 2\pi/\kappa$, as (R) requires mode by mode, $q = 1/(e^{x} + 1)$ with the one value $x = 2\pi\omega/\kappa$, each mode carries $s(x)$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boundary-mode-thermal-entropy}), $\langle s\rangle = s(x)$, and Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy}(i) gives $\kappa_{c} = 1/(4s(x))$. For the last sentence: $N_{\mathrm{tot}}^{2}$ commutes with the rotations and is not in $\operatorname{span}\{\id, N_{\mathrm{tot}}\}$ for $n \ge 2$; the script computes the full Fock commutant, of dimension $5$ at $n = 2$ and $8$ at $n = 3$.

(ii) $[N_{\mathrm{tot}}, E_{ij}] = \widehat{[\id, e_{ij}]} = 0$, so $N_{\mathrm{tot}}$ commutes with the algebra $\mathcal{A}_{0}$ the $E_{ij}$ generate, and it lies in $\mathcal{A}_{0}$: it is central. Hence $\operatorname{Ad}(e^{Jt\omega N_{\mathrm{tot}}})$ is the identity on $\mathcal{A}_{0}$ for all $t$ and $\omega$. On the Fock space $\rho_{q}$ has density matrix $D_{q} = q^{N_{\mathrm{tot}}}(1 - q)^{n - N_{\mathrm{tot}}}$ (the product state of Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-quasi-free-states-car-algebra} on a window), a function of $N_{\mathrm{tot}}$, so it commutes with $\mathcal{A}_{0}$ and $\rho_{q}(AB) = \operatorname{tr}(D_{q}AB) = \operatorname{tr}(BD_{q}A) = \rho_{q}(BA)$ for $A, B \in \mathcal{A}_{0}$: the restriction is tracial. A tracial state satisfies the KMS condition for the trivial flow at every $\beta$, since then $F_{A,B}(t) = \rho_{q}(AB)$ is constant and equals $\rho_{q}(BA)$. Finally $\rho_{q}(N_{\mathrm{tot}}) = nq$, so distinct $q$ give distinct states on $\mathcal{A}_{0}$. Thus the data on $\mathcal{A}_{0}$ (the restricted flow, trivial, and the KMS condition, satisfied by all $\rho_{q}$) leave $q$, and with it $\omega$ at fixed $\beta$, undetermined; the argument from the trivial restriction to $q = \tfrac12$ has a false premise.

(iii) In the standard basis $|j, m\rangle$, $L_{3} = \operatorname{diag}(m)$ and $(L_{+})_{m+1,m} = c(m) = \sqrt{(j - m)(j + m + 1)}$, with $c(-m-1) = c(m)$ and $L_{-} = L_{+}^{T}$. The matrix $\varepsilon_{m,m'} = (-1)^{j-m}\delta_{m,-m'}$ is a signed permutation, so an orthogonal matrix; since $(-1)^{j+m} = (-1)^{2j}(-1)^{j-m}$, $\varepsilon^{T} = (-1)^{2j}\varepsilon$, so the bilinear form it defines is symmetric for integer $j$ and symplectic for half-integer $j$, and $\varepsilon^{2} = (-1)^{2j}\id$. It satisfies $\varepsilon X + X^{T}\varepsilon = 0$ for $X = L_{3}, L_{\pm}$: for $L_{3}$ the $(m, -m)$ entry is $(-1)^{j-m}(-m + m) = 0$; for $L_{+}$ the only possibly nonzero entries are at $(a, b)$ with $a = -b - 1$, where they are $(-1)^{j+b+1}c(b) + (-1)^{j+b}c(-b-1) = 0$, and $L_{-}$ follows by transposition. Over $\C$ the identity extends to $L_{1}, L_{2}$. Set $C(\psi_{i}) = \sum_{k}\varepsilon_{ik}\psi_{k}^{\dagger}$; since $\varepsilon\varepsilon^{T} = \id$ the images satisfy the CAR, so $C$ is a Bogoliubov automorphism. Then $C(E_{ij}) = \sum_{kl}\varepsilon_{ik}\varepsilon_{jl}\psi_{k}\psi_{l}^{\dagger} = \delta_{ij} - \sum_{kl}\varepsilon_{ik}\varepsilon_{jl}E_{lk}$, so $C(\hat{X}) = \operatorname{tr}(X) - \widehat{(\varepsilon^{T}X\varepsilon)^{T}}$. For $X = L_{a}$: $\operatorname{tr}L_{a} = 0$ and $L_{a}^{T} = -\varepsilon L_{a}\varepsilon^{T}$, so $(\varepsilon^{T}L_{a}\varepsilon)^{T} = \varepsilon^{T}L_{a}^{T}\varepsilon = -L_{a}$ and $C(\hat{L}_{a}) = \hat{L}_{a}$. For $X = \id$: $C(N_{\mathrm{tot}}) = n - N_{\mathrm{tot}}$. A Bogoliubov automorphism carries quasi-free states to quasi-free states; $\rho_{q}\circ C$ has $\rho_{q}(C(\psi_{i}^{\dagger}\psi_{j})) = \sum_{kl}\varepsilon_{ik}\varepsilon_{jl}(\delta_{kl} - q\delta_{kl}) = (1 - q)\delta_{ij}$ and $\rho_{q}(C(\psi_{i}\psi_{j})) = \sum\varepsilon_{ik}\varepsilon_{jl}\rho_{q}(\psi_{k}^{\dagger}\psi_{l}^{\dagger}) = 0$, so it is gauge invariant with symbol $(1 - q)\id$: $\rho_{q}\circ C = \rho_{1-q}$ by the uniqueness clause of Fact \claimref{hawking.imported-quasi-free-states-car-algebra}. Since $C^{2}(\psi_{i}) = \sum_{k}\varepsilon_{ik}C(\psi_{k}^{\dagger}) = \sum_{l}(\varepsilon^{2})_{il}\psi_{l} = (-1)^{2j}\psi_{i}$, $C$ is an involution for integer $j$ and squares to the parity automorphism for half-integer $j$; none of the following uses $C^{2} = \id$. Hence $\rho_{q}\circ C = \rho_{q}$ if and only if $q = \tfrac12$, which under the KMS relation of (i) is $x = 0$, $\omega = 0$. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy}(ii), equality $\kappa_{c} = 1/(4\ln 2)$ holds exactly when every counted mode has zero weight, which under (i) is $q = \tfrac12$, which is $C$-invariance. The direction from $C$-invariance uses only rotation and gauge invariance: for any such state $\omega$ the two-point matrix is $q\,\id$ by the argument of (i) (which uses only invariance of the symbol), and $\omega\circ C = \omega$ gives $q = \omega(C(E_{ii})) = 1 - q$.

(iv) On $n = 2j + 1$, $h = 2L_{3}$ has spectrum $\{2m\}$, so $\kappa h/2$ has spectrum $\kappa\{-j, \ldots, j\}$, the weights of Premise \claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave} on a window centred at the sea level; these are $n$ distinct values, while by (i) a rotation-invariant quasi-free generator has one, and $[h, L_{\pm}] = \pm 2L_{\pm} \neq 0$.

For the closing remark: Definition \claimref{obj.hawking.boundary-mode-algebra-windows-boost-dynamics} takes $\omega_{j} > 0$; with (i) the common weight is then positive, $q < \tfrac12$, $s(x) < \ln 2$, and $\kappa_{c} = 1/(4s(x)) > 1/(4\ln 2)$.

The script verifies the finite instances exactly: the commutant dimensions for $n = 2, \ldots, 6$ against the partition $(n-1, 1)$, which has a two-dimensional commutant; the second-quantised statements on Jordan-Wigner modes for $n = 2, 3, 4$; the centrality of $N_{\mathrm{tot}}$, $\dim\mathcal{A}_{0} = \sum_{k}\binom{n}{k}^{2}$ and the tracial property for rational $q$; the existence and nondegeneracy of the invariant form for $n = 2, \ldots, 6$, antisymmetric for even $n$ and symmetric for odd $n$; that $\varepsilon^{2} = -\id$ for spin $\tfrac12$ and $+\id$ for spin $1$, the order of $C$; and, for spin $\tfrac12$ and spin $1$ in orthonormal real bases, that $C$ preserves the $\mathfrak{gl}(n)$ relations, fixes the rotation generators, sends $N_{\mathrm{tot}}$ to $n - N_{\mathrm{tot}}$ and carries $\rho_{q}$ to $\rho_{1-q}$ on a spanning set of $\mathcal{A}_{0}$.

synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy.technical:
The entropy paper leaves one number undetermined, the calibration residue: how many boundary modes are counted per Planck area of horizon in each modular period. It also proves that no rational recount of cells can give the value it needs. Here the residue is re-expressed, under one hypothesis: that the counted modes carry the hole's thermodynamic entropy, which the series' temperature fixes at a quarter of the area. Each mode at that temperature carries at most $\ln 2$, and exactly $\ln 2$ only at zero energy. So the residue is the reciprocal of four times the average entropy per counted mode. It is at least $1/(4\ln 2)$, and equals the registered value $1/(4\ln 2)$ precisely when every counted mode has zero energy.

The $\ln 2$ is the entropy of one maximally mixed fermion, as the entropy paper itself remarks, which is consistent with its proof that no counting rule produces it. At the cosmological horizon the count is strictly above $\pi N^{2}/\ln 2$, since its modes have nonzero weight. Two cautions. The counted modes' energy is below half the hole's mass, and zero at the registered value, so the mass is not their energy. And the hypothesis is the very area-law match the entropy paper holds under test, so this re-expresses the residue rather than deriving it. Taken literally, the singularity paper's s-wave weights give $0.3470$ arrays per Planck area per period, not the registered $0.3607$, whichever modes are counted: if those weights were ever promoted to a derivation, the boundary-mode prediction's kill condition would refute the intrinsic-clock premise.
synthesis.residue-from-mode-entropy.lay: The series needs one number to turn its count of a black hole's boundary modes into the hole's entropy. That number could not be found by counting, and the series proved it never could be. This result re-expresses that number. It is really about how much information each mode holds, and a mode holds its maximum, one bit, only if it carries no energy. If the counted modes are exactly the zero-energy ones, the number takes the value the series registered as a prediction; if some carry energy, more modes are needed. So the open question becomes a sharper one: which modes are counted, and what energies do they carry? The one energy assignment the series has, its s-wave convention, gives a number about four per cent below the registered prediction.

proofs.main:
By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.quarter-from-temperature}, under (P, \claimref{singularity.p-univalence}) and (R, \claimref{singularity.r-regularity-fixed-locus}) the hole's thermodynamic entropy is $S = A/4$. The hypothesis $\sum_{j} s(x_{j}) = A/4$ gives $|J|\,\langle s\rangle = A/4$, so $\kappa_{c} = |J|/A = 1/(4\langle s\rangle)$, which is (i).

By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boundary-mode-thermal-entropy}, $s(x) \le \ln 2$ with equality exactly at $x = 0$, so $\langle s\rangle \le \ln 2$ with equality exactly when every $x_{j} = 0$, that is every $\omega_{j} = 0$. Hence $\kappa_{c} = 1/(4\langle s\rangle) \ge 1/(4\ln 2)$, with the same case of equality, which is (ii). In the capacity convention T08 sets $\kappa_{c} = 1/(4\ln 2)$ and the boundary-mode prediction states $\nu = 1/(16\pi\ln 2)$; by (ii) these hold under the hypothesis exactly when the counted modes are at zero weight.

For (iii): T08's remark on $\nu$ already identifies $\ln 2$ as the entropy of a maximally mixed fermionic mode. At equality $\kappa_{c} = 1/(4\ln 2)$ with $\ln 2 = s(0)$, the entropy of the state $\tfrac12\mathbf 1$ of one mode, so the transcendental factor is a property of the state of a mode and not of a tally; a rule that assigns a rational number of modes per cell of rational area produces a residue in $\mathbb{Q}\pi^{k}$, which T08 shows never equals $1/(4\ln 2)$ for $k = 0$.

For (iv): under (P) and (R$_{\Lambda}$, \claimref{synthesis.r-lambda-regularity-cosmological-horizon}) each mode of the cosmological horizon is Fermi-Dirac at $T_{\Lambda} = \kappa_{\Lambda}/2\pi$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-temperature-frozen-point-norm}); the computation of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boundary-mode-thermal-entropy} uses only the Fermi-Dirac form, so with $x_{j} = 2\pi\omega_{j}/\kappa_{\Lambda}$ the same bound $s \le \ln 2$ holds, with equality exactly at zero weight. With $S_{\Lambda} = \pi N^{2}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-entropy-pi-n-squared}) the hypothesis $\sum_{j} s(x_{j}) = S_{\Lambda}$ gives $|J| = \pi N^{2}/\langle s\rangle \ge \pi N^{2}/\ln 2$, with equality exactly at zero weight; since Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.cosmological-horizon-boundary-modes} has $\omega_{j} > 0$, the inequality is strict.

For (v): with $n = 1/(e^{x} + 1)$, $s(x) = \ln(1 + e^{-x}) + xn > xn = \beta\omega n$ for every finite $x$, since $\ln(1 + e^{-x}) > 0$. Summing, $\beta E = \sum_{j}\beta\omega_{j}n_{j} < \sum_{j} s(x_{j}) = A/4 = S$, so $E < TS$, and $TS = (1/8\pi M)(4\pi M^{2}) = M/2$. At equality in (ii) every $\omega_{j} = 0$ and $E = 0$.

For (vi): under (Q) (\claimref{singularity.q-joint-quasi-freeness-s-wave} records the weights $\omega_{k} = \kappa k$, the sea level at $k = 0$) an array's modes have $x = 2\pi k$, $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, and since $s$ is even its entropy is $s(0) + 2\sum_{k \ge 1} s(2\pi k) = \ln 2 + \varepsilon$. The check brackets $\varepsilon$ with rational bounds: the terms $k = 1, 2, 3$ by rational enclosures of $\pi$ and the exponential, and the tail by $s(x) < (1 + x)e^{-x}$ for $x > 0$. The three readings follow: every mode counted gives $\langle s\rangle = (\ln 2 + \varepsilon)/m$ for an array of $m$ modes, which tends to $0$ as $m$ grows; arrays counted give $\kappa_{c} = 1/(4(\ln 2 + \varepsilon))$; only zero-weight modes counted give $\sum s = |J|\ln 2$ while the arrays hold $|J|(\ln 2 + \varepsilon)$.

synthesis.sds-clausius-fixes-area-consta.technical:
The Schwarzschild-de Sitter gravitational field on flat spacetime has two horizon loci in its Painlev\'e-Gullstrand chart, the black hole's and the cosmological one. Assume (T) that each sits at the temperature the series' regularity premises give at the ends of the family (surface gravity over $2\pi$), here assumed for every mass, and (Cl) that each obeys Hawking's Clausius relation as the mass varies at fixed $\Lambda$. Then each horizon's entropy is a quarter of the area of its cross-section plus a constant, one constant per horizon, independent of the mass, and the temperatures say nothing about the constants. Two normalisations fix them: (Z) the black hole's entropy vanishes as its mass goes to zero (Hawking's normalisation, already used for the quarter), and (N) the two entropies agree where the two horizons merge (the Nariai limit). Under (T), (Cl), (Z) and (N) both constants are zero, and the cosmological horizon of pure de Sitter space has entropy $\pi\ell^{2} = \pi N^{2}$, derived from these four hypotheses rather than from the imported area law.

A constant added to every spherical horizon passes (T), (Cl) and (N) and fails (Z); a negative one also makes small black holes' entropy negative, which a count of boundary modes cannot be. The series' MacDowell-Mansouri action as written adds such a negative constant through its Gauss-Bonnet term, under the Wald entropy hypothesis; its value is computed in a result filed alongside. Under (Z), or under nonnegativity, the topological contribution has to be removed.
synthesis.sds-clausius-fixes-area-consta.lay: A black hole in a universe with a cosmological constant has two horizons: its own and the universe's. Assuming the framework's horizon temperatures hold all along this family, and the ordinary law linking heat and entropy, each horizon's entropy comes out as a quarter of its area plus an unknown constant. Requiring a vanishing black hole to carry no entropy, and the two horizons to agree where they merge, sets both constants to zero, which gives the universe's horizon its standard entropy from these assumptions rather than from the standard area law. The framework's own form of the gravitational action instead subtracts a fixed amount from every horizon, which would make small black holes' entropy negative; if horizon entropy counts quantum modes, that subtraction cannot stand.

proofs.main:
\emph{The family.} Write $g(r) := r f(r) = r - 2M - r^{3}/\ell^{2}$. Then $g(0) = -2M < 0$, $g$ has its maximum on $r > 0$ at $r = \ell/\sqrt{3}$ with value $\tfrac{2\ell}{3\sqrt{3}} - 2M$, positive exactly when $M < M_{N}$, and $g \to -\infty$; so for $0 < M < M_{N}$ there are exactly two positive zeros, $r_{b} < \ell/\sqrt{3} < r_{c}$, and since the zeros of $-\ell^{2}g$ sum to $0$ the third is $-(r_{b} + r_{c})$. Comparing coefficients in $-\ell^{2}g(r) = (r - r_{b})(r - r_{c})(r + r_{b} + r_{c})$ gives $\ell^{2} = r_{b}^{2} + r_{b}r_{c} + r_{c}^{2}$ and $2M\ell^{2} = r_{b}r_{c}(r_{b} + r_{c})$; in particular $r_{c}^{2} < \ell^{2}$. On the horizon locus $f(r_{h}) = 0$ the mass is $M = \tfrac12 r_{h}(1 - r_{h}^{2}/\ell^{2})$, a function of either radius, with $dM/dr_{h} = \tfrac12(1 - 3r_{h}^{2}/\ell^{2})$, positive on the black-hole branch and negative on the cosmological branch.

\emph{(i).} By (T), $4\pi T_{h} = |f'(r_{h})|$ with $f'(r_{h}) = 2M/r_{h}^{2} - 2r_{h}/\ell^{2} = r_{h}^{-1}(1 - 3r_{h}^{2}/\ell^{2})$ after substituting $2M = r_{h}(1 - r_{h}^{2}/\ell^{2})$; so $f'(r_{b}) > 0 > f'(r_{c})$. Hence $T_{h}\,d(\pi r_{h}^{2}) = \tfrac{|f'(r_{h})|}{4\pi}\,2\pi r_{h}\,dr_{h} = \pm\tfrac12(1 - 3r_{h}^{2}/\ell^{2})\,dr_{h} = \pm\,dM$, with the upper sign on the black-hole branch and the lower on the cosmological one. So $S_{h} = \pi r_{h}^{2} = A_{h}/4$ satisfies (Cl) on each branch, and since (Cl) fixes $dS_{h}/dr_{h}$ on a connected interval of $M$, every solution is $A_{h}/4 + c_{h}$ with a constant $c_{h}$, and every constant occurs. The same computation at $\Lambda = 0$ is $f'(2M) = 1/2M = 2\kappa$ with $\kappa = 1/4M$, the input of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.quarter-from-temperature}, which this extends; at $M = 0$ it is $4\pi T_{c} = 2/\ell$, so $(2\pi T_{c})^{2} = 1/\ell^{2} = Q(I_{\Lambda})$, the temperature of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.de-sitter-temperature-frozen-point-norm}.

\emph{(ii).} As $M \to 0$ on the black-hole branch, $r_{b} \to 0$ (from $2M\ell^{2} = r_{b}r_{c}(r_{b} + r_{c}) > r_{b}r_{c}^{2} > r_{b}\ell^{2}/3$, so $r_{b} < 6M$), hence $A_{b} \to 0$ and $S_{b} \to c_{b}$.

\emph{(iii).} As $M \to M_{N}$ the maximum of $g$ tends to $0$ and both zeros tend to the double zero $\ell/\sqrt{3}$ (at $r_{b} = r_{c} = r_{N}$ the relations above give $\ell^{2} = 3r_{N}^{2}$ and $M = r_{N}/3 = M_{N}$, with $f(r_{N}) = f'(r_{N}) = 0$). So $A_{b}$ and $A_{c}$ have the common limit $4\pi\ell^{2}/3$, and $\lim S_{b} = \lim S_{c}$ if and only if $c_{b} = c_{c}$.

\emph{(iv).} As $M \to 0$ on the cosmological branch, $\ell^{2} = r_{b}^{2} + r_{b}r_{c} + r_{c}^{2}$ with $r_{b} \to 0$ gives $r_{c} \to \ell$, so $S_{c} \to \pi\ell^{2} + c_{c}$, which is $\pi\ell^{2}$ under (Z) and (N). In Planck units $\ell^{2} = 1/H^{2} = M_{P}^{2}/Q(I_{\Lambda}) = N^{2}$ by Fact \claimref{standard-model.imported-frozen-point-dictionary}, with $Q(I_{\Lambda}) = \Lambda/3$ checked on the frozen point $I_{\Lambda} = \ninf + (\Lambda/6)\nO$ by the script, in the normalisation $\nO\cdot\nInf = +1$ that the script uses ($\nO = \tfrac12(e_{+} + e_{-})$, $\nInf = e_{+} - e_{-}$); in T01's normalisation $\nO\cdot\nInf = -1$ the same vector has $Q(I_{\Lambda}) = -\Lambda/3$.

\emph{(v).} A common constant $c$ leaves (T) and (Cl) untouched by (i) and gives equal limits at the merger, so (N) holds; (Z) fails since $S_{b} \to c \neq 0$. As $M \to 0$, $S_{b} \to c$, so $c < 0$ makes $S_{b}$ negative for all small $M$; each boundary mode's thermal entropy is $s \ge 0$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boundary-mode-thermal-entropy}: $s$ is even and decreasing in $|x|$ with limit $0$), so any sum of such entropies is nonnegative and nonnegativity alone excludes $c < 0$, while (Z) fixes $c = 0$ exactly. For orientation (the bound is computed in the result filed alongside, synthesis.euler-term-horizon-entropy-shift): since $r_{b} < \ell/\sqrt{3}$ on the family, a constant $c = -\pi\ell^{2}$ would give $S_{b} < -\tfrac23\pi\ell^{2}$ for every black hole of the family, the inequality the script checks. That the Gauss-Bonnet term of the action of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector} contributes a constant of this kind rests on the Wald (Jacobson-Myers) entropy of an Euler term, which is proportional to the Euler characteristic of the horizon cross-section and so the same for every spherical horizon of the family (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-wald-noether-charge-entropy}(c), read as horizon entropy).

The script checks exactly, on five rational horizon pairs: both radii are zeros of $f$, the factorisation of $\ell^{2} r f(r)$, the bracketing by the Nariai radius, the mass function and its derivative as rational functions of $r$, the two Clausius identities, the inequalities $r_{b}^{2} < \ell^{2}/3 < r_{c}^{2} < \ell^{2}$ and the orientation bound of (v); the double zero at the Nariai merger; the $M = 0$ and $\Lambda = 0$ limits, the former against the frozen point's norm in the conformal model.

synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-a.formal:
Work as in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.light-ray-good-part-of-a-spinor-is-two-chirality-arrays}: the spacetime algebra $\Cl(1,3)$, a horizon's null plane $N_{k}$ with generators along $k = \gamma_{0} + \gamma_{3}$ and second null direction $m = \gamma_{0} - \gamma_{3}$, $B = \gamma_{3}\gamma_{0}$, $\Lambda(k) = \tfrac12(1 + B)$, $\Lambda(m) = \tfrac12(1 - B)$, so that the canonical part of a spinor on $N_{k}$ is $\Lambda(m)\psi$, one complex channel per chirality. Let $V = \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$ be the fermionic slot module (numbers and the module's complex structure are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, the module read on the tower's floors, where $I_{4}$ commutes with the tower vectors) (modes $1, 2$ the slots, $3, 4, 5$ the pairs) with the gauge algebra $\mathfrak{s}(\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3))$ and $Y = (3n - 2k)/6$ on states with $n$ slots and $k$ pairs (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}), and call a CPT halving any involution $\Gamma$ commuting with the gauge algebra whose $-1$ eigenspace $V_{-}$ is isomorphic to the conjugate of its $+1$ eigenspace $V_{+}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.spin10-clause-content-is-the-neutral-singlet-choice}). Read one generation as the left-handed Weyl fields valued in $V_{+}$, its antiparticles in $V_{-}$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Mass terms reach only the constraint.)} With $\ip{k}{m} = 2$, every vector splits as $a = \tfrac12 m\,\ip{k}{a} + \tfrac12 k\,\ip{m}{a} + a_{\perp}$, so $k\nabla = \tfrac12 km\,(k\cdot\nabla) + k\nabla_{\perp}$ contains no derivative off $N_{k}$; $km = 4\Lambda(k)$, $k$ anticommutes with $\gamma_{1}, \gamma_{2}$, and $k\Lambda(k) = 0$, so $k\psi X = k\Lambda(m)\psi X$ for every multivector $X$ acting from the right, and $L_{k}$ is injective on the image of $\Lambda(m)$. Every Lorentz-covariant mass term, of Dirac or of Majorana type, acts from the right, so on $N_{k}$ it enters only the equation that fixes $\Lambda(k)\psi$ from $\Lambda(m)\psi$: the free data on $N_{k}$ are $\Lambda(m)\psi$, with one boundary value of $\Lambda(k)\psi$ per generator, for every mass matrix (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.canonical-part-of-a-spinor-on-a-null-plane}(iv)), one complex channel per Weyl component. In the count of the light-ray result, $2n_{D} + n_{W}$ is the number of Weyl components, and whether they are grouped as Dirac or Majorana species is a property of the mass matrix that the count does not see.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Sixteen per generation.)} The gauge-commuting CPT halvings are the $2^{5}$ choices of one member from each of the five conjugate pairs of non-neutral isotypic components of $V$, times a line in the two-dimensional neutral block; for each of them $\dim_{\C}V_{+} = 16$ and the weights of $V_{-}$ are the negatives of those of $V_{+}$. So a generation supplies $16$ arrays per light ray, $8\ln 2$ at the Hawking temperature with one (Q) version 3 array per channel (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.half-integer-weight-array-carries-half-ln2}(i)), that is $8$ registered units of two arrays, an integer, for every choice of the neutral singlet; $N_{g}$ generations give $16N_{g}$ arrays and $8N_{g}$ units. A generation without the neutral singlet, fifteen components, is not a CPT halving of $V$; it would give $\tfrac{15}{2}$ units.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The particle half is chiral.)} In every such halving no nonzero weight of $V_{+}$ under the Cartan algebra of $\mathfrak{s}(\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3))$ has its negative in $V_{+}$, and the zero weight occurs once (the neutral singlet). A Hestenes spinor field valued in a representation $R$ carries $R$ on both chiralities, so its left-handed content is $R \oplus \bar{R}$; hence no gauge-covariant Dirac field can be formed from a generation except from neutral singlets, and among $N_{g}$ generations at most $\lfloor N_{g}/2 \rfloor$ such pairs. At the anomaly-free halving $\pm(-1)^{n + k}$ the hypercharges of $V_{+}$ are $0$ (once), $-\tfrac23$ (three times), $\tfrac16$ (six), $-\tfrac12$ (two), $1$ (once), $\tfrac13$ (three), and no nonzero value occurs with its negative.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(After electroweak breaking.)} Labelled by electric charge $T_{3} + Y$ and colour, the half $V_{+}$ of the halving $(-1)^{n + k}$ pairs into exactly $7$ charged Dirac species (up and down quarks in three colours, the electron) and $2$ neutral components. With a nonzero Majorana term, the $\nu^{c}\nu^{c}$ entry of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.majorana-element}(1), the neutral components are two Majorana species, $n_{D} = 7$ and $n_{W} = 2$; with none, and a Dirac entry pairing the neutral singlet with the doublet's neutral member, they form one Dirac species, $n_{D} = 8$; both give $16$ arrays. This clause is stated for the halvings $\pm(-1)^{n + k}$ only: whether such a Dirac entry exists in the halving with the other neutral line is not decided here, and if it does not, $n_{D} = 7$, $n_{W} = 2$ there too, again $16$ arrays.
\end{enumerate}
Hence for the series' matter the clause that each counted species is a Dirac species with both chiralities fails on the gauge-covariant reading in every halving, and under a nonzero Majorana term also on the mass reading; what is derived is the count: the CAR content of a light ray is the number of Weyl components, sixteen per generation, eight registered units. Integer-weight fields lie outside this count. The count is per four-dimensional field; a five-dimensional field contributes one array set per Kaluza-Klein level, equivalently per resolution cell of the fifth direction. This is consistent with the common count of the dark-matter premise P1 (one frozen point, one count for every tower) when that count fixes the number of light rays, the arrays per light ray being tower-dependent; if instead every tower had the same number of boundary modes, a five-dimensional tower's cells per Planck area would have to be smaller by its level count. The count of Kaluza-Klein levels as emission channels of the exterior is a different count and is not constrained by this. The projector $\Lambda(m)$ is the idempotent $f = \tfrac12(1 + e_{t}e_{a})$, $e_{t} = \gamma_{0}$, $e_{a} = \gamma_{3}$, of the residue-$0$ signature $(1,1)$ in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.lowest-causal-residues-zero-four-content}(ii): the canonical part is one chiral ideal of the even algebra of the plane of $k$ and $m$, and a mass couples it to the complementary ideal, as there.
synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-a.technical: The registered residue needs a counted unit of two s-wave arrays, and the stored light-ray result reads two arrays as one massless Dirac species. The open problem asks for a derivation that the horizon's counted species are Dirac species. This result takes the field content from the Standard Model subject, the slot module, and counts. Two points come out. The null-plane count does not see the Dirac or Weyl character of a species: the canonical part is fixed by the flux of the current, an algebraic identity, and mass terms, which in the spacetime algebra act from the right, reach only the equation that fixes the other component along the plane. So the arrays are the Weyl components, whatever the masses. And every CPT halving of the slot module has sixteen states in its particle half, so a generation gives sixteen arrays, eight units of $\ln 2$: an integer number of registered units, whichever line of the neutral block is chosen; the Standard Model without a right-handed neutrino, fifteen components, is not a halving. The particle half is chiral in every halving: apart from the neutral singlet no representation occurs with its conjugate, so the content cannot be grouped into gauge-covariant Dirac fields, and after electroweak breaking with the Majorana term it is seven Dirac species and two Majorana neutrals. The problem's Dirac clause therefore fails for the series' own matter; the count it was meant to secure holds without it. The area law still fixes only the product of arrays per light ray and cells per Planck area, so the residue is not derived here.
synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-a.lay: The series counts quantum ladders on a black hole's horizon, and a counted unit has to be two ladders. An earlier result showed that one electron-like particle, which comes in two handednesses, supplies exactly two ladders, and the open question was whether every counted particle is of that kind. This result counts the particles the series itself predicts, one generation of sixteen handed components from its slot construction. Each component supplies one ladder whatever its mass, so a generation gives sixteen ladders, eight units, a whole number. But the series' matter is handed: almost no component has a mirror partner with the same charges, so the particles cannot be grouped into two-handed ones in a way the forces respect, and with the series' neutrino mass the neutrinos are one-handed. The count works; the reason offered for it does not.

The flux of the current through $N_{k}$, which defines the canonical part, is $2|\Lambda(m)\psi|^{2}$ by an algebraic identity in $\psi$ that involves no field equation (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.canonical-part-of-a-spinor-on-a-null-plane}(ii); Theorem \claimref{synthesis.light-ray-good-part-of-a-spinor-is-two-chirality-arrays}(i)). So the free data on $N_{k}$ are $\Lambda(m)\psi$, with the same anticommutator, for every mass matrix: one complex canonical channel per Weyl component of the field content (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.light-ray-good-part-of-a-spinor-is-two-chirality-arrays}(iii), (v)). (Two units appear in this step: the spinor values carry Hestenes' unit, right multiplication by $I_{4}\sigma_{3}$, as in the massive equation above, and the numbers of the slot module and of its internal index are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$. They act on different factors and are not identified here; a count of complex channels is half the real dimension of the data, so it is the same for either unit.) (The mass independence of the null-plane data is the familiar property of light-front quantisation, Kogut and Soper 1970, cited from memory as orientation; the argument above does not use it.) The script of this result still checks $k^{2} = 0$, $km = 2 + 2B$, the splitting of each $\gamma_{\mu}$, the anticommutation of $k$ with $\gamma_{1}, \gamma_{2}$, $\mathrm{rank}(L_{k}\Lambda(k)) = 0$, $\mathrm{rank}(L_{k}\Lambda(m)) = 4$, and $\mathrm{rank}(L_{k}R_{X}\Lambda(k)) = 0$ for each of the sixteen basis blades $X$. A Dirac field has two Weyl components and a Majorana field one, so $2n_{D} + n_{W}$ of the light-ray result is the number of Weyl components; how they group into species is decided by the mass matrix and is invisible to the count.

\emph{The link to residue $0$.} $f = 	frac12(1 + \gamma_{0}\gamma_{3}) = 	frac12(1 - \gamma_{3}\gamma_{0}) = \Lambda(m)$; $(\gamma_{0}\gamma_{3})^{2} = 1$, so the even algebra of the plane of $k$ and $m$ is $\mathrm{span}\{1, \gamma_{0}\gamma_{3}\} \cong \R \oplus \R$ with the two primitive idempotents $f$ and $1 - f = \Lambda(k)$, $f(1 - f) = 0$, $mf = 0 
eq kf$. This is the single chiral ideal of the residue-$0$ signature $(1,1)$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.lowest-causal-residues-zero-four-content}(ii) with $e_{t} = \gamma_{0}$, $e_{a} = \gamma_{3}$; there, mass needs one constituent from each ideal, as here the mass couples $\Lambda(m)\psi$ to $\Lambda(k)\psi$.

\emph{(ii).} Build $V = \Lambda^{ ullet}\C^{5}$ from the empty state by the creation operators of the five modes (the exterior model of the library), with number operators $n_{i} = a^{\dagger}_{i}a_{i}$; on the basis state with occupation $(o_{1}, \dots, o_{5})$ the slot number is $n = o_{1} + o_{2}$, the pair number $k = o_{3} + o_{4} + o_{5}$, $Y = (3n - 2k)/6$, $T_{3} = (o_{1} - o_{2})/2$, and the colour weights are $o_{2 + i} - k/3$, $i = 1, 2, 3$. The gauge algebra preserves $(n, k)$, and the isotypic components are the twelve spaces $F_{n} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$, of which the two neutral ones, $(n, k) = (0, 0)$ and $(2, 3)$, are both $(1,1)_{0}$, and the other ten form five conjugate pairs: $(0,1)$ with $(2,2)$, $(0,2)$ with $(2,1)$, $(0,3)$ with $(2,0)$, $(1,0)$ with $(1,3)$, $(1,1)$ with $(1,2)$ (the script finds the pairing by comparing weight multisets). By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.spin10-clause-content-is-the-neutral-singlet-choice}(i) a gauge-commuting CPT halving takes one member of each conjugate pair into $V_{+}$ and the other into $V_{-}$, and splits the neutral block into two lines. Each pair contributes the same dimension to both halves, and the neutral block one dimension to each, so $\dim V_{+} = \dim V_{-} = 16$ for all $2^{5}$ sign patterns and every line; the script enumerates the $32$ patterns with each of the two coordinate lines (other lines in the neutral block have the same weights) and finds $\dim V_{\pm} = 16$ and the weights of $V_{-}$ equal to the negatives of those of $V_{+}$ in all $64$ cases. By (i) a generation, the left-handed Weyl fields valued in $V_{+}$, has $16$ complex canonical channels per light ray, whatever the mass matrix; the antiparticles in $V_{-}$ are the holes of the same arrays (the conjugate entry of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.light-ray-good-part-of-a-spinor-is-two-chirality-arrays}(iv)), not further arrays. With one (Q) version 3 array per channel and $	frac12\ln 2$ per array (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.half-integer-weight-array-carries-half-ln2}(i)) a generation carries $8\ln 2$, eight registered units of two arrays, and $N_{g}$ generations $8N_{g}$. Removing the neutral singlet leaves fifteen components, an odd number, so not the half of a $32$-dimensional module, and $	frac{15}{2}$ units.

\emph{(iii).} In a halving each non-neutral isotypic component of $V$ occurs once, and its conjugate is the other member of its pair, which the halving puts in $V_{-}$; distinct pairs carry disjoint weight multisets. So for a nonzero weight $w$ of $V_{+}$ the weight $-w$ lies only in $V_{-}$, and the zero weight of $V_{+}$ is the neutral line, once. The script confirms this for all $64$ cases, and as a contrast that $V$ itself is vector-like (every weight occurs with its negative), so the test can fail. A Hestenes spinor field valued in a representation $R$ has left-handed part in $R$ and right-handed part in $R$, the latter being a left-handed field in $ ar{R}$; a gauge-covariant Dirac field in the content therefore needs $R \oplus  ar{R}$ inside $V_{+}$, which by the above happens only for $R$ the neutral singlet, and a single neutral singlet pairs only with itself (a Majorana field). Among $N_{g}$ generations the $N_{g}$ neutral singlets give at most $\lfloor N_{g}/2 floor$ such pairs; the script finds no nonzero weight paired with its negative in $N_{g}$ copies, $N_{g} = 1, \dots, 4$. At the anomaly-free halving, $(-1)^{n + k}$ with the particle half containing $(2,3)_{1/6}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}(2)), the hypercharge histogram of $V_{+}$ is $\{0: 1, -	frac23: 3, 	frac16: 6, -	frac12: 2, 1: 1, 	frac13: 3\}$, with sum $0$ and no nonzero value with its negative.

\emph{(iv).} After electroweak breaking the unbroken algebra is colour and the electric charge $T_{3} + Y$. Take the halving $(-1)^{n + k}$ (the clause is stated for $\pm(-1)^{n + k}$ only). Labelling the states of its $V_{+}$ by (charge, colour weights), a Dirac species needs a label and its negative. The labels with nonzero charge pair exactly: charge $	frac23$ in colour $c$ with charge $-	frac23$ in $ ar{c}$ (three pairs), $-	frac13$ with $	frac13$ (three), $-1$ with $1$ (one), seven charged Dirac species; the two remaining labels are neutral and colourless (the $
u$ of the doublet and $
u^{c}$). With a nonzero $
u^{c}
u^{c}$ entry (Theorem \claimref{standard-model.majorana-element}(1)) the neutral mass matrix is a symmetric $2 	imes 2$ matrix $ egin{pmatrix} 0 & d \ d & M \end{pmatrix}$ with $M 
eq 0$; its two singular values differ (they coincide only at $M = 0$), so its Takagi eigenvectors are two Majorana fields of different masses, which no unitary mixing combines into one Dirac field, so $n_{D} = 7$, $n_{W} = 2$, $2n_{D} + n_{W} = 16$; with no Majorana entry and a Dirac entry coupling $
u^{c}$ to the doublet's neutral member, the two neutrals form one Dirac species, $n_{D} = 8$, $n_{W} = 0$, again $16$. In the halving with the other neutral line the existence of such a Dirac entry depends on the bilinears available to the full state and is not decided here; if there is none, the two neutrals are Majorana or massless Weyl fields, $n_{D} = 7$, $n_{W} = 2$, and the count is $16$ again. The count is per four-dimensional field. A five-dimensional field is, level by level, a tower of four-dimensional fields of masses set by its Kaluza-Klein levels, and by (i) each level's Weyl components give one array each on a light ray whatever its mass: one array set per Kaluza-Klein level, equivalently per resolution cell of the fifth direction. The area law fixes only the product of arrays per light ray and cells per Planck area, so this agrees with the common count of the dark-matter premise P1 (one frozen point, one count for every tower) when that count fixes the number of light rays, with tower-dependent arrays per light ray; were every tower to carry the same number of boundary modes instead, the five-dimensional tower's cell density would have to be smaller by its level count. Kaluza-Klein levels counted as emission channels of the exterior are a different count, not constrained here. Without $
u^{c}$ the charged pairing is unchanged and one neutral component is left, $2 \cdot 7 + 1 = 15$. The script computes these pairings from the weights.

\emph{Conclusion.} The count of arrays per light ray is the number of Weyl components (i), sixteen per generation for every halving (ii); the grouping into Dirac species is neither gauge covariant (iii) nor, under a nonzero Majorana term, complete (iv). Nothing here uses the area law; the residue's calibration, which fixes the product of arrays per light ray and cells per Planck area, is untouched. The result is transport-absent.
